# 1. Setup

## 1.1 Packages

```{r setup-packages, message=FALSE}
required_packages <- c("data.table", "dplyr", "lubridate", "ggplot2",
                       "ACDm", "forecast", "FinTS", "scales", "archive", "tseries")

missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !sapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE)
]
if (length(missing_packages) > 0) install.packages(missing_packages)

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  invisible(lapply(required_packages, library, character.only = TRUE))
})

# Package notes:
#   data.table - primary manipulation layer. Chosen for memory efficiency:
#   ACDm       - acdFit() / sim_ACD() for the ACD specifications.
#   forecast   - ARMA(1,1) rung of the ladder.
#   archive    - handles the compressed Databento .zst files.
#   tseries    - adf.test(), the Augmented Dickey-Fuller unit-root test
#                 applied to diurnally-adjusted durations (Section 8.0).
```

## 1.2 Paths and global constants

```{r setup-constants}
DATA_DIR <- "D:/Dissertation/Data_dir"
NVDA_DIR <- "D:/Dissertation/Datasets/nvidia_stock"
if (!dir.exists(DATA_DIR)) dir.create(DATA_DIR, recursive = TRUE)

# Sample window 
SAMPLE_START <- as.POSIXct("2026-05-01 00:00:00", tz = "UTC")
SAMPLE_END   <- as.POSIXct("2026-05-31 23:59:59", tz = "UTC")

TRAIN_DAYS <- 14L
TEST_DAYS  <- 5L
SPLIT_TIME <- SAMPLE_START + TRAIN_DAYS * 86400              # start of day 15
TEST_END   <- SPLIT_TIME + TEST_DAYS * 86400                 # 5 days of TEST, not the whole remaining sample

# NVDA regular session (UTC minutes since midnight)
SESSION_OPEN  <- 13*60 + 30      # 13:30 UTC
SESSION_CLOSE <- 20*60           # 20:00 UTC

# Diagnostics
LB_LAGS <- 15L    # Engle & Russell (1998) use 15 lags
LB_CRIT <- 25     # chi-squared(15), 5% critical value

# Estimation blocks
ARMA_N <- 100000L    # ARMA(1,1): 2 parameters, 100k is ample
FIT_N  <- Inf        # ACD specifications: the FULL training window, per asset.
                     

# Simulation
SIM_N    <- 100000L
SIM_BURN <- 1000L    
ACF_LAGS <- c(1, 10)

set.seed(5872)       # module code, for reproducibility
```

```{r durations-cache-check}

#  If a cached `durations` (the Section 6 checkpoint) is already on disk,
#  load it and SKIP those sections entirely, every chunk in them is gated
#  on `!DURATIONS_CACHED` below. Delete the cache file to force a rebuild.

DURATIONS_CACHE_FILE <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "durations_final.rds")
DURATIONS_CACHED <- file.exists(DURATIONS_CACHE_FILE)

STANDARDISED_CACHE_FILE <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "standardised_final.rds")
STANDARDISED_CACHED <- file.exists(STANDARDISED_CACHE_FILE)

MODEL_CACHE_FILE <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "model_fits_cache.rds")
MODELS_CACHED <- file.exists(MODEL_CACHE_FILE)

SPLIT_CACHE_FILE <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "split_sets_cache.rds")
SPLIT_CACHED <- file.exists(SPLIT_CACHE_FILE)

if (DURATIONS_CACHED) {
  cached <- readRDS(DURATIONS_CACHE_FILE)
  if (!is.null(cached$durations)) {
    # current cache format: list(durations = ..., pipeline_counts = ...)
    durations       <- cached$durations
    pipeline_counts <- cached$pipeline_counts
  } else {
    # older cache file, predates pipeline_counts: `cached` IS the durations list
    durations       <- cached
    pipeline_counts <- NULL
    cat("(cache predates pipeline_counts -- basic-data-structure removal counts\n")
    cat(" will show NA. Delete the cache and re-knit to pick them up.)\n")
  }
  rm(cached)
  cat(sprintf("Loaded cached durations from %s -- skipping Sections 2-6.\n",
              DURATIONS_CACHE_FILE))
  cat("(delete this file and re-knit to force a full rebuild)\n")
} else if (STANDARDISED_CACHED) {
  cat(sprintf("No durations cache, but found standardised cache %s\n",
              STANDARDISED_CACHE_FILE))
  cat("-- skipping raw load + standardisation; filter/build will still run.\n")
} else {
  cat("No cache found -- Sections 2-6 will run in full (slow).\n")
}
```

## 1.3 Quick-start — skip straight to model fitting

Run ONLY the chunk below in a fresh R session to bypass Sections 2-9
entirely (raw load, filtering, duration build, rollover, diurnal
adjustment, split) and go directly to any model chunk in Section 10+. Self-
contained: needs nothing else run first. Requires `SPLIT_CACHE_FILE` to
already exist (produced automatically at the end of `split`, once, the
first time the document is run in full) - if it doesn't yet, this chunk
says so and does nothing else; run the document normally that one time
first.

```{r quickstart-model-inputs}
if (SPLIT_CACHED) {
  suppressMessages({
    library(data.table); library(ACDm); library(ggplot2); library(splines)
  })

  .qs <- readRDS(SPLIT_CACHE_FILE)
  split_sets      <- .qs$split_sets
  diurnal_fits    <- .qs$diurnal_fits
  diurnal_winners <- .qs$diurnal_winners
  rm(.qs)

  #  exact copies of the helpers every model chunk depends on
  get_fit_series <- function(nm, n = FIT_N) {
    x <- head(split_sets[[nm]]$train$adjDur, n)
    x[is.finite(x) & x > 0]
  }

  fit_ready <- function(varname, assets = names(split_sets)) {
    exists(varname, inherits = FALSE) &&
      length(get(varname, inherits = FALSE)) > 0 &&
      all(assets %in% names(get(varname, inherits = FALSE)))
  }

  save_model_progress <- function(...) {
    new_objs <- list(...)
    existing <- if (file.exists(MODEL_CACHE_FILE)) {
      tryCatch(readRDS(MODEL_CACHE_FILE), error = function(e)
        stop(sprintf(
          "save_model_progress: %s exists but cannot be read (%s). Refusing to\n",
          MODEL_CACHE_FILE, conditionMessage(e)),
          "overwrite it with only the object(s) from this call.", call. = FALSE))
    } else list()
    existing[names(new_objs)] <- new_objs
    tmp <- paste0(MODEL_CACHE_FILE, ".tmp", Sys.getpid())
    saveRDS(existing, tmp)
    ok <- file.rename(tmp, MODEL_CACHE_FILE)
    if (!ok) { file.remove(tmp); stop("save_model_progress: atomic rename failed -- see ", tmp) }
    cat(sprintf("  [saved %s -> %s]\n", paste(names(new_objs), collapse = ", "), MODEL_CACHE_FILE))
  }

  gof <- function(f, what) f$goodnessOfFit[what, "value"]

  cat(sprintf("Loaded %s -- split_sets/diurnal_fits/diurnal_winners restored.\n", SPLIT_CACHE_FILE))
  cat("get_fit_series() / fit_ready() / save_model_progress() / gof() defined.\n")
  if (MODELS_CACHED) cat(sprintf("Model cache also found (%s) -- already-fitted models will load, not refit.\n", MODEL_CACHE_FILE))
  cat("\nReady. Jump to any Section 10+ chunk directly (e.g. eacd-fit).\n")
} else {
  cat("SPLIT_CACHE_FILE not found yet (", SPLIT_CACHE_FILE, ").\n")
  cat("Run the document normally, top to bottom, once -- `split` (Section 9)\n")
  cat("will create it automatically. After that, this chunk alone is enough\n")
  cat("in every future fresh session.\n")
}
```

# 2. Data loaders

Each loader returns the data in its **native schema**. 

## 2.1 GBP/USD — Dukascopy

```{r loader-fx}

if (!DURATIONS_CACHED) {
load_forex <- function(instrument = "gbpusd",
                       from_date  = format(SAMPLE_START, "%Y-%m-%d"),
                       to_date    = format(SAMPLE_END, "%Y-%m-%d"),
                       out_dir    = DATA_DIR) {
  
  # Gives the name string to identify file name
  csv_pattern <- sprintf("^%s.*%s.*%s.*\\.csv$", instrument, from_date, to_date)

  # Lists files and filter out any files  with 0bytes(empty)
  valid_csvs <- function() {
    f <- list.files(out_dir, pattern = csv_pattern, full.names = TRUE)
    f[file.size(f) > 0]
  }

  csvs <- valid_csvs()
  
  # Uses existing file and skips re-downloading
  if (length(csvs) > 0) {
    message("Using existing CSV file.")
  } else {
    
    #Downloads file if not found
    cmd <- sprintf(
      'npx dukascopy-node -i %s -from %s -to %s -t tick -f csv -dir "%s"',
      instrument, from_date, to_date, out_dir
    )
    message("Downloading forex data...")
    status <- system(cmd)

    csvs <- valid_csvs()
    if (length(csvs) == 0) {
      stop("Download failed: no non-empty CSV created (exit status ", status,
           "). Check network access and date availability.")
    }
  }

  fread(csvs[which.max(file.mtime(csvs))])
}
}
```

## 2.2 BTCUSDT — Binance aggTrades

```{r loader-btc}
if (!DURATIONS_CACHED) {

load_bitcoin <- function(symbol = "BTCUSDT", dates, out_dir = DATA_DIR) {

  # Base url of binanace's historical trade - endpoint serves one zip file per symbol per day.
  base  <- "https://data.binance.vision/data/spot/daily/aggTrades"
  parts <- vector("list", length(dates))

  # Loops over every day
  for (i in seq_along(dates)) {
    d       <- dates[i]
    fname   <- sprintf("%s-aggTrades-%s.zip", symbol, d) # file naming convention
    url     <- sprintf("%s/%s/%s", base, symbol, fname) # full download url
    zippath <- file.path(out_dir, fname) # zip file saved location

    csv_name <- sub("\\.zip$", ".csv", fname) # csv name
    csv_path <- file.path(out_dir, csv_name) # file path to csv

    # Downloads only when the zip and the csv does not exists.
    if (!file.exists(csv_path) && !file.exists(zippath)) {
      message("Downloading ", url)
      download.file(url, zippath, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
    }

    if (!file.exists(csv_path)) {
      inner    <- unzip(zippath, list = TRUE)$Name[1]
      unzip(zippath, files = inner, exdir = out_dir, overwrite = TRUE)
      csv_path <- file.path(out_dir, inner)
    } else {
      message("Using cached csv: ", csv_path) # csv already existing
    }

    # aggTrades dump has NO header row. Column names assigned.
    parts[[i]] <- fread(csv_path, header = FALSE,
                        col.names = c("aggId", "price", "qty",
                                      "firstId", "lastId", "ts",
                                      "isBuyerMaker", "isBestMatch"))
  }

  rbindlist(parts)
}
}

```

## 2.3 NVDA — Databento market-by-order

```{r loader-nvda}
if (!DURATIONS_CACHED) {
# Nanosecond timestamps CANNOT go through POSIXct. A double carries ~15-17
# significant digits; a May-2026 nanosecond epoch value needs 19. Trades tens of
# nanoseconds apart would round to a common value, manufacturing simultaneity
# that consolidation would then treat as one event.
#
# The timestamp is therefore parsed as a STRING and split into two integers:
#   sec     - whole seconds since epoch  
#   frac_ns - nanosecond remainder       
  
load_stock_nvda <- function(path = NVDA_DIR) {

  files <- list.files(path, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
  if (length(files) == 0) stop("No CSV files found in ", path)

  read_one <- function(f) {
    d <- fread(f, colClasses = list(character = "ts_event"))

    s     <- sub("Z$", "", d$ts_event)          # strip trailing Z
    whole <- sub("\\.\\d+$", "", s)             # "2026-05-01T08:00:07"
    frac  <- sub("^[^.]+\\.?", "", s)           # "475335610"
    frac  <- ifelse(frac == "", "0", frac)

    frac_ns <- as.integer(formatC(
      as.numeric(substr(frac, 1, 9)) * 10^(9 - nchar(substr(frac, 1, 9))),
      format = "d"))

    sec <- as.numeric(as.POSIXct(whole, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC"))

    data.table(
      time     = as.POSIXct(sec, origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC"),
      sec      = sec,
      frac_ns  = frac_ns,
      price    = d[["price"]],
      size     = d[["size"]],
      action   = d[["action"]],    # "T" = trade; other codes are book events
      flags    = d[["flags"]],     # F_LAST (128) marks a matching-event boundary
      sequence = d[["sequence"]]   # exchange event counter
    )
  }

  dt <- rbindlist(lapply(files, read_one))
  setorder(dt, sec, frac_ns)
  dt[]
}
}
```

# 3. Standardisation — three schemas, one schema

```{r standardise-helpers}
if (!DURATIONS_CACHED) {

#  Three providers, three schemas, three timestamp units, mapped onto ONE
#  representation:
#
#      time | sec | frac_ns | price | size

  
assert_epoch_unit <- function(ts, divisor, label,
                              lo = SAMPLE_START, hi = SAMPLE_END) {
  if (!length(ts) || all(is.na(ts)))
    stop(label, ": no usable timestamps to check.")

  probe <- as.POSIXct(min(ts, na.rm = TRUE) / divisor,
                      origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC")

  if (probe < lo - 86400 || probe > hi + 86400) {
    stop(label, ": timestamp unit is WRONG.\n",
         "  min(ts)/", format(divisor, scientific = FALSE), " -> ", format(probe),
         "\n  Expected a date inside ", format(lo), " .. ", format(hi))
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# Split into sec and fractional ns

split_epoch <- function(ts, per_sec, ns_per) {
  ts  <- as.numeric(ts)
  sec <- floor(ts / per_sec)
  list(sec     = sec,
       frac_ns = as.integer(round((ts - sec * per_sec) * ns_per)))
}
}
```



```{r standardise-fx}
if (!DURATIONS_CACHED) {
# GBP/USD: Dukascopy, MILLISECONDS, quote feed
  
# PRICE = the mid. Bid and ask are two sides of one quote; the mid is the single
# summary price, and unlike either side individually it is not subject to the
# bid-ask bounce that would induce spurious price variation.
  
# SIZE = NA. Nothing was traded, so there is no traded size to record.
  
standardise_fx <- function(raw) {
  d <- copy(raw); setDT(d)

  stopifnot(all(c("timestamp", "askPrice", "bidPrice") %in% names(d)))
  assert_epoch_unit(d$timestamp, 1e3, "GBP/USD")

  sp  <- split_epoch(d$timestamp, per_sec = 1e3, ns_per = 1e6)
  out <- data.table(
    time    = as.POSIXct(sp$sec, origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC"),
    sec     = sp$sec,
    frac_ns = sp$frac_ns,
    price   = (d$askPrice + d$bidPrice) / 2,
    size    = NA_real_,
    ask     = d$askPrice,   
    bid     = d$bidPrice    
  )
  setorder(out, sec, frac_ns)
  out[]
}
}
```

```{r standardise-btc}
if (!DURATIONS_CACHED) {
  
# BTCUSDT: Binance aggTrades, MICROSECONDS
standardise_btc <- function(raw) {
  d <- copy(raw); setDT(d)

  stopifnot(all(c("ts", "price", "qty") %in% names(d)))
  assert_epoch_unit(d$ts, 1e6, "BTCUSDT")

  sp  <- split_epoch(d$ts, per_sec = 1e6, ns_per = 1e3)
  out <- data.table(
    time    = as.POSIXct(sp$sec, origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC"),
    sec     = sp$sec,
    frac_ns = sp$frac_ns,
    price   = as.numeric(d$price),
    size    = as.numeric(d$qty)
  )
  setorder(out, sec, frac_ns)
  out[]
}
}
```

```{r standardise-nvda}
if (!DURATIONS_CACHED) {
# NVDA: Databento, already (sec, frac_ns)

standardise_nvda <- function(raw) {
  d <- copy(raw); setDT(d)

  if ("action" %in% names(d)) {
    n0 <- nrow(d)
    d  <- d[action == "T"] # TRADES ONLY: action == "T". 

    message(sprintf("standardise_nvda: %s -> %s rows after action=='T' filter",
                    format(n0, big.mark = ","), format(nrow(d), big.mark = ",")))
  }

  keep <- intersect(c("time", "sec", "frac_ns", "price", "size",
                      "flags", "sequence"), names(d))
  out  <- d[, ..keep]
  out[, `:=`(price = as.numeric(price), size = as.numeric(size))]

  setorder(out, sec, frac_ns)
  out[]
}
}
```



# 4. Event filtering — applied to RAW EVENTS

 **filter before differencing**. Removing an observation
after differencing leaves the durations either side of it unchanged, so the
record no longer describes a consistent sequence of arrivals. Removing it
beforehand causes the surrounding interval to be computed correctly as the gap
between the events that remain.

## 4.1 FX - retain price revisions only

```{r filter-fx}
if (!DURATIONS_CACHED) {

#  GBP/USD is a QUOTE feed. An event is a revision to the best bid or best ask.
#
#  NOT the same as consolidation. Two orthogonal problems:
#
#                   | non-event       | timestamp collision
#    ---------------|-----------------|--------------------------
#    timestamps     | DIFFER          | IDENTICAL
#    prices         | SAME            | DIFFER
#    duration       | small, non-zero | exactly zero
#    fix            | FILTER (delete) | CONSOLIDATE (merge)
#    grounds        | definitional    | one arrival, several fills

  filter_fx_events <- function(d) {
  n0 <- nrow(d)

  stopifnot(!anyNA(d$ask), !anyNA(d$bid)) # Checks for missing values and stops execution

  d[, .keep := (ask != shift(ask)) | (bid != shift(bid))]   # shift() is the lag
  # If both do not change, remove, else keep
  d[1, .keep := TRUE] # Row 1 - no previous event
  d <- d[.keep == TRUE] # Removing other rows
  d[, .keep := NULL] # Deleting temporary column

  message(sprintf("filter_fx_events: %s -> %s rows (%s removed, %.2f%%)",
                  format(n0, big.mark = ","), format(nrow(d), big.mark = ","),
                  format(n0 - nrow(d), big.mark = ","),
                  100 * (n0 - nrow(d)) / n0)) # Percentage removed ~ 0.23%
  
  d[] # returns filtered dataset
}
}
```

## 4.2 FX - exclude the Sunday reopening

```{r filter-fx-weekend}
if (!DURATIONS_CACHED) {
#  Sunday reopening - the 48h weekend closure boundary.
#
#  A reopening after a low-liquidity boundary is not a continuation of
#  continuous trading (Engle & Russell 1998, who exclude the equity session
#  open; Chen, Chung & Russell, who discard overnight durations for CME FX
#  futures).


  filter_fx_weekend <- function(d) {
  n0 <- nrow(d) # Number of obs before filtering
  d  <- d[wday(time) != 1]   # wday()==1 is Sunday, locale-independent (weekdays() is not)
  message(sprintf("filter_fx_weekend: %s -> %s rows (%s removed, %.2f%%)",
                  format(n0, big.mark = ","), format(nrow(d), big.mark = ","),
                  format(n0 - nrow(d), big.mark = ","),
                  100 * (n0 - nrow(d)) / n0))
  d[]
}
}
```

## 4.3 NVDA — regular trading session only

```{r filter-nvda}
if (!DURATIONS_CACHED) {
#  Restrict NVDA to the REGULAR US session, 13:30-20:00 UTC.
#
#  FILTER THE RAW TRADES, NOT THE DURATIONS. If durations were filtered
#  instead, each day's first in-session trade would sit ~17.5h after the
#  previous day's last, manufacturing a fake overnight duration at EVERY
#  session boundary.

  filter_nvda_session <- function(d) {
  n0 <- nrow(d)
  d  <- copy(d)

  d[, tod_min := hour(time) * 60 + minute(time)] # Converts time to minutes after midnight
  d <- d[tod_min >= SESSION_OPEN & tod_min < SESSION_CLOSE] # Minutes within session timing
  d[, tod_min := NULL]

  message(sprintf("filter_nvda_session: %s -> %s events (%.1f%% retained)",
                  format(n0, big.mark = ","), format(nrow(d), big.mark = ","),
                  100 * nrow(d) / n0))
  message(sprintf("  time-of-day range now: %s .. %s UTC",
                  format(min(d$time), "%H:%M:%S"),
                  format(max(d$time), "%H:%M:%S")))
  d[]
}
}
```

## 4.5 Filter 

```{r filter-apply}
if (!DURATIONS_CACHED) {
# post-standardise copies (fx0/btc0/nvda0) 
  
n0_fx  <- nrow(fx0)
fx     <- filter_fx_events(copy(fx0))   # quote feed: non-events removed
n1_fx  <- nrow(fx)
fx     <- filter_fx_weekend(fx)         # Sunday reopening sliver removed
n2_fx  <- nrow(fx)
btc    <- copy(btc0) # No filtering in Crypto
n0_nvda <- nrow(nvda0)
nvda   <- filter_nvda_session(copy(nvda0))   # session hours filter 
n1_nvda <- nrow(nvda)

# Per-asset filter-stage removal counts, referenced by the basic-data-structure

filter_log <- rbindlist(list(
  data.table(asset = "GBP/USD", nonevent_removed = n0_fx - n1_fx,
             weekend_removed = n1_fx - n2_fx, extended_hours_removed = NA_integer_),
  data.table(asset = "BTCUSDT", nonevent_removed = NA_integer_,
             weekend_removed = NA_integer_, extended_hours_removed = NA_integer_),
  data.table(asset = "NVDA", nonevent_removed = NA_integer_,
             weekend_removed = NA_integer_, extended_hours_removed = n0_nvda - n1_nvda)
))

# One structure, three assets
# Everything downstream iterates over THIS. No asset is special-cased by name
# again after this point.
assets <- list("GBP/USD" = fx, "BTCUSDT" = btc, "NVDA" = nvda)

cat("\n=== EVENT COUNTS AFTER FILTERING ===\n")
for (nm in names(assets)) {
  a <- assets[[nm]]
  cat(sprintf("%-8s : %11s events | %s .. %s\n",
              nm, format(nrow(a), big.mark = ","),
              format(min(a$time)), format(max(a$time))))
}
}
```

# 5. Duration construction

```{r duration-consolidate}

#  CONSOLIDATION —
#
#  Two events sharing a timestamp yield
#  a duration of zero, which the likelihood cannot accommodate. The substantive
#  motivation is that a zero would assert two economically distinct arrivals
#  with no interval between them.
#
#  MERGE INTO 
#    time  -> the shared timestamp
#    size  -> the SUM (450)
#    price -> VWAP:  sum(p_j * q_j) / sum(q_j)  =  102.5078
#
# The two attributions are DISTINCT: the principle that simultaneous
#  transactions constitute one arrival is E&R (1998); the VWAP rule for
#  combining them is Huth & Abergel (2011).
#
#  ASSET-BY-ASSET -- objective held constant, implementation varies:
#    NVDA : REQUIRED               - venue splits one fill across legs
#    BTC  : PARTIAL upstream       - aggTrades merges same-price fills only, so
#                                     a sweep across several price levels still
#                                     emits one record per level
#    FX   : STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT - an OTC quote feed has no matching engine
#                                     and no fills to aggregate. Ties are two
#                                     genuine quote revisions inside one
#                                     millisecond: a CLOCK-RESOLUTION limit,
#                                     not a split fill. Still merged (one
#                                     duration per observable instant).

consolidate <- function(d) {
  n0 <- nrow(d)

  out <- d[, {
    if (all(is.na(size))) {
      # FX: no traded size, so no weights available. Simple mean - exact
      # anyway, since within one instant the mid is a single number unless two
      # providers revised simultaneously.
      list(price = mean(price), size = NA_real_, n_events = .N)
    } 
    # BTC / NVDA
      else {
      list(price    = sum(price * size) / sum(size),   # VWAP
           size     = sum(size),
           n_events = .N)
    }
  }, by = .(sec, frac_ns)]

  out[, time := as.POSIXct(sec, origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC")] # creates POSIX timestamp from seconds
  setcolorder(out, c("time", "sec", "frac_ns", "price", "size", "n_events"))
  setorder(out, sec, frac_ns)

  message(sprintf("  consolidate: %s -> %s instants (%s records merged, %.2f%%)",
                  format(n0, big.mark = ","), format(nrow(out), big.mark = ","),
                  format(n0 - nrow(out), big.mark = ","),
                  100 * (n0 - nrow(out)) / n0))
  attr(out, "n_merged") <- n0 - nrow(out)  # same-timestamp collisions collapsed
                                            # (would otherwise be zero durations)
  out[]
}
```

```{r duration-build}

#  THE central function. 
#
#    (1) CONSOLIDATE - merge events sharing an identical timestamp into ONE
#                       economic event                     [Engle & Russell 1998]
#    (2) SEGMENT     - never let a duration span a session boundary
#    (3) DIFFERENCE  - gaps between consecutive consolidated events
#
#  Order matters in both directions. Consolidating AFTER differencing cannot
#  work: the zero is already baked into the series. 
#  Differencing BEFORE segmenting manufactures overnight gaps at every session boundary.
#
#  PRECISION:  duration = (sec_i - sec_{i-1}) + (frac_ns_i - frac_ns_{i-1})/1e9

#  SEGMENTATION: the first event of each session yields NA - there is no
#  preceding event within that session, so no duration bridges the boundary.

build_durations <- function(d, single_session = FALSE) {

  stopifnot(all(c("sec", "frac_ns", "price") %in% names(d))) # checks if rows are present
  d <- copy(d)
  setorder(d, sec, frac_ns)          # sort on the INTEGER PAIR, never on `time`
                                     # (which is truncated to whole seconds and
                                     # would tie-break arbitrarily)

  d <- consolidate(d)                                                    # (1)
  n_merged <- attr(d, "n_merged")

  d[, session := if (single_session) 1L else as.integer(as.Date(time))]  # (2)

  d[, duration := {                                                      # (3)
    dsec  <- c(NA_real_, diff(sec)) # 1st value is NA
    dfrac <- c(NA_real_, diff(frac_ns))
    dsec + dfrac / 1e9
  }, by = session]

  n_boundary <- sum(is.na(d$duration)) # Every session, one NA - Gives number of session-opening events
  d <- d[!is.na(duration)]           # drop the first event of each session

  # Consolidation should have eliminated EVERY zero. A survivor means two events
  # shared an instant and were not merged, not a market feature.
  if (any(d$duration == 0))
    stop("build_durations: ", sum(d$duration == 0),
         " ZERO durations survived consolidation.")
  if (any(d$duration < 0))
    stop("build_durations: NEGATIVE duration - data are not sorted.")

  message(sprintf("  durations  : %s (dropped %d session-opening events)",
                  format(nrow(d), big.mark = ","), n_boundary))
  attr(d, "n_zero_removed")     <- n_merged   # consolidation merges (Section 5)
  attr(d, "n_boundary_dropped") <- n_boundary # first event of each session
  d[]
}
```

## 5.1 Build all three

```{r duration-run}

if (!DURATIONS_CACHED) {
message("GBP/USD"); dur_fx   <- build_durations(fx)
message("BTCUSDT"); dur_btc  <- build_durations(btc,  single_session = TRUE)
message("NVDA");    dur_nvda <- build_durations(nvda)

durations <- list("GBP/USD" = dur_fx, "BTCUSDT" = dur_btc, "NVDA" = dur_nvda)

# Pipeline removal counts, for the basic-data-structure table (Section 7.1):
# filter_log (raw-event-stage removals, from filter-apply) joined with the
# consolidation/session-boundary counts attached as attributes above.

pipeline_counts <- merge(
  filter_log,
  rbindlist(lapply(names(durations), function(nm) {
    d <- durations[[nm]]
    data.table(asset = nm,
               n_zero_removed     = attr(d, "n_zero_removed"),
               n_boundary_dropped = attr(d, "n_boundary_dropped"))
  })),
  by = "asset")
}
```

## 5.2 Validation — is BTC same-timestamp grouping justified?

```{r check-btc-contiguity}
if (!DURATIONS_CACHED) {

#  Holy (2022) objects that a shared timestamp does not establish that records
#  arose from a single order, so aggregation is not automatically valid. The
#  Binance data permit this to be EXAMINED rather than assumed.
#
#  The exchange assigns sequential identifiers to raw trades and reports, for
#  each aggregated record, the first and last identifier it subsumes. The
#  identifier ranges of records sharing a timestamp can therefore be inspected
#  for gaps.
#
#  Contiguous IDs  => one continuous sweep => VWAP is unambiguously correct.
#  Gaps            => two separate orders in the same microsecond.
#
#  This establishes a NECESSARY condition, not a sufficient one: non-contiguity
#  would falsify the single-arrival interpretation. It is nonetheless stronger
#  than the argument from clock resolution available to E&R (1998), whose data
#  contained no comparable identifier.

  btc_check <- copy(btc_raw)
setDT(btc_check)
setorder(btc_check, ts, aggId)

btc_check[, grp_n := .N, by = ts]
multi <- btc_check[grp_n > 1]

# Contiguity must be checked on the RAW-TRADE id RANGE each aggregate record
# subsumes (firstId/lastId), not on aggId: aggId is Binance's own aggregate-
# record counter, incremented by exactly 1 for every record unconditionally,
# so (aggId - shift(aggId) == 1) is true by construction and cannot falsify
# anything. firstId/lastId are the actual raw-trade identifier range.
multi[, contiguous := (firstId - shift(lastId) == 1), by = ts]

cat(sprintf("Same-microsecond groups with >1 record : %s\n",
            format(uniqueN(multi$ts), big.mark = ",")))
cat(sprintf("Within-group gaps that are contiguous  : %.2f%%\n",
            100 * mean(multi$contiguous, na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("Non-contiguous (separate orders)       : %.2f%%\n",
            100 * mean(!multi$contiguous, na.rm = TRUE)))

btc_contig_tbl <- data.table(
  metric = c("Same-microsecond groups with >1 record",
             "Within-group gaps that are contiguous",
             "Non-contiguous (separate orders)"),
  value  = c(sprintf("%s", format(uniqueN(multi$ts), big.mark = ",")),
             sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * mean(multi$contiguous, na.rm = TRUE)),
             sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * mean(!multi$contiguous, na.rm = TRUE)))
)
print(btc_contig_tbl)

rm(btc_check, multi); invisible(gc())
}

# OUTPUT (stale -- was recorded against the vacuous aggId-based check, which
# could only ever read 100%/0%; not yet re-run against the corrected
# firstId/lastId-based check above. Re-run and replace before citing.)

```


## 5.3 Validation — does NVDA's batch flag agree with timestamp grouping?

```{r check-nvda-flags}
if (!DURATIONS_CACHED) {

  #  For NVDA the justification does not rest on inference. The MBO feed records
#  a flag for every event, and fills arising from a single matching event are
#  marked with F_LAST (bit value 128) on the final record of the batch. The
#  exchange itself therefore delimits which fills constitute one event.
#
#  THE CHECK: does grouping by (sec, frac_ns) reproduce the boundary the venue
#  has already declared? Two failure modes are possible:
#    - one event spanning MULTIPLE timestamps  -> harmless (one order, slow fill)
#    - one timestamp holding MULTIPLE events   -> timestamp-grouping WOULD have
#                                                  merged two distinct arrivals

if ("flags" %in% names(nvda)) {

  chk <- standardise_nvda(nvda_raw)
  # Order by (sec, frac_ns, sequence), not sequence alone: if the exchange's
  # own sequence counter resets per day or per file, sorting on it alone
  # would scramble batch boundaries across those resets. Sorting by actual
  # timestamp first, with sequence only as the within-timestamp tiebreak, is
  # strictly safer and identical to the old order if sequence never resets.
  setorder(chk, sec, frac_ns, sequence)

  # F_LAST marks the LAST row of an event, so the NEXT row starts a new one:
  # cumsum of the flag, shifted DOWN by one.
  
  chk[, is_last  := bitwAnd(as.integer(flags), 128L) > 0L]
  chk[, event_id := shift(cumsum(is_last), n = 1, fill = 0)]

  per_event <- chk[, .(n_ts = uniqueN(paste(sec, frac_ns)), n_rows = .N),
                   by = event_id]
  per_ts    <- chk[, .(n_events = uniqueN(event_id)), by = .(sec, frac_ns)]

  cat(sprintf("Events spanning >1 timestamp : %d  (harmless: one order, slow fill)\n",
              sum(per_event$n_ts > 1)))
  cat(sprintf("Timestamps holding >1 event  : %d  (these WOULD be corrupted by ts-grouping)\n",
              sum(per_ts$n_events > 1)))
  cat(sprintf("Agreement rate               : %.4f%%\n",
              100 * mean(per_ts$n_events == 1)))

  rm(chk, per_event, per_ts); invisible(gc())

} else {
  message("`flags` column not present -- skipping F_LAST verification.")
}
}
```


```{r free-raw-memory}

# Because of memory constraints 

#  FREE THE RAW/PRE-FILTER OBJECTS - this is the LAST chunk that needs any of
#  fx_raw/btc_raw/nvda_raw/btc0/nvda0. check-btc-contiguity (5.2) was the last
#  consumer of btc_raw; check-nvda-flags (5.3, just above) was the last
#  consumer of nvda_raw; btc0/nvda0's only use was building the filtered
#  `btc`/`nvda` in filter-apply (4.x), already done by this point. fx_raw is
#  likewise unused again until Section 13 (marked-pd-build), which re-reads
#  the CSV fresh there rather than depending on this copy surviving that long.
#
#  fx0 is the ONE exception - KEPT, not freed: eda-outlier-fx-isolated
#  (Section 7) uses it for a gap-diagnosis check, already written to degrade
#  gracefully (`if (!exists("fx0"))`) if it isn't available, so freeing it
#  here would be safe either way, but there is no memory pressure reason to
#  force that gate to fire when the object is cheap to keep and legitimately
#  still useful.
#
#  BTCUSDT is the biggest win: ~10.6M raw aggTrades rows across 8 columns
#  (id/price/qty/first/last/ts/two logicals) is the single largest object
#  this pipeline ever holds, and nothing past this point needs it - Sections
#  10 onward work from `durations`/`diurnal_fits`/`split_sets` (already
#  reduced to (time, duration, price, factor, adjDur) alone), not the raw
#  trade-level columns.
#
#  Also freed here, same reasoning: `assets` (filter-apply's own print-loop
#  list -- never referenced again after that loop, not even by duration-run,
#  which uses the bare fx/btc/nvda names directly) and btc/nvda themselves
#  (last used by duration-run; btc, "no filter" per filter-apply's own
#  comment, is a full unfiltered copy of btc0 and therefore just as large;
#  nvda survives until check-nvda-flags just above, so is safe to free only
#  from this point on, not any earlier).
#
#  `fx` is DELIBERATELY NOT freed here, unlike btc/nvda: fx-rollover
#  (Section 6, right after this chunk) now rebuilds GBP/USD's durations from
#  raw filtered events itself (build_durations_gap_aware()), not just from
#  the already-built durations table, so fx is still needed one chunk later.
#  Freed inside fx-rollover itself instead, once it's genuinely done with it.

if (!DURATIONS_CACHED) {
  freeable <- intersect(c("fx_raw", "btc_raw", "nvda_raw", "btc0", "nvda0",
                           "assets", "btc", "nvda"), ls(envir = .GlobalEnv))
  if (length(freeable) > 0) {
    sizes <- sort(sapply(freeable, function(nm) object.size(get(nm, envir = .GlobalEnv))), decreasing = TRUE)
    cat("=== Freeing raw/pre-filter objects (sizes before removal) ===\n\n")
    print(round(sizes / 1024^2, 1))   # MB
    rm(list = freeable, envir = .GlobalEnv)
    invisible(gc())
    cat(sprintf("\nFreed %s. fx0 is deliberately KEPT (see comment above) for\n",
                paste(freeable, collapse = ", ")))
    cat("eda-outlier-fx-isolated's gap-diagnosis check in Section 7.\n")
  }
}
```

```{r fx-rollover}

# The mean duration spikes at this period, and hence, if not removed, corrupts every duration model downstream.
# Drops the entire timestamps between the period before duration construction.

EXCLUDE_ROLLOVER   <- TRUE                 # set FALSE to reproduce prior results
ROLLOVER_UTC_START <- 21*60                # 21:00 UTC - DATA-DERIVED (rollover-fine-bin-plot),
ROLLOVER_UTC_END   <- 21*60 + 40           # 21:40 UTC - half-open [21:00, 21:40): 21:35 excluded, 21:40 kept.

FX_ARTIFACT_CUT_TIMES <- as.POSIXct(c(
  "2026-05-13 14:00:00", "2026-05-24 22:00:00", "2026-05-25 20:00:00",
  "2026-05-25 22:00:00", "2026-05-26 00:00:00", "2026-05-26 22:00:00",
  "2026-05-26 23:00:00", "2026-05-27 23:00:00"
), tz = "UTC")

#  Same underlying principle as the Sunday exclusion (Engle & Russell 1998,
#  who exclude the equity session open; Chen, Chung & Russell, who discard
#  overnight durations for CME FX futures) - a reopening after a
#  low-liquidity boundary is not a continuation of continuous trading.


build_durations_gap_aware <- function(d, gap_start_min, gap_end_min, single_session = FALSE,
                                       extra_cut_times = NULL) {
  stopifnot(all(c("sec", "frac_ns", "price") %in% names(d)))
  d <- copy(d)
  setorder(d, sec, frac_ns)

  d[, tod_min := hour(time) * 60 + minute(time)]
  d <- d[tod_min < gap_start_min | tod_min >= gap_end_min]   # DROP the window's own events
  d[, tod_min := NULL]

  d <- consolidate(d)
  n_merged <- attr(d, "n_merged")

  d[, tod_min := hour(time) * 60 + minute(time)]
  d[, day_part := as.integer(tod_min >= gap_end_min)]

  d[, extra_part := if (is.null(extra_cut_times)) 0L
                     else Reduce(`+`, lapply(extra_cut_times, function(ct) as.integer(time >= ct)))]


  d[, date := as.Date(time)]
  d[, session := if (single_session) 1L else .GRP, by = .(date, day_part, extra_part)]

  n_groups_with_extra    <- uniqueN(d[, .(date, day_part, extra_part)])
  n_groups_without_extra <- uniqueN(d[, .(date, day_part)])
  n_artifact_cut <- n_groups_with_extra - n_groups_without_extra
  d[, tod_min := NULL]

  d[, duration := {
    dsec  <- c(NA_real_, diff(sec))
    dfrac <- c(NA_real_, diff(frac_ns))
    dsec + dfrac / 1e9
  }, by = session]

  n_boundary <- sum(is.na(d$duration))
  d <- d[!is.na(duration)]

  if (any(d$duration == 0))
    stop("build_durations_gap_aware: ", sum(d$duration == 0), " ZERO durations survived consolidation.")
  if (any(d$duration < 0))
    stop("build_durations_gap_aware: NEGATIVE duration -- data are not sorted.")

  message(sprintf("  durations (gap-aware): %s (dropped %d session/gap-opening events, %d of which from extra_cut_times)",
                  format(nrow(d), big.mark = ","), n_boundary, n_artifact_cut))
  attr(d, "n_zero_removed")     <- n_merged
  attr(d, "n_boundary_dropped") <- n_boundary
  attr(d, "n_artifact_cut")     <- n_artifact_cut
  d[, c("day_part", "extra_part", "date") := NULL]
  d[]
}

if (!DURATIONS_CACHED) {

n_start <- nrow(durations[["GBP/USD"]])   # the plain build_durations(fx) result from duration-run

cat("FX events by weekday (Sunday already excluded upstream, Section 4.2):\n")
print(durations[["GBP/USD"]][, .(n = .N,
               mean_dur = round(mean(duration), 3),
               median   = round(median(duration), 3),
               cv       = round(sd(duration) / mean(duration), 2)),
           by = .(weekday = weekdays(time))][order(-n)])

if (EXCLUDE_ROLLOVER) {
  d_fx <- build_durations_gap_aware(fx, ROLLOVER_UTC_START, ROLLOVER_UTC_END,
                                     extra_cut_times = FX_ARTIFACT_CUT_TIMES)
  cat(sprintf("\nRollover-hour exclusion (gap-aware, %02d:%02d-%02d:%02d UTC): %s -> %s (%s fewer rows, %.2f%%)\n",
              ROLLOVER_UTC_START %/% 60, ROLLOVER_UTC_START %% 60,
              ROLLOVER_UTC_END %/% 60, ROLLOVER_UTC_END %% 60,
              format(n_start, big.mark = ","), format(nrow(d_fx), big.mark = ","),
              format(n_start - nrow(d_fx), big.mark = ","),
              100 * (n_start - nrow(d_fx)) / n_start))

  pipeline_counts[asset == "GBP/USD", rollover_removed := n_start - nrow(d_fx)]
  pipeline_counts[asset == "GBP/USD", n_zero_removed     := attr(d_fx, "n_zero_removed")]
  pipeline_counts[asset == "GBP/USD", n_boundary_dropped := attr(d_fx, "n_boundary_dropped")]
  if (!"n_artifact_cut" %in% names(pipeline_counts)) pipeline_counts[, n_artifact_cut := NA_integer_]
  pipeline_counts[asset == "GBP/USD", n_artifact_cut := attr(d_fx, "n_artifact_cut")]
} else {
  d_fx <- durations[["GBP/USD"]]
  cat("\nRollover exclusion DISABLED (EXCLUDE_ROLLOVER = FALSE)\n")
  pipeline_counts[asset == "GBP/USD", rollover_removed := 0L]
}

durations[["GBP/USD"]] <- d_fx

rm(d_fx, n_start)
if (exists("fx", inherits = FALSE)) rm(fx)   # last use was build_durations_gap_aware() above
invisible(gc())
}
```
