# 7. Exploratory data analysis

## 7.1 Summary statistics and overdispersion

```{r eda-basic-structure}
#  BASIC DATA STRUCTURE - one row per asset, the sample-description table.


basic_structure <- rbindlist(lapply(names(durations), function(nm) {
  d <- durations[[nm]][time < TEST_END]   # TRAIN+TEST only -- the data actually used
  x <- d$duration
  q <- quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.75), names = FALSE)

  pc <- if (exists("pipeline_counts") && !is.null(pipeline_counts))
          pipeline_counts[asset == nm] else NULL
  get_count <- function(col) {
    if (is.null(pc) || !col %in% names(pc)) return(NA_integer_)
    v <- pc[[col]]
    if (length(v) == 0 || is.na(v)) NA_integer_ else v
  }
  n_zero      <- get_count("n_zero_removed")

  
  weekend_n   <- get_count("weekend_removed")
  boundary_n  <- get_count("n_boundary_dropped")
  rollover_n  <- get_count("rollover_removed")
  if (is.null(pc)) { weekend_n <- boundary_n <- rollover_n <- NA_integer_ }

  data.table(
    asset            = nm,
    n_transactions   = nrow(d),
    start            = format(min(d$time), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    end              = format(max(d$time), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    trading_days     = length(unique(as.Date(d$time))),
    min_dur_s        = signif(min(x), 4),
    max_dur_s        = round(max(x), 2),
    mean_s           = round(mean(x), 4),
    median_s         = round(median(x), 4),
    sd_s             = round(sd(x), 4),
    Q1_s             = round(q[1], 4),
    Q3_s             = round(q[2], 4),
    IQR_s            = round(q[2] - q[1], 4),
    pct_lt_1ms       = round(100 * mean(x < 0.001), 3),
    pct_lt_10ms      = round(100 * mean(x < 0.01),  3),
    pct_lt_100ms     = round(100 * mean(x < 0.1),   3),
    pct_lt_1s        = round(100 * mean(x < 1),     3),
    n_zero_removed     = n_zero,
    weekend_removed    = weekend_n,
    n_boundary_dropped = boundary_n,
    rollover_removed   = rollover_n
  )
}))

print(basic_structure)

cat("\nn_zero_removed      : same-timestamp events consolidated into one\n")
cat("                       instant (Section 5) -- would otherwise be a\n")
cat("                       zero duration, which the likelihood cannot take.\n")
cat("weekend_removed     : RAW EVENTS dropped by filter_fx_weekend (FX only,\n")
cat("                       pre-duration-build; NA elsewhere).\n")
cat("n_boundary_dropped  : CONSOLIDATED-INSTANT count -- each session's first\n")
cat("                       event, dropped everywhere it has no preceding-\n")
cat("                       event gap to measure (BTC is single-session, 0\n")
cat("                       there). For FX this is the GAP-AWARE build's own\n")
cat("                       count (daily splits + rollover + the 8\n")
cat("                       FX_ARTIFACT_CUT_TIMES), not the plain build's.\n")
cat("rollover_removed    : FX only -- net DURATION-COUNT delta between the\n")
cat("                       plain and gap-aware builds. Deliberately kept\n")
cat("                       separate from the two counts above rather than\n")
cat("                       summed with them: it is a different unit (a\n")
cat("                       row-count difference across two builds, not a\n")
cat("                       raw-event or consolidated-instant count) and\n")
cat("                       already partly reflects their own difference.\n")
cat("NA in any column means the durations cache predates pipeline_counts --\n")
cat("delete DURATIONS_CACHE_FILE and re-knit to populate it.\n")
cat("\nn_transactions/start/end/trading_days and every duration-level stat\n")
cat("above are restricted to time < TEST_END (TRAIN+TEST, the data the\n")
cat("pipeline actually fits/predicts on). The four removal-count columns are\n")
cat("NOT re-restricted -- pipeline_counts is captured once, upstream, over\n")
cat("the WHOLE loaded SAMPLE_START..SAMPLE_END window, so those counts can\n")
cat("include removals from the unused SAMPLE_END-side tail.\n")
```

```{r eda-summary}

#  THE NUMBER THAT MOTIVATES THE MODEL: the coefficient of variation.
#
#  Under a homogeneous Poisson process durations are iid Exponential, for which
#  mean and standard deviation coincide exactly, so CV = 1. This is a
#  CONSEQUENCE of the model, not a quantity to be estimated, and it yields a
#  test requiring only the sample moments.
#
#  CV > 1 is OVERDISPERSION: more short durations and more extreme long ones
#  than a constant arrival rate permits.
#
#  RESTRICTED TO time < TEST_END (TRAIN+TEST only) -- same scope as
#  eda-basic-structure's own basic_structure table, and the same reasoning:
#  everything from TEST_END to SAMPLE_END is loaded but never used by any
#  fit or forecast, so it has no place in a table motivating the model.

eda_summary <- rbindlist(lapply(names(durations), function(nm) {
  d <- durations[[nm]][time < TEST_END, duration]
  data.table(
    asset        = nm,
    n            = length(d),
    lambda_hat   = 1 / mean(d),
    mean_s       = mean(d),
    median_s     = median(d),
    sd_s         = sd(d),
    CV           = sd(d) / mean(d),        # = 1 under Poisson
    skew         = mean((d - mean(d))^3) / sd(d)^3,
    min_s        = min(d),
    max_s        = max(d),
    p99          = quantile(d, 0.99),
    pct_sub_ms   = 100 * mean(d < 0.001),
    mean_median  = mean(d) / median(d)     # ratio: extreme for NVDA
  )
}))

print(eda_summary)

cat("\n=== PER-ASSET DETAIL (TRAIN+TEST only) ===\n")
for (nm in names(durations)) {
  d <- durations[[nm]][time < TEST_END, duration]
  cat(sprintf("\n--- %s (n = %s) ---\n", nm, format(length(d), big.mark = ",")))
  cat(sprintf("  min / median / mean / max : %.9f / %.4f / %.4f / %.2f  seconds\n",
              min(d), median(d), mean(d), max(d)))
  cat(sprintf("  coefficient of variation  : %.4f   (Poisson requires 1.0)\n",
              sd(d) / mean(d)))
  cat(sprintf("  %% below 1 ms / 1 s        : %.2f%% / %.2f%%\n",
              100 * mean(d < 0.001), 100 * mean(d < 1)))
  cat(sprintf("  quantiles 50/90/99/99.9   : %.5f / %.4f / %.4f / %.4f\n",
              quantile(d, .5), quantile(d, .9),
              quantile(d, .99), quantile(d, .999)))
}

cat("\nREADING IT: CV exceeds unity on all three assets. The homogeneous\n")
cat("Poisson process requires exactly 1, so it is rejected on the sample\n")
cat("moments alone, before any estimation.\n")
```


## 7.2 Distribution of durations

```{r eda-distribution}

#  THE SHAPE ITSELF, before any test statistic summarises it. Four views of the
#  same distribution:
#    histogram / density  -- the raw right skew
#    boxplot               -- how far the extreme tail sits from the box, on a
#                              scale that makes outlier density visible
#    log-duration histogram-- the skew compressed; sub-ms mass (BTC/NVDA
#                              especially) separated from the bulk instead of
#                              piled into the first bin of a linear-scale plot
#
#  Mean and SD are reported alongside: under the exponential benchmark
#  (Poisson arrivals) mean == SD exactly, i.e. CV = 1 (Section 7.1's number,
#  repeated here next to the plot it explains).

dist_dt <- rbindlist(lapply(names(durations), function(nm)
  data.table(asset = nm, x = durations[[nm]]$duration)))

ggplot(dist_dt, aes(x = x)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100, fill = "steelblue", colour = NA) +
  facet_wrap(~ asset, ncol = 1, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Histogram of durations", x = "Duration (s)", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(dist_dt, aes(x = asset, y = x)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "steelblue", outlier.size = 0.3, outlier.alpha = 0.2) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(title    = "Boxplot of durations (log y-axis)",
       subtitle = "Linear-scale boxplot would compress into an unreadable sliver at these skew levels",
       x = NULL, y = "Duration (s, log scale)") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(dist_dt, aes(x = x)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100, fill = "steelblue", colour = NA) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ asset, ncol = 1, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Histogram of durations, log-x scale", x = "Duration (s, log scale)", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

cat("=== Mean / SD / CV (repeated from Section 7.1, next to the plots) ===\n\n")
print(dist_dt[, .(mean_s = round(mean(x), 4), sd_s = round(sd(x), 4),
                   CV = round(sd(x) / mean(x), 4)), by = asset])
cat("\nCV = 1 is what the exponential (Poisson-arrival) benchmark requires.\n")
cat("CV > 1 here is the same overdispersion finding as Section 7.1, now read\n")
cat("directly off the right-skewed shape in the plots above.\n")

rm(dist_dt); invisible(gc())
```

## 7.5 Duration clustering — the direct motivation for ACD

```{r eda-acf}

#  If durations were iid (pure Poisson), the autocorrelation would be zero at
#  every lag. Slow decay is duration CLUSTERING: a short duration tends to be
#  followed by another short one.
#
#  This is the feature ACD is built to model, and it is the reason neither
#  Poisson specification can survive.
#
#  ⚠ THE ACF PLOT is capped at the FIRST 2M observations (a contiguous
#  chronological head, via d[1:2e6] -- NOT a random subsample/sample() draw,
#  so this is a plotting-tractability cap, not a claim about subsampling
#  stability), for plotting tractability -- defensible because ACF at these
#  short lags reflects LOCAL, short-range dependence, so any representative
#  contiguous stretch shows essentially the same decay pattern. The LJUNG-BOX
#  STATISTIC below is deliberately
#  NOT capped: Q(L) scales roughly linearly with n (stated explicitly in
#  Section 10.2's own commentary), so capping it here would make this chunk's
#  LB value disagree with Table I's (Section 10.2), which correctly uses the
#  full series. Verified empirically before making this change: capping
#  BTC/NVDA at 2M changes Q(15) by 81%/50% respectively, which is the likely
#  source of the report discrepancy noted in Section 11's outstanding-work
#  list. Computing both on the full series removes the mismatch at the root.

acf_dt <- rbindlist(lapply(names(durations), function(nm) {
  d <- durations[[nm]]$duration
  if (length(d) > 2e6) d <- d[1:2e6]     # PLOT ONLY -- see note above
  a <- acf(d, lag.max = 100, plot = FALSE)
  data.table(asset = nm, lag = as.integer(a$lag), acf = as.numeric(a$acf))
}))[lag > 0]

ggplot(acf_dt, aes(x = lag, y = acf)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue", width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ asset, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title    = "Autocorrelation of raw durations",
       subtitle = "Slow decay = duration clustering, the feature ACD is built to model",
       x = "Lag", y = "ACF") +
  theme_minimal()

# Formal test that durations are NOT independent. FULL series, not capped --
# so this matches the Ljung-Box values used later in Table I (Section 10.2).
lb_raw <- rbindlist(lapply(names(durations), function(nm) {
  d <- durations[[nm]]$duration
  t <- Box.test(d, lag = LB_LAGS, type = "Ljung-Box")
  data.table(asset   = nm,
             LB_stat = round(t$statistic, 1),
             df      = LB_LAGS,
             crit    = LB_CRIT,
             p_value = format.pval(t$p.value))
}))
print(lb_raw)
```

## 7.6 PACF of durations

```{r eda-pacf}
# =============================================================================
#  PARTIAL autocorrelation, alongside the ACF above. Not used to choose ACD
#  orders directly -- unlike ARMA on a stationary linear series, there is no
#  clean PACF-cutoff rule for ACD's multiplicative, non-negative conditional
#  mean. Formal order selection stays where it belongs: likelihood, AIC, BIC,
#  LR tests, residual diagnostics, done per rung in Section 10. This plot is
#  read qualitatively, for a first sense of the dependence structure only.
# =============================================================================
pacf_dt <- rbindlist(lapply(names(durations), function(nm) {
  d <- durations[[nm]]$duration
  if (length(d) > 2e6) d <- d[1:2e6]     # PLOT ONLY -- same cap as the ACF above
  p <- pacf(d, lag.max = 100, plot = FALSE)
  data.table(asset = nm, lag = as.integer(p$lag), pacf = as.numeric(p$acf))
}))

ggplot(pacf_dt, aes(x = lag, y = pacf)) +
  geom_col(fill = "firebrick", width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ asset, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title    = "Partial autocorrelation of raw durations",
       subtitle = "Qualitative read only -- order selection uses likelihood/AIC/BIC/LR/residual diagnostics (Section 10), not this plot",
       x = "Lag", y = "PACF") +
  theme_minimal()

rm(pacf_dt); invisible(gc())
```


## 7.8 Diurnal pattern — justifies the seasonal adjustment

```{r eda-diurnal-raw}

#  Trading activity follows a predictable daily pattern. This DETERMINISTIC
#  variation must be separated from the stochastic clustering the model is
#  intended to capture -- otherwise a slow midday period is indistinguishable
#  from a genuine lull.
#
#  Expected shapes, and they differ by market structure:
#    GBP/USD -- smooth 24h wave; trough at the London/NY overlap (~13-14 UTC),
#               sharp peak at the daily rollover (~21-22 UTC)
#    NVDA    -- U-shaped ACTIVITY within the session, which inverts to a
#               mid-session MAXIMUM when expressed in durations
#    BTC     -- flattest: 24/7 venue with no imposed schedule

diurnal_raw <- rbindlist(lapply(names(durations), function(nm) {
  d <- copy(durations[[nm]])
  d[, hour := as.integer(format(time, "%H", tz = "UTC"))]
  d[, .(mean_dur = mean(duration), n = .N), by = hour][, asset := nm]
}))

ggplot(diurnal_raw, aes(x = hour, y = mean_dur)) +
  geom_line(colour = "darkorange", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ asset, ncol = 1, scales = "fixed") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(title    = "Mean duration by hour of day (UTC)",
       subtitle = "Deterministic time-of-day structure; motivates the diurnal adjustment",
       x = "Hour (UTC)", y = "Mean duration, seconds (log scale)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 7.10 Cross-asset tie structure — the microstructure finding

```{r eda-ties}

#  How much consolidation each venue required, and what that reveals about its
#  market structure. This is a cross-asset finding in its own right:
#
#    FX   -- ~0% empirically, NOT because ties are structurally impossible:
#            Section 5's own consolidate() comment notes FX ties ARE genuine
#            (two quote revisions inside one millisecond, a clock-resolution
#            collision, not a split fill) and are merged when they occur. The
#            reason the rate is near-zero here specifically is this feed's own
#            practical timestamp granularity (~50ms between distinct raw
#            ticks, confirmed directly against the raw CSV), which makes two
#            quotes landing in the exact same millisecond rare in practice --
#            an empirical fact about this vendor's resolution, not a
#            structural "no fills to aggregate" argument (an OTC feed lacking
#            a matching engine has no ORDER fills, but that says nothing about
#            whether two quote REVISIONS can share a timestamp).
#    BTC  -- ~49%, DESPITE Binance aggregating upstream. The upstream step
#            merges same-price fills only, so a sweep across several price
#            levels still emits one record per level
#    NVDA -- ~48%, and here the exchange's own flags confirm the boundary
#
#  n_events counts RECORDS ABSORBED into each instant, so mean_batch > 1 means
#  the venue splits arrivals across multiple reported lines.

ties <- rbindlist(lapply(names(durations), function(nm) {
  d <- durations[[nm]]
  data.table(
    asset            = nm,
    instants         = nrow(d),
    raw_records      = sum(d$n_events),
    pct_consolidated = round(100 * (1 - nrow(d) / sum(d$n_events)), 2),
    max_batch        = max(d$n_events),
    mean_batch       = round(mean(d$n_events), 3),
    pct_singletons   = round(100 * mean(d$n_events == 1), 2)
  )
}))
print(ties)
```


## 7.13 Sub-millisecond analysis

```{r eda-submillisecond}
# =============================================================================
#  THE bucket table motivating the near-zero-duration corruption discussed
#  throughout the WACD/Log-ACD sections (Section 10.5 onward): what fraction
#  of each asset's durations fall below successively finer thresholds.
#
#  Approximate benchmarks already established elsewhere in this document:
#  GBP/USD ~0% below 1ms (a quote feed has no matching-engine batching to
#  produce sub-ms ties), BTCUSDT ~11%, NVDA ~31% -- the gap between an OTC
#  quote feed and two execution venues with batched fills, and the reason
#  Weibull's density blow-up near zero (Section 10.5) affects BTC/NVDA but not
#  FX.
# =============================================================================
submill <- rbindlist(lapply(names(durations), function(nm) {
  x <- durations[[nm]]$duration
  data.table(
    asset      = nm,
    `<1us`     = round(100 * mean(x < 1e-6), 4),
    `<100us`   = round(100 * mean(x < 1e-4), 4),
    `<1ms`     = round(100 * mean(x < 1e-3), 3),
    `1-10ms`   = round(100 * mean(x >= 1e-3 & x < 1e-2), 3),
    `>10ms`    = round(100 * mean(x >= 1e-2), 3)
  )
}))

cat("=== Sub-millisecond bucket table (% of durations in each bucket) ===\n\n")
print(submill)

cat("\nRow sums (should be ~100%; the three RIGHTMOST columns are mutually\n")
cat("exclusive and exhaustive -- <1us and <100us are cumulative subsets of <1ms,\n")
cat("shown for finer resolution, not additional mass):\n")
print(submill[, .(asset, total_pct = `<1ms` + `1-10ms` + `>10ms`)])

cat("\nBenchmark check against the approximate figures already established:\n")
for (nm in names(durations)) {
  cat(sprintf("  %-8s: %.2f%% below 1ms\n", nm, submill[asset == nm]$`<1ms`))
}
```

## 7.14 Trading-day comparison

```{r eda-trading-day}
# =============================================================================
#  PER-DAY duration statistics -- mean, median, n transactions, CV -- reveal
#  whether particular days had dramatically different market activity (a news
#  event, a holiday-thinned session, a data gap) that a single whole-sample
#  statistic (Section 7.1) would mask by averaging over.
# =============================================================================
by_day <- rbindlist(lapply(names(durations), function(nm) {
  d <- copy(durations[[nm]])
  d[, day := as.Date(time)]
  d[, .(asset = nm, n = .N, mean_dur = mean(duration), median_dur = median(duration),
        sd_dur = sd(duration), CV = sd(duration) / mean(duration)), by = day]
}))

cat("=== Per-day statistics, GBP/USD (head) ===\n\n")
print(by_day[asset == "GBP/USD"][order(day)][1:min(10, .N)])

ggplot(by_day, aes(x = day, y = mean_dur)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue") + geom_point(size = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ asset, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Mean duration by trading day", x = NULL, y = "Mean duration (s)") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(by_day, aes(x = day, y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkorange") +
  facet_wrap(~ asset, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Transaction count by trading day", x = NULL, y = "n") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(by_day, aes(x = day, y = CV)) +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick") + geom_point(size = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~ asset, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title    = "Coefficient of variation by trading day",
       subtitle = "Dotted line at 1 = the exponential/Poisson benchmark (Section 7.1), now tracked day by day",
       x = NULL, y = "CV") +
  theme_minimal()

cat("\n=== Day with the most extreme mean duration, per asset ===\n\n")
print(by_day[, .SD[which.max(mean_dur)], by = asset][, .(asset, day, n, mean_dur, CV)])

rm(by_day); invisible(gc())
```

## 7.15 Outlier / extreme-duration audit

```{r eda-outlier-audit}

#  THE LONGEST raw durations per asset, examined rather than assumed. A large
#  duration should not be dropped just because it is large -- it needs to be
#  read against its context first:
#    genuine market inactivity  -- a quiet stretch, no external cause
#    market closure             -- should already be IMPOSSIBLE here: weekend
#                                   (filter_fx_weekend), extended hours
#                                   (filter_nvda_session) and the daily
#                                   rollover (fx-rollover) are removed
#                                   upstream, and every session's opening gap
#                                   is dropped by build_durations. A survivor
#                                   coinciding with one of those boundaries
#                                   regardless would point at a bug in that
#                                   filtering, not a market event.
#    data problem                -- an isolated single-observation spike with
#                                   ordinary durations immediately either side
#                                   is more consistent with a bad timestamp
#                                   than a real gap in trading
#                                   (PREV/NEXT columns below let this be
#                                   checked directly)
#    unusual trading behaviour   -- a real, newsworthy lull; nothing in the
#                                   data itself distinguishes this from
#                                   "genuine inactivity" above, it is a
#                                   judgement call the timestamp/weekday/hour
#                                   columns are printed to support
#
#  PREV/NEXT are the durations immediately before/after each flagged one, in
#  the asset's own chronological order (not shown sorted) -- a spike sitting
#  between two ordinary durations reads differently from a spike inside an
#  already-slow run of several long ones.

OUTLIER_TOP_N <- 15

outlier_audit <- rbindlist(lapply(names(durations), function(nm) {
  d <- copy(durations[[nm]]); setorder(d, sec, frac_ns)
  d[, `:=`(prev_dur = shift(duration, 1), next_dur = shift(duration, -1))]
  d[, rank_desc := frank(-duration, ties.method = "first")]
  top <- d[rank_desc <= OUTLIER_TOP_N]
  setorder(top, rank_desc)
  data.table(
    asset      = nm,
    rank       = top$rank_desc,
    time       = format(top$time, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    weekday    = weekdays(top$time),
    hour_utc   = hour(top$time),
    duration_s = round(top$duration, 2),
    prev_dur_s = round(top$prev_dur, 3),
    next_dur_s = round(top$next_dur, 3),
    pctile     = round(100 * (1 - OUTLIER_TOP_N / nrow(d)), 4)
  )
}))

for (nm in names(durations)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n=== %s: top %d longest durations ===\n\n", nm, OUTLIER_TOP_N))
  print(outlier_audit[asset == nm][, -"asset"])
}

# ---- Boundary-survivor check: should be EMPTY on every asset -----------------
# If any flagged duration's time-of-day falls inside a window that upstream
# filtering (weekend/extended-hours/rollover) was supposed to already remove,
# that filter has a bug -- this is not a judgement call like the rest of the
# audit, it is a pass/fail correctness check.
cat("\n=== Boundary-survivor check (should print 0 rows on every asset) ===\n\n")
boundary_hits <- rbindlist(lapply(names(durations), function(nm) {
  top <- outlier_audit[asset == nm]
  tod_min <- hour(as.POSIXct(top$time, tz = "UTC")) * 60 +
             minute(as.POSIXct(top$time, tz = "UTC"))
  flag <- rep(FALSE, nrow(top))
  if (nm == "GBP/USD") {
    # wday()==1 (Sunday), not top$weekday=="Sunday": that column comes from
    # weekdays(), which is locale-dependent and would silently match nothing
    # on a non-English locale.
    flag <- flag | wday(as.POSIXct(top$time, tz = "UTC")) == 1 |
            (tod_min >= ROLLOVER_UTC_START & tod_min < ROLLOVER_UTC_END)
  } else if (nm == "NVDA") {
    flag <- flag | !(tod_min >= SESSION_OPEN & tod_min < SESSION_CLOSE)
  }
  top[flag]
}))
print(boundary_hits)
if (nrow(boundary_hits) == 0)
  cat("None -- every flagged extreme sits inside filtered trading hours, as it should.\n")

cat("\nREADING IT: with market-closure explanations already ruled out by\n")
cat("construction (see boundary-survivor check above), each remaining extreme\n")
cat("is either genuine inactivity/unusual behaviour (ordinary PREV/NEXT\n")
cat("neighbours -- the gap is real, just long) or a data problem worth a closer\n")
cat("look (PREV/NEXT also elevated, or an isolated spike with no discernible\n")
cat("market cause). None are dropped here: this is an audit, not a filter --\n")
cat("any resulting removal should be a deliberate, documented decision the way\n")
cat("Sections 4 and 6 already document theirs, not a silent threshold.\n")

rm(boundary_hits); invisible(gc())   # outlier_audit kept -- used by the two follow-up chunks below
```

# 8. Train / test partition

```{r split}
# =============================================================================
#  Chronological split: TRAIN_DAYS (14) calendar days from SAMPLE_START for
#  training, TEST_DAYS (5) calendar days immediately after that (day 15,
#  SPLIT_TIME, through TEST_END) held out as TEST -- not everything
#  remaining to SAMPLE_END. Both boundaries defined once in Section 1.2.
#
#  CHRONOLOGICAL, NOT RANDOM. Durations are autocorrelated: a random partition
#  would place observations from the same burst of activity on both sides of
#  the division, and the held-out data would not be independent of the data
#  used for fitting.
#
#  MOVED BEFORE DIURNAL ADJUSTMENT (Section 9): the diurnal factor itself is
#  fit on TRAIN only -- this chunk now DEFINES that boundary once, on the raw
#  (pre-diurnal) duration series, and every diurnal-fit function (Section 9)
#  reads split_sets[[asset]]$train directly instead of re-deriving its own
#  time<SPLIT_TIME filter. split_sets is ENRICHED with adjDur/factor once
#  diurnal_fits exists -- see split-attach-adjdur at the end of Section 9 --
#  but the TRAIN/TEST partition itself, and the guarantee that no TEST row
#  informs any fit, is established here, before any preprocessing choice.
#
#  Every model on the ladder uses this split and no other.
# =============================================================================
split_sets <- lapply(names(durations), function(nm) {
  d <- durations[[nm]]
  setorder(d, sec, frac_ns)
  list(train = d[time <  SPLIT_TIME],
       test  = d[time >= SPLIT_TIME & time < TEST_END])
})
names(split_sets) <- names(durations)

split_summary_raw <- rbindlist(lapply(names(split_sets), function(nm) {
  tr <- split_sets[[nm]]$train
  te <- split_sets[[nm]]$test
  data.table(
    asset          = nm,
    n_train        = nrow(tr),
    n_test         = nrow(te),
    pct_train      = round(100 * nrow(tr) / (nrow(tr) + nrow(te)), 1),
    train_start    = format(min(tr$time)),
    train_end      = format(max(tr$time)),
    test_start     = format(min(te$time)),
    test_end       = format(max(te$time)),
    mean_dur_train = round(mean(tr$duration), 4),
    mean_dur_test  = round(mean(te$duration), 4)
  )
}))
print(split_summary_raw)

# No overlap, and the test set begins where the training set ends.
for (nm in names(split_sets)) {
  stopifnot(max(split_sets[[nm]]$train$time) < min(split_sets[[nm]]$test$time))
}
cat("\nSplit verified: no overlap on any asset.\n")

cat("\nNOTE: this is the RAW (pre-diurnal) partition -- mean_dur_train/test\n")
cat("above are on UNADJUSTED durations, so any difference between them mixes\n")
cat("genuine activity-level drift with the ordinary time-of-day cycle (e.g.\n")
cat("TRAIN and TEST simply covering different average hours-of-day). The\n")
cat("adjusted-scale version of this same check (isolating genuine level drift\n")
cat("from the diurnal cycle) is reported again once diurnal_fits exists --\n")
cat("see split-attach-adjdur at the end of Section 9.\n")
```



# 9. Diurnal adjustment

```{r diurnal-method-decision-helper}

pick_diurnal_winner <- function(res_tbl, near_zero_frac = 0.001, blowup_mult = 50) {
  near_zero_thresh <- if ("raw_scale" %in% names(res_tbl) && is.finite(res_tbl$raw_scale[1]))
    near_zero_frac * res_tbl$raw_scale[1] else near_zero_frac

  finite_rmse <- res_tbl$rmse_profile[is.finite(res_tbl$rmse_profile)]
  
  ref_rmse <- if (length(finite_rmse) > 0) min(finite_rmse) else NA_real_
  trustworthy <- is.finite(res_tbl$rmse_profile) &
                 res_tbl$rmse_profile > near_zero_thresh &
                 res_tbl$rmse_profile < blowup_mult * ref_rmse
  if (!any(trustworthy)) trustworthy <- is.finite(res_tbl$rmse_profile)  # fallback: don't crash if ALL flagged
  untrustworthy_reason <- ifelse(!is.finite(res_tbl$rmse_profile), "non-finite (numerical blow-up)",
                          ifelse(res_tbl$rmse_profile <= near_zero_thresh, "implausibly near-zero (near-interpolation)",
                          ifelse(res_tbl$rmse_profile >= blowup_mult * ref_rmse, "far above the best arm (blow-up)", "")))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(res_tbl))) {
    if (!trustworthy[i]) cat(sprintf("  EXCLUDED from winner eligibility: %s (%s)\n",
                                     res_tbl$method[i], untrustworthy_reason[i]))
  }
  winner_idx <- which(trustworthy)[which.min(res_tbl$rmse_profile[trustworthy])]
  res_tbl$method[winner_idx]
}
```

## 9.0 Diurnal adjustment: two methods, compared

Two candidate methods for the seasonal factor s(t), fitted for all three
assets and compared directly rather than assumed:

**Method 1 -- E&R exact replication.** Engle & Russell's (1998) own approach:
average raw durations in 30-minute time-of-day intervals, then smooth the
resulting step function with a natural cubic spline knotted hourly.

**Method 2 -- finer averaging, same 2x knot-to-bin ratio.** Average at
5-minute resolution instead of 30-minute (far more data feeding the same
spline), knots spaced every 10 minutes -- the SAME bin-to-knot ratio Method
1 uses (30-min bin / 60-min knot = 2x), just applied at a finer resolution,
so bin width is the only thing that changes between the two methods, not
the relative knot density.

Both are natural cubic splines (`ns()`), differing only in how much data
feeds the smoother before fitting; the comparison below is therefore a
direct test of averaging resolution, holding the smoothing method (and its
relative knot density) fixed.

```{r diurnal-method-fit}

#  TRY 1: fit_ER_exact() -- 30-min interval averaging, hourly knots. E&R's
#  own method, replicated as literally as this dataset allows.
#
#  TRY 2: fit_5min_10knot() -- 5-min interval averaging, 10-min knot spacing
#  (same 2x bin-to-knot ratio as fit_ER_exact's 30-min-bin/60-min-knot).
#  Verified directly against real data before being written here: BTCUSDT
#  (288 bins/143 knots) and NVDA (78/38) both 0 NA coefficients; GBP/USD
#  (280/143) has 1 NA coefficient (RANK DEFICIENT) -- 143 knots pushes
#  close to overfitting FX's own bin count, reported as such below rather
#  than hidden, and read alongside score_diurnal's own numbers when judging
#  whether this method should actually win for GBP/USD specifically.
#
#  Both write factor_tbl on the SAME 5-min GRID (0..1435) regardless of
#  their own internal fitting resolution, so downstream code that reads
#  diurnal_fits[[nm]]$factor_tbl (e.g. Section 10.2's ipp-forecast, which
#  assumes bin_min=5) is unaffected by which of the two wins below.

library(splines); library(ggplot2)
tod_min_fn <- function(t) hour(t) * 60 + minute(t)
DIURNAL_GRID <- seq(0, 1435, 5)

fit_ER_exact <- function(asset, floor_q = 0.05) {
  # Column-trimmed, not a full copy(durations[[asset]]) -- this function only
  # ever needs (time, sec, frac_ns, duration) from dfx (the merge/adjDur step
  # at the end), never price/size/n_events/session. At BTC's ~10.6M raw rows
  # a full-width copy() was the direct cause of a real "cannot allocate TMP
  # for my_n=10643178 items" setorder() crash under memory pressure; the
  # 4-column subset is both a genuine copy (safe to mutate/sort without
  # touching the shared durations[[asset]]) and roughly half the footprint.
  dfx <- durations[[asset]][, .(time, sec, frac_ns, duration)]
  setorder(dfx, sec, frac_ns)
  trn <- split_sets[[asset]]$train   # from `split`, Section 8 -- RAW pre-diurnal partition

  bm_all <- trn[, .(m = mean(duration), n = .N),
                by = .(tb = (tod_min_fn(time) %/% 30) * 30)][is.finite(m)]
  n_thin <- sum(bm_all$n < 5)   # captured BEFORE the n>=5 filter, not after
  bm <- bm_all[n >= 5][order(tb)]
  knots_hourly <- seq(60, 1380, 60)
  knots_use <- knots_hourly[knots_hourly > min(bm$tb) & knots_hourly < max(bm$tb)]

  # weights = n: an unweighted fit gives a bin with 3 raw observations the
  # same influence as one with 200,000, even though the bin mean's own
  # variance scales as 1/n. Weighting by each bin's own observation count is
  # the minimal correction (a log-duration fit would be the stronger one).
  fitobj <- withCallingHandlers(
    lm(m ~ ns(tb, knots = knots_use), data = bm, weights = n),
    warning = function(w) invokeRestart("muffleWarning"))
  n_na <- sum(is.na(coef(fitobj)))
  cat(sprintf("%-8s [E&R exact]:    %d 30-min bins, %d hourly knots, %d NA coef%s\n",
              asset, nrow(bm), length(knots_use), n_na, if (n_na > 0) " -- RANK DEFICIENT" else ""))

  f_grid <- as.numeric(predict(fitobj, newdata = data.frame(
    tb = pmin(pmax(DIURNAL_GRID, min(bm$tb)), max(bm$tb)))))
  # Floor computed over IN-DOMAIN grid points only: outside [min(bm$tb),
  # max(bm$tb)] f_grid is a flat-extrapolated duplicate of the boundary
  # prediction (from the pmin/pmax clamp above), not a genuine quantile of
  # the fitted curve. For a session-bounded asset like NVDA, most of the
  # 0..1435 grid is outside its ~810..1170 domain, so quantile() over the
  # padded array is mostly counting repeats of one endpoint value.
  in_domain <- DIURNAL_GRID >= min(bm$tb) & DIURNAL_GRID <= max(bm$tb)
  fl <- unname(quantile(f_grid[in_domain], floor_q, na.rm = TRUE)); if (!is.finite(fl) || fl <= 0) fl <- 1e-3
  f_grid <- pmax(f_grid, fl)

  factor_tbl <- data.table(tod_bin = DIURNAL_GRID, factor = f_grid)
  dfx[, tod_bin := (tod_min_fn(time) %/% 5) * 5]
  dfx <- merge(dfx, factor_tbl, by = "tod_bin", all.x = TRUE)
  setorder(dfx, sec, frac_ns)               # merge() scrambles order -- must re-sort
  dfx[, adjDur := duration / factor]
  list(adj = dfx, factor_tbl = factor_tbl, floor = fl, n_thin = n_thin, n_na_coef = n_na,
       domain = c(min(bm$tb), max(bm$tb)))
}

fit_5min_10knot <- function(asset, floor_q = 0.05) {
  # Column-trimmed -- see fit_ER_exact's own comment above for why (a real
  # memory crash at BTC's scale, fixed by not carrying price/size/n_events/
  # session through a function that never reads them).
  dfx <- durations[[asset]][, .(time, sec, frac_ns, duration)]
  setorder(dfx, sec, frac_ns)
  trn <- split_sets[[asset]]$train   # from `split`, Section 8 -- RAW pre-diurnal partition

  bm_all <- trn[, .(m = mean(duration), n = .N),
                by = .(tb = (tod_min_fn(time) %/% 5) * 5)][is.finite(m)]
  n_thin <- sum(bm_all$n < 3)   # captured BEFORE the n>=3 filter, not after
  bm <- bm_all[n >= 3][order(tb)]
  knots_10min <- seq(10, 1430, 10)
  knots_use <- knots_10min[knots_10min > min(bm$tb) & knots_10min < max(bm$tb)]

  # weights = n -- see fit_ER_exact's own comment above for why.
  fitobj <- withCallingHandlers(
    lm(m ~ ns(tb, knots = knots_use), data = bm, weights = n),
    warning = function(w) invokeRestart("muffleWarning"))
  n_na <- sum(is.na(coef(fitobj)))
  cat(sprintf("%-8s [5min/10knot]:  %d 5-min bins, %d knots, %d NA coef%s\n",
              asset, nrow(bm), length(knots_use), n_na, if (n_na > 0) " -- RANK DEFICIENT" else ""))

  f_grid <- as.numeric(predict(fitobj, newdata = data.frame(
    tb = pmin(pmax(DIURNAL_GRID, min(bm$tb)), max(bm$tb)))))
  # Floor over in-domain grid points only -- see fit_ER_exact's own comment.
  in_domain <- DIURNAL_GRID >= min(bm$tb) & DIURNAL_GRID <= max(bm$tb)
  fl <- unname(quantile(f_grid[in_domain], floor_q, na.rm = TRUE)); if (!is.finite(fl) || fl <= 0) fl <- 1e-3
  f_grid <- pmax(f_grid, fl)

  # factor_tbl/tod_bin below stay on the fixed 5-min DIURNAL_GRID -- here
  # this fit's own averaging resolution and the output grid happen to
  # coincide (both 5-min), unlike fit_ER_exact's 30-min-bin fit, but the
  # merge/tod_bin step is kept identical across both functions regardless.
  factor_tbl <- data.table(tod_bin = DIURNAL_GRID, factor = f_grid)
  dfx[, tod_bin := (tod_min_fn(time) %/% 5) * 5]
  dfx <- merge(dfx, factor_tbl, by = "tod_bin", all.x = TRUE)
  setorder(dfx, sec, frac_ns)
  dfx[, adjDur := duration / factor]
  list(adj = dfx, factor_tbl = factor_tbl, floor = fl, n_thin = n_thin, n_na_coef = n_na,
       domain = c(min(bm$tb), max(bm$tb)))
}

er_exact_fits <- setNames(lapply(names(durations), fit_ER_exact),      names(durations))
five_min_fits <- setNames(lapply(names(durations), fit_5min_10knot),   names(durations))
```

```{r diurnal-method-compare}
# =============================================================================
#  Same score() shape as this document's earlier A/D/E/F comparisons, now
#  applied to just the two surviving methods. pick_diurnal_winner() (defined
#  above, unchanged) still guards against a non-finite, implausibly
#  near-zero, or blown-up rmse_profile winning by accident.
# =============================================================================
score_diurnal <- function(nm, o, raw_on_grid) {
  a <- o$adj$adjDur; a <- a[is.finite(a) & a > 0]
  gap <- abs(diff(approx(o$factor_tbl$tod_bin, o$factor_tbl$factor, xout = c(0, 1440), rule = 2)$y))
  # rmse_profile restricted to IN-DOMAIN grid points (o$domain, from the
  # fitter). Outside a session-bounded asset's own domain (e.g. NVDA's
  # ~810-1170), both the fitted factor AND raw_on_grid are flat rule=2
  # extrapolation -- comparing two constants over ~75% of the full grid, not
  # measuring fit quality there. Restricting avoids that fabricated agreement.
  in_domain <- o$factor_tbl$tod_bin >= o$domain[1] & o$factor_tbl$tod_bin <= o$domain[2]
  data.table(asset = nm,
             mean_adjDur = round(mean(a), 4), CV_adjDur = round(sd(a) / mean(a), 4),
             ACF1_adj = round(acf(a, lag.max = 1, plot = FALSE)$acf[2], 4),
             LB15_adj = round(Box.test(a, lag = 15, type = "Ljung-Box")$statistic, 1),
             rmse_profile = round(sqrt(mean((o$factor_tbl$factor[in_domain] - raw_on_grid[in_domain])^2)), 4),
             midnight_gap = round(gap, 4),
             raw_scale = round(sd(raw_on_grid[in_domain], na.rm = TRUE), 6))
}

diurnal_compare_tbl <- rbindlist(lapply(names(durations), function(nm) {
  raw_prof <- durations[[nm]][time < SPLIT_TIME][
    , .(m = mean(duration)), by = .(tb = (tod_min_fn(time) %/% 5) * 5)][order(tb)]
  raw_on_grid <- approx(raw_prof$tb, raw_prof$m, xout = DIURNAL_GRID, rule = 2)$y

  rbind(
    cbind(method = "E&R exact (30min bin, hourly knot)", score_diurnal(nm, er_exact_fits[[nm]], raw_on_grid)),
    cbind(method = "5min bin, 10min knot",               score_diurnal(nm, five_min_fits[[nm]], raw_on_grid))
  )
}))

cat("=== Diurnal method comparison: E&R exact (30min bin) vs 5min bin (all 3 assets) ===\n\n")
print(diurnal_compare_tbl)

diurnal_winners <- setNames(character(length(durations)), names(durations))
for (nm in names(durations)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n--- %s ---\n", nm))
  diurnal_winners[nm] <- pick_diurnal_winner(diurnal_compare_tbl[asset == nm])
  cat(sprintf("WINNER: %s\n", diurnal_winners[nm]))
}
if (length(unique(diurnal_winners)) == 1) {
  cat(sprintf("\nAll three assets agree: %s\n", diurnal_winners[1]))
} else {
  cat("\nAssets do NOT agree on a single winner -- each asset uses its own,\n")
  cat("read from diurnal_winners rather than assumed to generalise.\n")
}

# ---- ASSIGN diurnal_fits: FIXED, not re-decided dynamically each run -----
# The comparison above already established, on real data, that 5-min-bin/
# 10-knot wins on rmse_profile for every asset -- that choice is encoded
# directly here rather than re-derived from diurnal_winners on every run
# (which would silently re-open the decision, and potentially flip it, if
# the comparison metrics ever shifted on a future data refresh). All three
# assets are FIXED to 5-min-bin/10-knot.
#
# CAVEAT, not hidden: GBP/USD's 5-min-bin fit has 1 rank-deficient
# coefficient (fit_5min_10knot's own header note -- 143 knots on 280 bins
# pushes close to overfitting FX's own bin count). pick_diurnal_winner()
# only screens rmse_profile for non-finite/near-zero/blow-up values, not
# rank-deficiency, so GBP/USD's win here is on rmse_profile alone -- a real
# additional caveat for that asset specifically, on top of the numeric win.
diurnal_fits <- list(
  "GBP/USD" = five_min_fits[["GBP/USD"]],
  "BTCUSDT" = five_min_fits[["BTCUSDT"]],
  "NVDA"    = five_min_fits[["NVDA"]]
)

cat("\ndiurnal_fits FIXED: all three assets = 5-min-bin/10-knot (the\n")
cat("established winner above, encoded directly, not re-derived at runtime).\n")
cat("GBP/USD's fit has 1 rank-deficient coefficient -- see this chunk's own\n")
cat("caveat above.\n")
cat("split_sets and every get_fit_series() call downstream reads this.\n")
```

```{r diurnal-rmse-significance-test}
# =============================================================================
#  Is the rmse_profile gap between E&R exact (30-min bin) and 5-min bin
#  ACTUALLY significant, or could it be noise? rmse_profile itself is a
#  single aggregate number per method per asset -- no variability attached.
#  But both methods are scored against the SAME raw_on_grid reference at
#  the SAME grid points, so the per-grid-point absolute error is a natural
#  PAIRED comparison: at each in-domain 5-min grid point, err_ER(t) and
#  err_5min(t) are two measurements of the same underlying quantity (how
#  far that method's fitted curve sits from the raw profile at time t),
#  differing only in which method produced the fit -- exactly the setup a
#  paired test is for.
#
#  H0: mean(err_ER - err_5min) = 0 (no genuine difference in fit error).
#  Two tests, not one: a paired t-test (mean difference, assumes
#  approximately normal differences) AND a Wilcoxon signed-rank test
#  (median difference, distribution-free) -- fitted-curve error at a grid
#  point is bounded below by zero and can have a long right tail (a few
#  grid points where one method fits badly), so the Wilcoxon result is the
#  more robust of the two; agreement between both is the strongest reading.
#
#  Sample size here is genuinely small (the number of IN-DOMAIN 5-min grid
#  points -- roughly 280 for GBP/USD/BTCUSDT, ~70 for session-bounded NVDA),
#  unlike every large-n test elsewhere in this document -- a significant
#  p-value here is NOT automatic and actually carries information.
# =============================================================================
sig_test_one <- function(nm) {
  raw_prof <- durations[[nm]][time < SPLIT_TIME][
    , .(m = mean(duration)), by = .(tb = (tod_min_fn(time) %/% 5) * 5)][order(tb)]
  raw_on_grid <- approx(raw_prof$tb, raw_prof$m, xout = DIURNAL_GRID, rule = 2)$y

  o_er <- er_exact_fits[[nm]]; o_5m <- five_min_fits[[nm]]
  # in-domain restricted to BOTH methods' own domains (same reasoning as
  # score_diurnal's own in_domain filter) so neither method contributes a
  # flat-extrapolated point to the comparison.
  in_domain <- DIURNAL_GRID >= max(o_er$domain[1], o_5m$domain[1]) &
               DIURNAL_GRID <= min(o_er$domain[2], o_5m$domain[2])

  err_er <- abs(o_er$factor_tbl$factor[in_domain] - raw_on_grid[in_domain])
  err_5m <- abs(o_5m$factor_tbl$factor[in_domain] - raw_on_grid[in_domain])

  tt <- t.test(err_er, err_5m, paired = TRUE)
  wt <- wilcox.test(err_er, err_5m, paired = TRUE, exact = FALSE)

  data.table(
    asset = nm, n_points = sum(in_domain),
    mean_err_ER = round(mean(err_er), 5), mean_err_5min = round(mean(err_5m), 5),
    mean_diff = round(mean(err_er - err_5m), 5),
    t_stat = round(unname(tt$statistic), 3), t_p = signif(tt$p.value, 3),
    wilcox_V = round(unname(wt$statistic), 1), wilcox_p = signif(wt$p.value, 3),
    verdict = ifelse(tt$p.value < 0.05 & wt$p.value < 0.05,
                      ifelse(mean(err_er - err_5m) > 0, "5-min significantly BETTER", "E&R exact significantly BETTER"),
                      "no significant difference")
  )
}

sig_test_tbl <- rbindlist(lapply(names(durations), sig_test_one))
cat("=== Is the rmse_profile gap (E&R exact vs 5-min bin) statistically significant? ===\n\n")
cat("H0: mean per-grid-point fit error is EQUAL between the two methods.\n")
cat("Paired on the SAME grid points (both methods scored against the same\n")
cat("raw profile), so this is a genuine paired comparison, not an\n")
cat("independent-samples test.\n\n")
print(sig_test_tbl)

cat("\nREADING IT: mean_diff > 0 means E&R exact's error is larger on average,\n")
cat("i.e. 5-min bin fits closer to the raw profile at a typical grid point --\n")
cat("consistent with 5-min bin's lower rmse_profile in diurnal-method-compare.\n")
cat("t_p is the paired t-test p-value (mean difference); wilcox_p is the\n")
cat("Wilcoxon signed-rank p-value (median difference, distribution-free --\n")
cat("the more robust of the two given fit-error's likely right skew).\n")
cat("n_points here is small (tens to a few hundred, NOT the hundreds-of-\n")
cat("thousands-to-millions of every other test in this document), so a\n")
cat("significant p-value is NOT automatic and genuinely means something.\n")

rm(er_exact_fits, five_min_fits); invisible(gc())
```

```{r diurnal-method-plot}
# Before/after, each asset's own winning method -- all three read directly
# from diurnal_fits (5-min-bin/10-knot for every asset, per
# diurnal-method-compare's FIXED assignment above).
plot_dt <- rbindlist(lapply(names(diurnal_fits), function(nm) {
  d <- copy(diurnal_fits[[nm]]$adj); setorder(d, sec, frac_ns)
  d[, hr := (hour(time) * 60 + minute(time)) %/% 30 * 30 / 60]
  rbind(
    d[, .(x = mean(duration), series = "Raw"),      by = hr][, asset := nm],
    d[, .(x = mean(adjDur),   series = "Adjusted"), by = hr][, asset := nm]
  )
}))

ggplot(plot_dt, aes(x = hr, y = x, colour = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +

  facet_wrap(~ asset, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +

       x = "Hour of day (UTC)", y = "Mean duration", colour = NULL) +

rm(plot_dt); invisible(gc())
```

## 9.1 Did the adjustment work?

```{r diurnal-plots}
# =============================================================================
#  Two visual checks:
#    Row 1 -- the fitted factor s(t). Its SHAPE should reconstruct the known
#             session structure of each market from duration data alone. That it
#             does so is independent evidence the estimator functions.
#    Row 2 -- mean duration by time of day, raw vs adjusted. The raw series
#             should show the diurnal wave; the adjusted series should be flat
#             at 1.
#
#  DISPLAY BIN: 30 min. At the factor's native 5-min resolution, bins just
#  outside the excluded FX rollover window carry only ~500-2,000 observations
#  of a heavy-tailed series (CV ~ 2 there), so the raw per-bin sample mean is
#  itself noisy -- invisibly so against the raw series' own huge deterministic
#  hump, but visible once that hump is divided out. That is a sampling
#  artefact of the DISPLAY bin, not evidence the adjustment misbehaves (mean
#  adjDur and the lag-1 ACF both match the documented benchmarks). Coarsening
#  to 30 min pools enough observations to remove it; the factor estimation
#  itself is untouched and still runs on the 5-min grid.
# =============================================================================
diur_check <- rbindlist(lapply(names(diurnal_fits), function(nm) {
  d <- copy(diurnal_fits[[nm]]$adj); setorder(d, sec, frac_ns)
  d[, tod := (hour(time) * 60 + minute(time)) %/% 30 * 30 / 60]
  rbindlist(list(
    d[, .(asset = nm, series = "Raw",      hour = tod, x = duration)],
    d[, .(asset = nm, series = "Adjusted", hour = tod, x = adjDur)]
  ))
}))

prof <- diur_check[, .(mean_dur = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
                   by = .(asset, series, hour)]

# Rollover exclusion applies to FX only; shade it on that facet alone.
rollover_band <- data.table(asset = "GBP/USD",
                            xmin = ROLLOVER_UTC_START / 60,
                            xmax = ROLLOVER_UTC_END / 60)

ggplot(prof, aes(x = hour, y = mean_dur, colour = series)) +
  geom_rect(data = rollover_band, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            fill = "grey85", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~ asset, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 4)) +
  labs(title    = "Intraday duration profile, before and after adjustment",
       subtitle = "Adjusted series should be flat at 1; residual structure = incomplete removal. Grey = excluded FX rollover window.",
       x = "Hour of day (UTC)", y = "Mean duration", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")

# Numeric companion to the plot above: the plot shows flatness, this quantifies it.
cat("=== Adjusted series flatness (should hover near 1) ===\n")
for (nm in names(diurnal_fits)) {
  a  <- diurnal_fits[[nm]]$adj$adjDur
  hr <- hour(diurnal_fits[[nm]]$adj$time)
  bh <- tapply(a, hr, mean)
  cat(sprintf("%-8s: hourly adjusted means %.2f–%.2f, overall %.3f\n",
              nm, min(bh), max(bh), mean(a)))
}

# The fitted factor itself, straight from factor_tbl (not back-derived).
fac <- rbindlist(lapply(names(diurnal_fits), function(nm) {
  ft <- copy(diurnal_fits[[nm]]$factor_tbl)
  ft[, `:=`(hour = tod_bin / 60, asset = nm)][]
}))

ggplot(fac, aes(x = hour, y = factor)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6, colour = "darkorange") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted") +

rm(diur_check, prof); invisible(gc())
```
