```{r diurnal-train-mean}
# =============================================================================
#  TRAIN-ONLY adjusted mean, alongside the whole-series flatness check above.
#
#  The factor s(t) is fit on TRAIN only (each candidate fitter's own
#  time < SPLIT_TIME guard) and then applied to the WHOLE series, so a whole-series
#  adjDur mean that departs from 1 is ambiguous by construction: it could mean
#  the factor itself is wrong, OR it could simply mean the test period's own
#  time-of-day composition/activity differs from what the factor was fit on --
#  an ordinary train/test difference, not an estimator problem.
#
#  This chunk isolates that: mean(adjDur) computed on TRAIN ONLY tests the
#  factor against the exact data it was fit to reproduce.
#    train mean ~= 1            -> the estimator is behaving correctly; a
#                                   whole-series mean away from 1 is a
#                                   train/test composition effect, not a bug.
#    train mean ALSO away from 1 -> the factor/smoothing itself needs a closer
#                                   look (factor_tbl directly), not just the
#                                   downstream mean.
#
#  NOT the primary validation criterion either way -- see the note below.
# =============================================================================
train_mean <- rbindlist(lapply(names(diurnal_fits), function(nm) {
  o <- diurnal_fits[[nm]]
  train_adj <- o$adj[time < SPLIT_TIME, adjDur]
  whole_adj <- o$adj$adjDur
  data.table(asset            = nm,
             train_mean_adj   = round(mean(train_adj), 4),
             whole_mean_adj   = round(mean(whole_adj), 4),
             n_train          = length(train_adj))
}))

cat("=== Adjusted-duration mean: TRAIN ONLY vs WHOLE SERIES ===\n\n")
print(train_mean)

cat("\nREADING IT: train_mean_adj near 1 with whole_mean_adj further off ==\n")
cat("train/test composition difference, not an estimator problem -- the\n")
cat("factor is doing exactly what it was fit to do on the data it was fit on.\n")
cat("train_mean_adj ALSO away from 1 would instead point at the factor/\n")
cat("smoothing itself (factor_tbl), a genuinely different diagnosis.\n\n")
cat("Neither number is the primary validation criterion, though. What matters\n")
cat("more: does the adjustment reduce the TIME-OF-DAY pattern (Section 9.1's\n")
cat("profile plot above), and does meaningful serial dependence survive it\n")
cat("(Section 9.2's before/after ACF/Ljung-Box)? A mean pinned exactly to 1\n")
cat("is neither necessary nor sufficient for the adjustment to have worked.\n")

rm(train_mean); invisible(gc())
```

## 9.2 Before vs after seasonal adjustment — ACF

```{r diurnal-acf-comparison}
# =============================================================================
#  THE DECISIVE CHECK on the adjustment, stated directly in terms of what it
#  is FOR: ACF(x_t) before adjustment against ACF(x_t^adj) after.
#
#  The adjustment should remove the PREDICTABLE intraday pattern -- the
#  deterministic diurnal wave documented in Sections 7.8/7.11 -- WITHOUT
#  removing the genuine serial dependence ACD is built to capture. Two ways
#  this could go wrong, both visible here:
#    - adjustment does nothing: ACF(adj) ~= ACF(raw), no flattening at all
#    - adjustment over-corrects: ACF(adj) collapses toward zero at EVERY lag,
#      including the short lags where genuine duration clustering lives, not
#      just the daily-cycle lags the diurnal wave itself would produce
#
#  What should actually happen: ACF(adj) sits BELOW ACF(raw) at the lags
#  dominated by the deterministic cycle, while remaining clearly positive and
#  slowly decaying at short lags -- the clustering signal survives because it
#  is a genuinely different source of dependence from the time-of-day effect.
# =============================================================================
acf_before_after <- rbindlist(lapply(names(diurnal_fits), function(nm) {
  d <- diurnal_fits[[nm]]$adj
  raw <- d$duration; adj <- d$adjDur
  if (length(raw) > 2e6) { raw <- raw[1:2e6]; adj <- adj[1:2e6] }  # PLOT ONLY, same cap as Section 7.5/7.7
  a_raw <- acf(raw, lag.max = 100, plot = FALSE)
  a_adj <- acf(adj, lag.max = 100, plot = FALSE)
  rbindlist(list(
    data.table(asset = nm, series = "Before (raw x_t)",     lag = as.integer(a_raw$lag), acf = as.numeric(a_raw$acf)),
    data.table(asset = nm, series = "After (adjusted x_t)", lag = as.integer(a_adj$lag), acf = as.numeric(a_adj$acf))
  ))
}))

ggplot(acf_before_after, aes(x = lag, y = acf, fill = series)) +
  geom_col(position = "identity", alpha = 0.6, width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ asset, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Before (raw x_t)" = "steelblue", "After (adjusted x_t)" = "darkorange")) +
  labs(title    = "ACF before vs after diurnal adjustment",
       subtitle = "Adjustment should remove the deterministic cycle while leaving short-lag clustering intact",
       x = "Lag", y = "ACF", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")

# Numeric companion: total dependence removed (whole-lag-range) vs retained at
# the shortest lags (where genuine clustering, not the diurnal cycle, lives).
acf_summary_ba <- rbindlist(lapply(names(diurnal_fits), function(nm) {
  d <- diurnal_fits[[nm]]$adj
  raw <- d$duration; adj <- d$adjDur
  if (length(raw) > 2e6) { raw <- raw[1:2e6]; adj <- adj[1:2e6] }
  lb_raw_ba <- Box.test(raw, lag = LB_LAGS, type = "Ljung-Box")
  lb_adj_ba <- Box.test(adj, lag = LB_LAGS, type = "Ljung-Box")
  data.table(asset = nm,
             acf1_before = round(acf(raw, lag.max = 1, plot = FALSE)$acf[2], 4),
             acf1_after  = round(acf(adj, lag.max = 1, plot = FALSE)$acf[2], 4),
             LB_before   = round(unname(lb_raw_ba$statistic), 1),
             LB_after    = round(unname(lb_adj_ba$statistic), 1))
}))
cat("=== Lag-1 ACF and Ljung-Box, before vs after adjustment ===\n\n")
print(acf_summary_ba)
cat("\nLB_after still far exceeding the chi-sq critical value (LB_CRIT, Section\n")
cat("1.2) alongside a substantially unchanged lag-1 ACF is the target reading:\n")
cat("the deterministic cycle is gone, the genuine clustering ACD targets is not.\n")

rm(acf_before_after, acf_summary_ba); invisible(gc())
```

## 9.3 Attach diurnal adjustment to the pre-existing train/test split

```{r split-attach-adjdur}
# =============================================================================
#  split_sets was DEFINED in `split` (Section 8), on RAW durations, before
#  any diurnal fitting -- this chunk enriches the SAME object with adjDur/
#  factor now that diurnal_fits exists, using the identical time<SPLIT_TIME
#  boundary already fixed there. Same train/test row partition throughout;
#  this only adds columns, it never re-decides which rows belong to which set.
# =============================================================================
for (nm in names(split_sets)) {
  adj <- diurnal_fits[[nm]]$adj
  setorder(adj, sec, frac_ns)
  split_sets[[nm]]$train <- adj[time <  SPLIT_TIME]
  split_sets[[nm]]$test  <- adj[time >= SPLIT_TIME & time < TEST_END]
}

split_summary_adj <- rbindlist(lapply(names(split_sets), function(nm) {
  tr <- split_sets[[nm]]$train
  te <- split_sets[[nm]]$test
  data.table(asset = nm,
             mean_adj_train = round(mean(tr$adjDur), 4),
             mean_adj_test  = round(mean(te$adjDur), 4),
             pct_change     = round(100 * (mean(te$adjDur) / mean(tr$adjDur) - 1), 1))
}))
print(split_summary_adj)

cat("\nThe change in mean adjusted duration between periods reflects a change in\n")
cat("the LEVEL of activity, not a seasonal effect the factor failed to capture,\n")
cat("since the factor is a function of time of day alone.\n")

# ---- Helper: the exact series every model is fitted on -----------------------
# Contiguous block in chronological order, taken from the TRAIN set. Defined
# once so that every specification on the ladder sees identical data --
# comparability across the grid requires it.
get_fit_series <- function(nm, n = FIT_N) {
  x <- head(split_sets[[nm]]$train$adjDur, n)
  x[is.finite(x) & x > 0]
}

# ---- Cache for quickstart-model-inputs (Section 1.3) -----------------------
# Same atomic-write pattern as save_model_progress: write to a temp file,
# rename only once complete, so a crash mid-write never corrupts the real
# cache. Saved every time this chunk runs (fresh data, current diurnal
# winner), so a fresh session's quickstart chunk always reflects the last
# full run, not a stale one.
.split_tmp <- paste0(SPLIT_CACHE_FILE, ".tmp", Sys.getpid())
saveRDS(list(split_sets = split_sets, diurnal_fits = diurnal_fits,
             diurnal_winners = if (exists("diurnal_winners", inherits = FALSE)) diurnal_winners else NULL),.split_tmp)
file.rename(.split_tmp, SPLIT_CACHE_FILE)
SPLIT_CACHED <- TRUE
cat(sprintf("\n[saved split_sets/diurnal_fits/diurnal_winners -> %s]\n", SPLIT_CACHE_FILE))
cat("Future fresh sessions: run only the quickstart-model-inputs chunk\n")
cat("(Section 1.3) to skip straight to model fitting.\n")
rm(.split_tmp)
```


# 3. Model Specifications and Results

Five specifications in order of increasing generality. Each relaxes a
restriction imposed by its predecessor, and each is rejected on stated grounds
before the next is introduced.

| Rung | Specification | Relaxes | Rejected on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Homogeneous Poisson | — | CV ≠ 1 |
| 2 | Inhomogeneous Poisson | constant rate | Ljung–Box survives adjustment |
| 3 | ARMA(1,1) | independence | negative durations; heteroskedastic residuals |
| 4 | EACD(1,1) | additive Gaussian errors | excess dispersion |
| 5 | WACD(1,1) | constant hazard | *(retained; see caveats)* |

```{r model-cache-check}
# =============================================================================
#  If model_fits_cache.rds exists, load every fitted-model object it contains
#  straight into the global environment and SKIP every expensive fitting loop
#  from here through the end of Section 12 -- each is individually gated on
#  `!MODELS_CACHED` below. Delete the file to force a full refit.
# =============================================================================
if (MODELS_CACHED) {
  # GUARDED, not a bare readRDS(): a corrupted cache file (e.g. from a crash
  # mid-write -- see save_model_progress()'s own atomic-write fix below,
  # added after exactly this happened) would otherwise throw an UNCAUGHT
  # error here and hard-stop the entire document at the very first chunk
  # that touches the cache -- blocking every later chunk, including ones
  # that don't even need the corrupted objects. Falls back to "no cache,
  # refit everything" instead, same as a genuinely missing file, rather
  # than bricking the whole session.
  cached_models <- tryCatch(readRDS(MODEL_CACHE_FILE), error = function(e) {
    cat(sprintf("MODEL CACHE CORRUPTED (%s): %s\n", MODEL_CACHE_FILE, conditionMessage(e)))
    cat("Falling back to NO CACHE -- every model below will refit from scratch.\n")
    cat("Move/rename the corrupted file once you can, so a future valid save\n")
    cat("doesn't get blocked trying to read-merge-write against a broken one.\n")
    NULL
  })
  if (!is.null(cached_models)) {
    list2env(cached_models, envir = .GlobalEnv)
    cat(sprintf("Loaded %d cached model-fit objects from %s -- skipping all refitting in Sections 10-12.\n",
                length(cached_models), MODEL_CACHE_FILE))
    cat("(delete this file and re-knit to force every model to refit)\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("No model cache found -- Sections 10-12 will fit every model in full (slow).\n")
}

# =============================================================================
#  INCREMENTAL save -- called at the end of EVERY fitting chunk below, not
#  just once at the very end of Section 12. Reads whatever is already on
#  disk, updates/adds only the object(s) just fitted, and writes the whole
#  thing back out. This means a crash/error in ANY later chunk (e.g. a
#  plotting bug three chunks after the last model fit) no longer loses every
#  model fitted before it -- each is safe on disk the moment its own chunk
#  finishes, so re-knitting after a downstream fix reloads all of them
#  instead of refitting from scratch.
# =============================================================================
save_model_progress <- function(...) {
  new_objs <- list(...)

  # FAIL LOUDLY if an existing cache can't be read, rather than silently
  # falling back to an empty list -- that would overwrite the WHOLE cache
  # with only the objects from THIS call, discarding every other model
  # already saved. A missing file is fine (genuinely nothing to merge); a
  # present-but-unreadable one is not, and must stop here, not proceed.
  existing <- if (file.exists(MODEL_CACHE_FILE)) {
    tryCatch(readRDS(MODEL_CACHE_FILE), error = function(e)
      stop(sprintf(
        "save_model_progress: %s exists but cannot be read (%s). Refusing to\n",
        MODEL_CACHE_FILE, conditionMessage(e)),
        "overwrite it with only the object(s) from this call -- that would\n",
        "silently discard every other cached model. Move the corrupted file\n",
        "aside by hand first, then re-run.", call. = FALSE))
  } else list()
  existing[names(new_objs)] <- new_objs

  # ATOMIC WRITE: write to a temp file in the SAME directory (so the rename
  # below is on one filesystem, hence atomic), then rename over the real
  # cache file only once the write has FULLY succeeded. A crash/kill mid-
  # write now truncates only the disposable temp file -- the real cache
  # file is never touched until a complete, valid replacement exists. This
  # is the direct fix for a real corruption this document hit: an
  # interrupted saveRDS() (out-of-memory kill mid-fit) left a truncated
  # gzip stream in model_fits_cache.rds itself, unrecoverable, blocking
  # every subsequent read of it.
  tmp <- paste0(MODEL_CACHE_FILE, ".tmp", Sys.getpid())
  saveRDS(existing, tmp)
  ok <- file.rename(tmp, MODEL_CACHE_FILE)
  if (!ok) { file.remove(tmp); stop("save_model_progress: atomic rename failed -- see ", tmp) }
  cat(sprintf("  [saved %s -> %s]\n", paste(names(new_objs), collapse = ", "), MODEL_CACHE_FILE))
}

# =============================================================================
#  fit_ready(): gate on COMPLETENESS, not just presence. `exists("X_fits")`
#  alone would treat an empty/partial list -- e.g. one saved by a run where
#  every asset's fit failed and got silently dropped (the [[nm]]<-NULL bug
#  fixed throughout this ladder) -- as "already done" and skip refitting it
#  forever. Requires every named asset to actually be a key in the list;
#  a key mapping to a genuine NULL (real, recorded convergence failure) still
#  counts as present -- only a MISSING key or a totally empty list fails this.
# =============================================================================
fit_ready <- function(varname, assets = names(split_sets)) {
  exists(varname, inherits = FALSE) &&
    length(get(varname, inherits = FALSE)) > 0 &&
    all(assets %in% names(get(varname, inherits = FALSE)))
}

# goodnessOfFit is a data.frame with NAMED rows -- index by name, not
# position. Defined here (not just at first use in eacd-fit) so any chunk
# that reads an already-fitted model's AIC/BIC/LogLikelihood -- including
# ones that come BEFORE eacd-fit is reached if chunks are run out of order --
# doesn't hit "could not find function gof".
gof <- function(f, what) f$goodnessOfFit[what, "value"]

# AR(1)-form recursion y_i = c_i + phi*y_{i-1}, y_1 = y0 -- computed via
# stats::filter(..., method="recursive"), a compiled-C linear filter, NOT a
# per-element R loop (verified to reproduce a hand-written for-loop exactly,
# max abs diff = 0 at n=500,000). Shared by every hand-rolled (non-ACDm)
# model on this ladder -- BS-ACD and Zero-Inflated ACD both need an
# ACD-style linear recursion inside a custom nlminb likelihood, where
# ACDm's compiled acdFit() isn't available. FIT_N=Inf means that recursion
# runs on the FULL 14-day training window (hundreds of thousands to millions
# of rows for BTC/NVDA) on EVERY optimiser evaluation, so keeping it out of
# R-level loops matters here in a way it doesn't for the cheap helpers above.
ar1_recursion <- function(c_rest, phi, y0) {
  c(y0, as.numeric(stats::filter(c_rest, filter = phi, method = "recursive", init = y0)))
}

# =============================================================================
#  FORMAL "how far from 1 is far" statistics for residual location, replacing
#  eyeballing |mean_resid - 1| with an actual hypothesis test -- same idea as
#  disp_stat_Exp1 (which already does this for the SECOND moment, Var(eps)=1,
#  via a Z-stat), now for the FIRST moment, E[eps]=1. Reported as a Z-stat,
#  not a t-stat: the t-distribution's own reason to differ from the normal is
#  small-sample correction (conventionally needed below n~30), and every
#  sample size in this document is in the hundreds of thousands to millions,
#  where a t(n-1) critical value is numerically indistinguishable from
#  qnorm(0.975)=1.96 -- so this is reported and read as the large-sample Z
#  it actually is.
#
#  NOT used to replace any existing CORRUPTED/trustworthy GATE (fit_health,
#  wacd_check$trustworthy) -- at this document's sample sizes (hundreds of
#  thousands to millions of observations per asset), |z|>1.96 would reject
#  for almost ANY nonzero deviation, the same power problem already
#  identified for Ljung-Box at this scale, and would flag even the clean
#  reference case (GBP/USD) as "corrupted". Reported ALONGSIDE the existing
#  0.05-magnitude gate as an additional rigor number, not a replacement for
#  it: the gate answers "is this deviation big enough to matter" (practical
#  significance, the right question for deciding whether to trust a fit);
#  the z-stat answers "is this deviation distinguishable from pure noise"
#  (statistical significance, which is a different, less useful question at
#  this n).
# =============================================================================
resid_mean_z <- function(e, mu = 1) {
  e <- e[is.finite(e)]; n <- length(e)
  if (n < 2) return(NA_real_)
  (mean(e) - mu) / (sd(e) / sqrt(n))
}

# Median-target analogue (BS-ACD's own natural check, not the mean): a sign
# test for H0: median=1 -- count of observations above 1 is Binomial(n, 0.5)
# under H0, normal-approximated the same way disp_test's own Z is built.
resid_median_z <- function(ratio) {
  ratio <- ratio[is.finite(ratio)]; n <- length(ratio)
  if (n < 2) return(NA_real_)
  n_above <- sum(ratio > 1)
  (n_above - n / 2) / sqrt(n / 4)
}

# =============================================================================
#  SURVIVOR-FUNCTION DIAGNOSTIC BUILDER (E&R Figure 5/8 analogue) -- the exact
#  visual form of the KS D-statistic: -log S(x) vs x is a straight 45-degree
#  line for a true Exp(1); bending above it is the same tail-heaviness KS_D
#  reports as a single number, just seen directly. Generalized (fits_list,
#  resid_fn, model_label) so it can be called once per model/order instead of
#  rewriting the empirical-survivor construction each time survivor-curve
#  (EACD vs WACD) needs a wider comparison -- e.g. across all four orders.
# =============================================================================
exp_resid <- function(f) {
  e <- as.numeric(f$residuals); e[is.finite(e) & e > 0]
}

build_survivor_dt <- function(fits_list, resid_fn, model_label, tail_quantile = 0.50, n_pts = 2000) {
  rbindlist(lapply(names(fits_list), function(nm) {
    f <- fits_list[[nm]]
    if (is.null(f)) return(NULL)
    e <- sort(resid_fn(f))
    n <- length(e)
    if (n < 20) return(NULL)
    S    <- 1 - (seq_len(n) - 0.5) / n
    keep <- e > quantile(e, tail_quantile)
    idx  <- which(keep)
    idx  <- idx[seq(1, length(idx), length.out = min(n_pts, length(idx)))]
    data.table(asset = nm, model = model_label, x = e[idx], neglogS = -log(S[idx]))
  }))
}
```

## 3.1 The Homogeneous Poisson Process

```{r poisson-calibrate}

#  H0: after the deterministic daily pattern is removed, what remains arrives as
#      a homogeneous Poisson process with constant intensity lambda. Then the
#      ADJUSTED durations are iid Exp(lambda), and E[x] = sd(x) = 1/lambda, so
#      CV = 1.
#
#  WHY ADJUSTED, NOT RAW DURATIONS. The models relying on the stationary
#  properties of a homogeneous Poisson process are applied to diurnally adjusted
#  durations, since raw durations carry a systematic time-of-day pattern that
#  must first be divided out by the seasonality factor (Bauwens & Hautsch 2006;
#  and the preprocessing-first principle set out in Section 8). Fitting on
#  adjusted durations also makes the rejection STRONGER: overdispersion that
#  survives seasonal adjustment cannot be attributed to seasonality.
#
#  CALIBRATE -> SIMULATE -> COMPARE. Estimating lambda and reporting that the
#  data disagree is not enough; the point is to show that data SIMULATED from
#  the fitted model does not resemble the observed (adjusted) series. That
#  establishes the discrepancy as a property of the SPECIFICATION, not the
#  estimator.

set.seed(5872)

# TRAIN-only (get_fit_series(), the same helper/window every later rung of
# the ladder uses) -- previously this read diurnal_fits[[nm]]$adj$adjDur,
# the FULL pre-split sample (train+test combined), so "n" here didn't match
# any other rung's n and lambda_hat was calibrated on data the later ladder
# never sees as a unit. Fixed so rung 1 is evaluated on exactly the same
# window as EACD/WACD/Log-ACD/etc.
pois_cal <- rbindlist(lapply(names(diurnal_fits), function(nm) {
  d <- get_fit_series(nm, FIT_N)
  data.table(
    asset      = nm,
    n          = length(d),
    lambda_hat = 1 / mean(d),
    E_tau_mean = mean(d),        # = 1/lambda_hat by construction; ~1 for adjusted
    median_s   = median(d),
    CV_real    = sd(d) / mean(d)
  )
}))
cat("=== (1) CALIBRATE lambda per asset (ADJUSTED durations, TRAIN only) ===\n\n")
print(pois_cal)
```

```{r poisson-simulate}
cat("\n=== (2) SIMULATE Exp(lambda_hat) AND COMPARE (ADJUSTED durations, TRAIN only) ===\n\n")

pois_compare <- rbindlist(lapply(names(diurnal_fits), function(nm) {
  d   <- get_fit_series(nm, FIT_N)   # TRAIN only -- matches pois_cal/get_fit_series
  sim <- rexp(length(d), rate = 1 / mean(d))
  data.table(
    asset     = nm,
    stat      = c("mean", "median", "sd", "CV", "% < 1ms", "P99"),
    observed  = c(mean(d), median(d), sd(d), sd(d) / mean(d),
                  100 * mean(d < 0.001), quantile(d, 0.99)),
    simulated = c(mean(sim), median(sim), sd(sim), sd(sim) / mean(sim),
                  100 * mean(sim < 0.001), quantile(sim, 0.99))
  )
}))
print(pois_compare)

cat("\nREADING IT: the exponential reproduces the MEAN by construction, since\n")
cat("lambda_hat was chosen to match it. It reproduces nothing else.\n")
cat("  - the simulated CV is close to 1 (up to sampling variation), as the\n")
cat("    exponential requires; the observed CV is far above it\n")
cat("  - the simulated median sits close to the simulated mean; the observed\n")
cat("    median is a fraction of the observed mean -- right-skew the\n")
cat("    exponential cannot generate\n")
cat("  - the sub-millisecond mass and the 99th percentile are both understated\n")
cat("    by the exponential\n")
```

```{r poisson-dispersion-test}
# =============================================================================
#  THE FORMAL THRESHOLD -- answering "how far from 1 is far enough?"
#
#  Reporting CV = 2.12 and asserting it is "far from 1" is not a test: with a
#  different sample size the same distance could be noise or signal. The
#  excess-dispersion statistic converts the distance into standard-error units,
#  so the sample size decides the threshold rather than the eye.
#
#  Under H0 (adjusted durations iid Exp(1)):
#      Z = sqrt(n/4) * (CV^2 - 1)   ~  N(0,1)  asymptotically.
#  |Z| > 1.96 rejects equidispersion at the 5% level. The statistic scales the
#  raw departure (CV^2 - 1) by sqrt(n/4), so a tiny departure is significant at
#  large n and a large one at small n -- which is exactly the point: the
#  criterion is not a fixed CV value but a distance measured in standard errors.
#
#  ⚠ THE DIVISOR IS 4, NOT 2. By the delta method on g(mu1,mu2) = mu2/mu1^2 - 1
#  (population CV^2 - 1, mu1=E[X], mu2=E[X^2]) evaluated at the Exp(1) moments
#  (mu1=1, mu2=2, mu3=6, mu4=24), Var(CV^2_hat - 1) -> 4/n, not 2/n. Verified
#  both analytically and by direct Monte Carlo simulation (empirical sd of
#  CV^2-1 across 15,000-20,000 replications at several n matched sqrt(4/n) to
#  three decimal places, and disagreed with sqrt(2/n) by a consistent factor of
#  sqrt(2)). An earlier version of this statistic used sqrt(n/2), which
#  overstated every Z here by a factor of sqrt(2) -- it never changed the
#  REJECT/not-rejected conclusion at these sample sizes, but the printed Z
#  values were wrong.
#
#  ⚠ At n in the millions the test rejects almost any departure, so a bare
#    rejection is not the finding. The MAGNITUDE of the departure (CV^2 - 1) is
#    what makes the rejection substantive rather than a large-sample artefact.
#    Both are reported below.
# =============================================================================
disp_test <- rbindlist(lapply(names(diurnal_fits), function(nm) {
  d  <- get_fit_series(nm, FIT_N)   # TRAIN only -- matches pois_cal/pois_compare
  n  <- length(d)
  cv <- sd(d) / mean(d)
  Z  <- sqrt(n / 4) * (cv^2 - 1)
  data.table(
    asset      = nm,
    n          = n,
    CV         = round(cv, 4),
    excess     = round(cv^2 - 1, 3),          # magnitude of departure from Poisson
    Z_stat     = round(Z, 1),                 # departure in standard errors
    crit_5pct  = 1.96,
    reject     = ifelse(abs(Z) > 1.96, "REJECT Poisson", "not rejected")
  )
}))
print(disp_test)

cat("\nREADING IT:\n")
cat("  Z is the distance of the observed dispersion from the Poisson value,\n")
cat("  measured in standard errors. |Z| > 1.96 rejects at 5%. All three assets\n")
cat("  reject by an enormous margin -- but the DECISIVE quantity is `excess`\n")
cat("  (CV^2 - 1): the observed dispersion is 2-6x the Poisson value, a\n")
cat("  departure of large magnitude, not a marginal one inflated by sample\n")
cat("  size. The rejection is therefore substantive, not a large-n artefact.\n")
```

```{r poisson-plot-dist}
# =============================================================================
#  Observed (adjusted) durations vs durations simulated from the fitted
#  homogeneous Poisson, Exp(lambda_hat). Log x-axis is essential: the observed
#  series spans ~6 orders of magnitude, the exponential ~1.5.
#
#  Reads ADJUSTED durations, TRAIN only, to match the calibrate/simulate/test
#  chunks (and every later rung of the ladder).
#  BTC is capped at 2e6 points FOR THE PLOT ONLY (10M bars render nothing
#  useful); the statistics and the test always use the full TRAIN series.
#
#  What the reader should see: the exponential (simulated) is a single smooth
#  hump; the observed series is right-shifted in its bulk, far heavier in both
#  the near-zero mass and the tail, and for NVDA visibly bimodal -- none of
#  which the exponential can reproduce.
# =============================================================================
plot_dat <- rbindlist(lapply(names(diurnal_fits), function(nm) {
  d <- get_fit_series(nm, FIT_N)   # TRAIN only
  if (length(d) > 2e6) d <- d[1:2e6]                 # plot cap only
  s <- rexp(length(d), rate = 1 / mean(d))
  rbindlist(list(
    data.table(asset = nm, source = "Observed (adjusted)",  duration = d),
    data.table(asset = nm, source = "Simulated Exp(lambda)", duration = s)
  ))
}))

ggplot(plot_dat, aes(x = duration, fill = source)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 60,
                 position = "identity", alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ asset, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(title    = "Observed adjusted durations vs fitted homogeneous Poisson",
       subtitle = "Exp(lambda-hat) matches the mean but not the shape; log x-axis, density scale",
       x = "Adjusted duration (log scale)", y = "Density", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")

rm(plot_dat); invisible(gc())
```


**Verdict — rung 1.** The simulated homogeneous Poisson process matches the
baseline mean durations, but the observed coefficients of variation
substantially exceed the theoretical requirement of unity, and the Fano factor
confirms this on binned counts. This is strong evidence that arrivals do not
occur at a constant, memoryless rate. The homogeneous Poisson process is
rejected, motivating a specification that at least admits a time-varying
intensity.


## Rung 3 — ARMA(1,1)

```{r arma-fit}
# =============================================================================
#  E&R eq.(17): the ACD(1,1) recursion IS an ARMA(1,1) in durations.
#
#  Writing psi_i for the conditional expectation and defining
#      eta_i = x_i - psi_i          (a martingale difference by construction)
#  substitution into the ACD recursion yields
#      x_i = omega + (alpha+beta) x_{i-1} - beta*eta_{i-1} + eta_i
#
#  which has the algebraic form of an ARMA(1,1) with
#      phi = alpha + beta,     theta = -beta
#
#  So an ARMA(1,1) fit delivers estimates of the ACD parameters WITHOUT any
#  specialised estimation, and phi is directly interpretable as persistence.
#  This makes ARMA the natural "simple case" and the honest benchmark ACD must
#  beat.
#
#  THE DIFFERENCE lies in the innovation. ARMA assumes e_i Gaussian, additive,
#  and of constant variance. The ACD innovation satisfies eta_i = psi_i(eps_i-1),
#  so its variance is psi_i^2 * Var(eps) -- which DEPENDS ON THE CONDITIONAL
#  MEAN. It is also skewed and bounded below by -psi_i. ARMA is therefore a
#  Gaussian approximation to a process whose innovations are neither Gaussian
#  nor homoskedastic. Two consequences are testable, and both are tested below.
#
#  Estimation by conditional sum of squares: asymptotically equivalent to full
#  ML and substantially faster at these sample sizes.
# =============================================================================
if (!fit_ready("arma_fits")) {
arma_fits <- list()

for (nm in names(split_sets)) {
  x <- get_fit_series(nm, ARMA_N)
  cat(sprintf("=== ARMA(1,1): %-8s (n = %s) ===\n",
              nm, format(length(x), big.mark = ",")))
  arma_fits[[nm]] <- arima(x, order = c(1, 0, 1),
                           include.mean = TRUE, method = "CSS")
}
save_model_progress(arma_fits = arma_fits)
}

arma_results <- rbindlist(lapply(names(arma_fits), function(nm) {
  fit <- arma_fits[[nm]]
  ar1 <- unname(coef(fit)["ar1"])
  ma1 <- unname(coef(fit)["ma1"])

  # Map ARMA(1,1) -> implied ACD(1,1) via E&R eq.(17):
  #   phi   = alpha + beta   (persistence)
  #   theta = -beta          => beta = -theta, alpha = phi - beta
  beta_impl  <- -ma1
  alpha_impl <- ar1 - beta_impl

  data.table(
    asset         = nm,
    n_used        = ARMA_N,
    phi           = round(ar1, 4),
    theta         = round(ma1, 4),
    persistence   = round(ar1, 4),          # = alpha + beta
    alpha_implied = round(alpha_impl, 4),
    beta_implied  = round(beta_impl, 4),
    sigma2        = round(fit$sigma2, 4),
    intercept     = round(unname(coef(fit)["intercept"]), 4)
  )
}))

cat("\n=== ARMA(1,1) ON ADJUSTED DURATIONS (train, first 100k) ===\n\n")
print(arma_results)

cat("\nREADING IT: phi lies close to unity on all three assets. Since phi\n")
cat("estimates alpha+beta, this is a finding of near-unit persistence obtained\n")
cat("WITHOUT any specialised estimation. The implied beta is large (0.86-0.97)\n")
cat("and the implied alpha small (0.02-0.11): the conditional mean responds\n")
cat("only weakly to any individual duration but retains almost all of its\n")
cat("previous value, which is what produces persistence of this magnitude.\n")
```

```{r arma-simulate}
# =============================================================================
#  ⚠ THE POINT OF THIS CHUNK.
#
#  The fitted ARMA assumes e_i ~ N(0, sigma^2) -- ADDITIVE and GAUSSIAN, hence
#  unbounded below. Durations are POSITIVE and multiplicative. Simulating from
#  the fitted model therefore generates NEGATIVE durations, which are
#  economically impossible.
#
#  That is not a broken simulation. It is the misspecification made VISIBLE,
#  and it is the strongest single argument in the dissertation for why ACD is
#  needed rather than standard time-series machinery.
#
#  No choice of coefficients avoids it: the difficulty lies in the FORM of the
#  specification, not in the values of its parameters. The fitted intercept is
#  close to unity and the fitted innovation sd close to two, so a normal
#  distribution with these parameters places a substantial part of its mass
#  below zero.
#
#  All three phi < 1, so unlike the EACD case every path here IS stationary and
#  a full comparison is well defined.
# =============================================================================
set.seed(5872)

arma_sim <- rbindlist(lapply(names(arma_fits), function(nm) {

  fit  <- arma_fits[[nm]]
  real <- get_fit_series(nm, ARMA_N)

  sim <- as.numeric(arima.sim(
    n     = SIM_N,
    model = list(ar = unname(coef(fit)["ar1"]), ma = unname(coef(fit)["ma1"])),
    sd    = sqrt(fit$sigma2))) + unname(coef(fit)["intercept"])

  ac_r <- acf(real, lag.max = max(ACF_LAGS), plot = FALSE)$acf[ACF_LAGS + 1]
  ac_s <- acf(sim,  lag.max = max(ACF_LAGS), plot = FALSE)$acf[ACF_LAGS + 1]

  data.table(
    asset     = nm,
    phi       = round(unname(coef(fit)["ar1"]), 4),
    stat      = c("mean", "dispersion", "ACF(1)", "ACF(10)", "% negative"),
    observed  = round(c(mean(real), sd(real)/mean(real), ac_r[1], ac_r[2], 0), 4),
    simulated = round(c(mean(sim),  sd(sim)/mean(sim),   ac_s[1], ac_s[2],
                        100 * mean(sim < 0)), 4)
  )
}))

cat("=== ARMA(1,1): SIMULATED against OBSERVED (n_sim =",
    format(SIM_N, big.mark = ","), ") ===\n\n")
print(arma_sim)

cat("\nREADING IT: on the first four statistics the agreement is CLOSE -- mean,\n")
cat("dispersion and both autocorrelations lie within a few per cent for every\n")
cat("asset. Judged on those alone the specification would appear adequate.\n")
cat("The final row establishes that it is not: between a quarter and a third of\n")
cat("simulated durations are negative. A process assigning that much\n")
cat("probability mass below zero cannot have generated waiting times, whatever\n")
cat("its moments.\n")
```

```{r arma-plot}
# Distributional shape, positives only. Restricting to x > 0 is ITSELF the
# point: the comparison is only definable on the sub-sample where ARMA did not
# violate its own support.
set.seed(5872)
PLOT_N <- 50000L

sim_dat <- rbindlist(lapply(names(arma_fits), function(nm) {
  fit  <- arma_fits[[nm]]
  real <- get_fit_series(nm, ARMA_N)
  sim  <- as.numeric(arima.sim(
    n     = length(real),
    model = list(ar = unname(coef(fit)["ar1"]), ma = unname(coef(fit)["ma1"])),
    sd    = sqrt(fit$sigma2))) + unname(coef(fit)["intercept"])

  rbindlist(list(
    data.table(asset = nm, source = "Observed",             x = head(real, PLOT_N)),
    data.table(asset = nm, source = "Simulated ARMA(1,1)",  x = head(sim,  PLOT_N))
  ))
}))

ggplot(sim_dat[x > 0], aes(x = x, fill = source)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, position = "identity", alpha = 0.55) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ asset, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title    = "Distributional shape, positive values only",
       subtitle = "Observed durations are right-skewed with heavy tails; the Gaussian innovation is symmetric",
       x = "Adjusted duration (log scale)", y = "Count", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")

rm(sim_dat); invisible(gc())
```

```{r arma-residuals}
# =============================================================================
#  ARMA RESIDUAL DIAGNOSTICS.
#
#  ⚠ DIFFERENT RESIDUALS FROM ACD. Do not reuse the ACD tests uncritically:
#      ACD:  eps_hat = x_i / psi_hat_i    -- MULTIPLICATIVE, should be Exp(1)
#      ARMA: e_hat   = x_i - x_hat_i      -- ADDITIVE,       should be N(0,s^2)
#  The excess-dispersion test therefore has NO ARMA analogue. The equivalent
#  question here is whether the residuals are NORMAL -- which is exactly the
#  assumption that produced the negative simulated durations above.
#
#  THREE TESTS:
#    1. Ljung-Box(15) on e_hat    -> did ARMA absorb the serial dependence?
#    2. Ljung-Box(15) on e_hat^2  -> is dependence left in the VARIANCE?
#       This is the one that matters. ARMA assumes homoskedastic errors;
#       durations are heteroskedastic, with Var(eta_i) = psi_i^2 Var(eps). If
#       LB on squares greatly exceeds LB on levels, ARMA cleaned the mean but
#       not the variance -- precisely the gap the multiplicative form closes.
#    3. Skewness / Jarque-Bera    -> are the residuals actually Gaussian?
# =============================================================================
arma_resid <- rbindlist(lapply(names(arma_fits), function(nm) {

  fit <- arma_fits[[nm]]
  x   <- get_fit_series(nm, ARMA_N)
  e   <- as.numeric(residuals(fit))
  e   <- e[is.finite(e)]
  n   <- length(e)

  z    <- (e - mean(e)) / sd(e)
  skew <- mean(z^3)
  kurt <- mean(z^4)                        # 3 under normality
  jb   <- n / 6 * (skew^2 + (kurt - 3)^2 / 4)   # ~ chi-sq(2), crit 5.99

  data.table(
    asset       = nm,
    n           = n,
    LB_before   = round(Box.test(x,   lag = LB_LAGS, type = "Ljung-Box")$statistic, 1),
    LB_resid    = round(Box.test(e,   lag = LB_LAGS, type = "Ljung-Box")$statistic, 1),
    LB_resid_sq = round(Box.test(e^2, lag = LB_LAGS, type = "Ljung-Box")$statistic, 1),
    mean_resid  = round(mean(e), 5),       # ~0 (additive); ACD gives ~1 instead
    sd_resid    = round(sd(e), 4),
    skewness    = round(skew, 3),          # 0 under normality
    ex_kurtosis = round(kurt - 3, 2),      # 0 under normality
    JB_stat     = round(jb, 0),
    normal      = ifelse(jb > 5.99, "REJECTED", "not rejected")
  )
}))

cat("=== ARMA(1,1) RESIDUAL DIAGNOSTICS ===\n")
cat("chi-sq(15) crit = 25 | Jarque-Bera chi-sq(2) crit = 5.99\n\n")
print(arma_resid)

cat("\nREADING IT:\n")
cat("  mean_resid ~ 0        -> additive residuals, as expected\n")
cat("  skewness > 0, kurt >> 0 -> strongly right-skewed and heavy-tailed. The\n")
cat("     symmetric Gaussian error is why the simulation generated negatives.\n")
cat("  LB_resid_sq >> LB_resid -> ARMA absorbed the MEAN dependence but left\n")
cat("     VARIANCE clustering untouched. This is the heteroskedasticity the\n")
cat("     multiplicative ACD form handles by construction.\n")
```

**Verdict — rung 3.** The ARMA(1,1) specification is rejected on three
independent grounds: it generates negative durations in simulation at a rate of
roughly one observation in three; its residuals depart from normality by a very
wide margin; and it leaves substantial dependence in the squared residuals. The
three failures share a cause — an additive model with Gaussian innovations of
constant variance applied to data that are strictly positive and whose
variability scales with their level. What is required is a specification in
which positivity holds by construction and the conditional variance varies with
the conditional mean.

## 3.4 Exponential ACD Model


```{r eacd-fit}

#  EACD(1,1) - the ACD multiplicative fix.
#
#    x_i   = psi_i * epsilon_i,   epsilon_i ~ iid Exp(1)
#    psi_i = omega + alpha*x_{i-1} + beta*psi_{i-1}          (E&R eq.15)
#
#  ESTIMATION: maximum likelihood on the recursion above (E&R eq. 15)
#  For each trial (omega, alpha, beta) the psi
#  series is generated deterministically from the data, the standardised
#  residuals x/psi are formed, and the exponential log-likelihood
#  -sum(log psi_i + x_i/psi_i) is maximised. 
#  There is no scale parameter: the Exp(1) innovation has unit mean by construction, so the only free #  parameters are the three in the recursion(omega, alpha, beta).

#   The optimiser's job is to find the (omega, alpha, beta) that maximises that sum.


#  Checks if model is present in cache, and if not re-runs and saves. If present, this part is skipped to prevent re-running.
if (!fit_ready("eacd_fits")) {
eacd_fits <- list()

# Assets known to need seeded nlminb, with their ARMA-implied start values.
# omega seeded near the other assets' scale; alpha/beta from the ARMA benchmark.
eacd_seed <- list("NVDA" = c(0.0015, 0.047, 0.925))

for (nm in names(split_sets)) {

  x <- get_fit_series(nm, FIT_N)
  cat(sprintf("\n=== EACD(1,1): %s (n = %s) ===\n",
              nm, format(length(x), big.mark = ",")))

  fit <- NULL

  #  Primary attempt
  if (!is.null(eacd_seed[[nm]])) { # If the asset has a seed, (NVDA)

    cat("  seeded nlminb (known-stiff likelihood; benign NA/NaN warnings muffled)...\n")
    fit <- tryCatch(
      withCallingHandlers( # inspects warnings
        acdFit(durations = x, model = "ACD", dist = "exponential", # model fit
               order = c(1, 1), optimFnc = "nlminb",
               startPara = eacd_seed[[nm]], output = FALSE),
        warning = function(w) {
          if (grepl("NA/NaN function evaluation", conditionMessage(w)))
            invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
        }),
      error = function(e) {
        cat("  seeded nlminb failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
  } else {
    fit <- tryCatch(
      acdFit(durations = x, model = "ACD", dist = "exponential",
             order = c(1, 1), output = FALSE),
      error = function(e) {
        cat("  default optimiser failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
  }

  #  Fallback: unseeded nlminb, for any asset that unexpectedly failed, trying another optimiser.
  if (is.null(fit)) {
    cat("  retrying with unseeded nlminb...\n")
    fit <- tryCatch(
      acdFit(durations = x, model = "ACD", dist = "exponential",
             order = c(1, 1), optimFnc = "nlminb", output = FALSE),
      error = function(e) {
        cat("  nlminb also failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
  }

  eacd_fits[nm] <- list(fit)   # [nm]<-list() not [[nm]]<- : preserves a NULL (failed-fit) entry
}
save_model_progress(eacd_fits = eacd_fits) # writes to the cache
}

stopifnot(!any(vapply(eacd_fits, is.null, logical(1)))) # stops if any asset is missing

# goodnessOfFit is a data.frame with NAMED rows, index by name, not position.

gof <- function(f, what) f$goodnessOfFit[what, "value"]


eacd_tbl <- rbindlist(lapply(names(eacd_fits), function(nm) {
  f <- eacd_fits[[nm]]; 
  p <- f$mPara # vector of fitted parameters
  se  <- f$parameterInference$robustSE   # row order matches mPara: omega, alpha1, beta1
  rho <- f$robustCorr
  pers    <- unname(p["alpha1"] + p["beta1"])
  
  #  Var(alpha+beta) = Var(alpha) + Var(beta) + 2*Cov(alpha,beta). se[2], se[3], 
  #  index(1-omega, 2-alpha, 3-beta)
  se_pers <- sqrt(se[2]^2 + se[3]^2 + 2 * rho[2, 3] * se[2] * se[3]) # SE of persistence
  
  z_pers  <- (pers - 1) / se_pers # Standard z-test : if |z_pers| > 1.96, we can say persistence differs from 1 at the 5% level.
  data.table(
    asset          = nm,
    omega          = round(unname(p["omega"]),  5),
    alpha          = round(unname(p["alpha1"]), 4),
    beta           = round(unname(p["beta1"]),  4),
    persistence    = round(pers, 4),
    SE_persistence = round(se_pers, 6),
    z_vs_1         = round(z_pers, 1),
    regime         = ifelse(p["alpha1"] + p["beta1"] < 1, "stationary", "INTEGRATED"),
    sig_vs_1       = ifelse(abs(z_pers) > 1.96, "YES (|z|>1.96)", "no"),
    logLik         = round(gof(f, "LogLikelihood"), 1),
    AIC            = round(gof(f, "AIC"), 1),
    BIC            = round(gof(f, "BIC"), 1)
  )
}))

cat("\n\n=== EACD(1,1) PARAMETER ESTIMATES ===\n")
cat("Benchmark (IBM, E&R 1998): alpha = 0.063, beta = 0.933, sum = 0.996\n\n")
print(eacd_tbl)

# Persistence is close to unity for all three assets. However, the z_vs_1 results show that these differences are statistically significant. Given the large sample size, even small departures from 1 can be detected clearly. In particular, GBP/USD has persistence that is significantly below 1, rather than simply being statistically indistinguishable from it.

#  The decomposition also differs across the three markets in a way that reflects their different market structures. The cryptocurrency series has the largest alpha and the smallest beta, meaning that its conditional mean reacts more strongly to each individual duration but places less weight on its previous value. In contrast, the FX series has a much smaller response to individual quote revisions but retains a greater dependence on its past values.

```


```{r eacd-residuals}

#  RESIDUAL DIAGNOSTICS
#
#  THE LOGIC: the model claims x_i = psi_i * eps_i with eps_i ~ iid Exp(1).
#  Divide it out:  eps_hat_i = x_i / psi_hat_i
#  If the claim is TRUE, eps_hat must be (a) serially INDEPENDENT and (b) Exp(1).
#
#    1. Ljung-Box(15) on eps_hat   -> did the model ABSORB the clustering?
#    2. Ljung-Box(15) on eps_hat^2 -> is clustering left in the VARIANCE?
#    3. Excess dispersion          -> is Exp(1) the right DISTRIBUTION?
#
#  Test 3 is the one that decides whether to fit WACD. 
#  E&R obtained sd = 1.18, rejected the exponential, and moved to Weibull. 

resid_diag <- rbindlist(lapply(names(eacd_fits), function(nm) {

  f <- eacd_fits[[nm]]
  e <- as.numeric(f$residuals)          # ACDm returns x_i / psi_hat_i
  e <- e[is.finite(e) & e > 0]          # Filters to finite positive value, else stray entries breaks the test.
  n <- length(e)

  # Box test
  
  lb_e_t  <- Box.test(e,   lag = LB_LAGS, type = "Ljung-Box") # mean dynamics
  lb_e2_t <- Box.test(e^2, lag = LB_LAGS, type = "Ljung-Box") # variance dynamics
  lb_e  <- lb_e_t$statistic
  lb_e2 <- lb_e2_t$statistic

  # Excess dispersion 
  #   Under Exp(1): sd(eps) = 1 exactly.
  #   Statistic: sqrt(N) * (sigma^2 - 1) / sigma_u,  sigma_u = sd((eps-1)^2)
  #   ~ N(0,1) asymptotically. |stat| > 1.96 => REJECT the exponential.
  s2        <- var(e)
  sig_u     <- sd((e - 1)^2) 
  disp_stat <- sqrt(n) * (s2 - 1) / sig_u # how far is the variance from 1.

  # Serial dependence in the data before fitting.
  x    <- get_fit_series(nm, FIT_N)
  lb_x_t <- Box.test(x, lag = LB_LAGS, type = "Ljung-Box")
  lb_x <- lb_x_t$statistic

  data.table(
    asset       = nm,
    n           = n,
    LB_before   = round(lb_x, 1),          # adjusted durations, pre-model
    LB_before_p = signif(lb_x_t$p.value, 3),
    LB_resid    = round(lb_e, 1),          # post-model  <- the headline
    LB_resid_p  = signif(lb_e_t$p.value, 3),  # p < .05 => still reject serial independence at LB_LAGS lags
    LB_drop_pct = round(100 * (1 - lb_e / lb_x), 1),
    LB_resid_sq = round(lb_e2, 1),
    LB_resid_sq_p = signif(lb_e2_t$p.value, 3),
    mean_resid  = round(mean(e), 6),       # should be ~1
    mean_resid_z = round(resid_mean_z(e), 1),  # formal z-stat for E[eps]=1 (magnitude, not a 1.96 pass/fail at this n)
    sd_resid    = round(sd(e), 4),         # should be ~1 under Exp(1)
    CV_resid    = round(sd(e) / mean(e), 4),  # should be ~1 under Exp(1) (CV=1 is exponential's defining property); mean_resid pinned near 1 by the MLE's own first-order condition, so CV_resid tracks sd_resid almost exactly here -- reported anyway since it's the same CV=1 diagnostic rung 1 used, now applied post-model
    disp_stat   = round(disp_stat, 1),
    exponential = ifelse(abs(disp_stat) > 1.96, "REJECTED", "not rejected")
  )
}))

cat("=== E&R (1998) TABLE II -- RESIDUAL DIAGNOSTICS ===\n")
cat("Benchmark (IBM): LB = 38.08, sd(resid) = 1.18, exponential REJECTED\n")
cat("chi-sq(15) crit = 25 (p < .05) | dispersion crit = |1.96|\n\n")
print(resid_diag)

#  The `LB_*_p` columns give the formal p-values for the Ljung–Box statistics, using a chi-squared distribution with 15 degrees of freedom. A p-value below 0.05 leads to the same conclusion as a statistic above the critical value of about 25. Instead of relying only on the critical value, the p-value shows the strength of the evidence against the null hypothesis of no residual autocorrelation.

#  However, with the very large sample sizes used here, the p-values should not be interpreted on their own. With hundreds of thousands or millions of observations, even very small amounts of autocorrelation can produce extremely small p-values. Therefore, the p-values should be considered alongside the percentage reduction in the Ljung–Box statistic and, more importantly, the actual size of the remaining autocorrelation.

#  Overall, the ACD model removes most of the dependence in the durations. The reduction is substantially larger than the 17.5% reduction reported by Engle and Russell for IBM. Nevertheless, the Ljung–Box statistic remains above 25 for all three assets. This does not necessarily mean that the model is misspecified. Engle and Russell's own EACD(1,1) model produced a statistic of 38.08, which was also above the critical value, and later literature, including Pacurar (2008), documents that some residual dependence can remain after fitting an ACD model. In addition, the Ljung–Box statistic increases with sample size, so at the sample sizes used here, values of this magnitude can correspond to autocorrelations that are very small in practical terms.

#  The squared-residual results are more favourable than the results for the residuals themselves. This highlights an important feature of the multiplicative ACD specification. The model may not completely remove dependence in the conditional mean, with its performance being broadly comparable to an ARMA-type approach, but it captures the conditional variance much more effectively. This is where the multiplicative structure provides its main advantage.

#  Finally, the residual dispersion results indicate that the exponential distribution is not adequate. Since the residual standard deviation is greater than 1 and the dispersion statistic is outside the 95% range, the assumption of an Exp(1) distribution is rejected. This suggests that the residuals are more dispersed and heavier-tailed than the exponential distribution allows, motivating the use of the Weibull ACD model.

```

```{r}
# EXPONENTIAL GOODNESS-OF-FIT

# This test checks whether the exponential distribution is the correct shape for the underlying data.

eacd_ks <- rbindlist(lapply(names(eacd_fits), function(nm) {

  e <- as.numeric(eacd_fits[[nm]]$residuals)
  e <- e[is.finite(e) & e > 0]

  ks <- ks.test(e, "pexp", rate = 1) # One-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
  
  # it takes the empirical residuals e, builds their empirical CDF (for any value v, "what fraction of my residuals are ≤ v"), and compares that curve directly against the theoretical CDF of an Exponential distribution with rate 1.

  data.table(
    asset = nm,
    n = length(e),
    D = unname(ks$statistic), # single largest vertical gap vetween the two curves
    p_value = ks$p.value,
    verdict = ifelse(ks$p.value < 0.05,
                     "REJECT Exp(1)",
                     "not rejected")
  )
}))

print(eacd_ks)
```

```{r eacd-order-seed-helpers}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# This chunk contains the functions which can be used for eacd and wacd model fitting. 
# No model fitting/ residual analysis is done here.
# Can be skipped.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Building a starting guess for EACD(2,2)

make_seed_22 <- function(nm, base_fits = eacd_fits) {
  p <- base_fits[[nm]]$mPara
  om <- unname(p["omega"]); a1 <- unname(p["alpha1"]); b1 <- unname(p["beta1"])
  shape <- unname(base_fits[[nm]]$dPara["gamma"]) # For WACD model, which has a shape parameter. EACD does not have $dPara.
  
  # put most of alpha on lag 1, a whisper on lag 2; split beta ~85/15
  c(om, a1 * 0.95, a1 * 0.05, b1 * 0.85, b1 * 0.15, shape)
}

# Seeds for the asymmetric orders (1,2) and (2,1)

make_seed_asym <- function(nm, order, base_fits = eacd_fits) {
  p  <- base_fits[[nm]]$mPara
  om <- unname(p["omega"]); a1 <- unname(p["alpha1"]); b1 <- unname(p["beta1"])
  shape <- unname(base_fits[[nm]]$dPara["gamma"])
  if (identical(order, c(1, 2))) c(om, a1, b1 * 0.85, b1 * 0.15, shape)   # omega, alpha1, beta1, beta2, [gamma]
  else                            c(om, a1 * 0.95, a1 * 0.05, b1, shape)  # omega, alpha1, alpha2, beta1, [gamma]
}

# Actual fit

fit_eacd_order <- function(order, dist = "exponential", base_fits = eacd_fits) {
  fits <- list(); status <- list()
  for (nm in names(split_sets)) {
    x    <- get_fit_series(nm, FIT_N)
    seed <- make_seed_asym(nm, order, base_fits = base_fits)
    fit <- tryCatch(
      withCallingHandlers(
        acdFit(durations = x, model = "ACD", dist = dist,
               order = order, optimFnc = "nlminb", startPara = seed,
               optimFncArgs = list(control = list(eval.max = 1000, iter.max = 800)),
               forceErrExpec = (dist != "exponential"),
               output = FALSE),
        warning = function(w) {
          if (grepl("NA/NaN function evaluation", conditionMessage(w)))
            invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
        }),
      error = function(e) NULL)
    fits[nm]     <- list(fit)   # [nm]<-list() not [[nm]]<- : preserves a NULL (failed-fit) entry
    status[[nm]] <- if (is.null(fit)) "FAILED (evidence of over-parameterisation)" else "converged"
  }
  list(fits = fits, status = status)
}


lb15 <- function(f, sq = FALSE, p = FALSE) {
  e <- as.numeric(f$residuals); e <- e[is.finite(e) & e > 0]
  
  if (length(e) <= LB_LAGS) return(NA_real_)
  bt <- Box.test(if (sq) e^2 else e, lag = LB_LAGS, type = "Ljung-Box")
  if (p) return(bt$p.value)
  unname(bt$statistic)
}

# Persistence calculator

persist_of <- function(f) {
  p <- f$mPara
  unname(sum(p[grepl("^alpha", names(p))]) + sum(p[grepl("^beta", names(p))]))
}

# To assemble the order selection comparison table

build_order_grid <- function(order_fits, order_k, order_crit, baseline_fits) {
  rbindlist(lapply(names(split_sets), function(nm) {
    rbindlist(lapply(names(order_fits), function(ord) {
      f <- order_fits[[ord]][[nm]]
      na_row <- function(verdict) data.table(
        asset = nm, order = ord, k = order_k[[ord]],
        logLik = NA_real_, AIC = NA_real_, BIC = NA_real_,
        persistence = NA_real_, LB_resid = NA_real_,
        LR = NA_real_, LR_crit = NA_real_, verdict = verdict)
      if (is.null(f)) return(na_row("FAILED to converge"))

      row <- tryCatch({
        ll <- gof(f, "LogLikelihood")
        lr <- lr_crit <- NA_real_; verdict <- "-- baseline --"
        if (ord != "(1,1)") {
          lr      <- 2 * (ll - gof(baseline_fits[[nm]], "LogLikelihood"))
          lr_crit <- order_crit[[ord]]
          verdict <- ifelse(lr > lr_crit, "sig. better than (1,1)", "NOT sig. better than (1,1)")
        }
        data.table(asset = nm, order = ord, k = order_k[[ord]],
                   logLik = round(ll, 1), AIC = round(gof(f, "AIC"), 1), BIC = round(gof(f, "BIC"), 1),
                   persistence = round(persist_of(f), 4), LB_resid = round(lb15(f), 1),
                   LR = round(lr, 2), LR_crit = lr_crit, verdict = verdict)
      }, error = function(e) NULL)

      if (is.null(row) || !is.finite(row$logLik)) return(na_row("converged but degenerate (non-finite fit)"))
      row
    }))
  }))
}

# Residual Diagnostics for the orders

build_resid_diag_by_order <- function(order_fits, dist_label = "exponential") {
  rbindlist(lapply(names(split_sets), function(nm) {
    rbindlist(lapply(names(order_fits), function(ord) {
      f <- order_fits[[ord]][[nm]]
      if (is.null(f))
        return(data.table(asset = nm, order = ord, n = NA_integer_,
                           LB_resid = NA_real_, LB_resid_p = NA_real_,
                           LB_resid_sq = NA_real_, LB_resid_sq_p = NA_real_,
                           mean_resid = NA_real_, mean_resid_z = NA_real_, sd_resid = NA_real_,
                           disp_stat = NA_real_, verdict = "FAILED to converge"))

      e <- as.numeric(f$residuals); e <- e[is.finite(e) & e > 0]
      n <- length(e)
      if (n <= LB_LAGS)
        return(data.table(asset = nm, order = ord, n = n,
                           LB_resid = NA_real_, LB_resid_p = NA_real_,
                           LB_resid_sq = NA_real_, LB_resid_sq_p = NA_real_,
                           mean_resid = round(mean(e), 4), mean_resid_z = NA_real_, sd_resid = NA_real_,
                           disp_stat = NA_real_, verdict = "degenerate"))

      lb_e_t  <- Box.test(e,   lag = LB_LAGS, type = "Ljung-Box")
      lb_e2_t <- Box.test(e^2, lag = LB_LAGS, type = "Ljung-Box")
      lb_e  <- unname(lb_e_t$statistic)
      lb_e2 <- unname(lb_e2_t$statistic)
      s2 <- var(e); sig_u <- sd((e - 1)^2)
      disp_stat <- sqrt(n) * (s2 - 1) / sig_u

      data.table(asset = nm, order = ord, n = n,
                 LB_resid = round(lb_e, 1), LB_resid_p = signif(lb_e_t$p.value, 3),
                 LB_resid_sq = round(lb_e2, 1), LB_resid_sq_p = signif(lb_e2_t$p.value, 3),
                 mean_resid = round(mean(e), 4), mean_resid_z = round(resid_mean_z(e), 1),
                 sd_resid = round(sd(e), 4),
                 disp_stat = round(disp_stat, 1),
                 verdict = ifelse(abs(disp_stat) > 1.96,
                                   sprintf("Var(eps)!=1 (not %s-consistent)", dist_label),
                                   sprintf("Var(eps)~1 (%s-consistent)", dist_label)))
    }))
  }))
}

```

```{r eacd-order-selection}

#  EACD ORDER SELECTION: (1,2), (2,1), (2,2), all fitted, tabulated, and
#  compared against the (1,1) baseline.
#
#  ALL THREE assets are seeded here, each at its OWN (1,1) solution extended
#  with small second-order lags. Richer orders are a harder optimisation than
#  (1,1): the extra parameters can leave the likelihood flat/ridged (if they
#  are redundant) or merely stiff (the near-zero-duration issue, now affecting
#  all assets). Seeding at the (1,1) optimum starts the search at the answer's
#  neighbourhood.
#
#  IF an asset STILL fails to converge after seeding, that itself is evidence
#  of over-parameterisation - a likelihood with no identified optimum at that
#  order - and is reported as such rather than forced.

# Order (2,2)

if (!fit_ready("eacd22_fits")) {
eacd22_fits <- list()
eacd22_status <- list()

for (nm in names(split_sets)) {

  x <- get_fit_series(nm, FIT_N)
  cat(sprintf("\n=== EACD(2,2): %s (n = %s) ===\n",
              nm, format(length(x), big.mark = ",")))

  seed <- make_seed_22(nm)
  cat(sprintf("  seeded at (1,1)-extended: omega=%.4g a1=%.3f a2=%.3f b1=%.3f b2=%.3f\n",
              seed[1], seed[2], seed[3], seed[4], seed[5]))

  fit <- tryCatch(
    withCallingHandlers(
      acdFit(durations = x, model = "ACD", dist = "exponential",
             order = c(2, 2), optimFnc = "nlminb",
             startPara = seed,
             optimFncArgs = list(control = list(eval.max = 1000, iter.max = 800)),
             output = FALSE),
      warning = function(w) {
        if (grepl("NA/NaN function evaluation", conditionMessage(w)))
          invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }),
    error = function(e) {
      cat("  FAILED to converge:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })

  eacd22_fits[nm]     <- list(fit)   # [nm]<-list() not [[nm]]<- : preserves a NULL (failed-fit) entry
  eacd22_status[[nm]] <- if (is.null(fit)) "FAILED (evidence of over-parameterisation)" else "converged"
}

cat("\n=== (2,2) CONVERGENCE STATUS ===\n")
for (nm in names(eacd22_status)) cat(sprintf("  %-8s: %s\n", nm, eacd22_status[[nm]]))
save_model_progress(eacd22_fits = eacd22_fits)
}

converged <- names(eacd22_fits)[!vapply(eacd22_fits, is.null, logical(1))]
cat(sprintf("\n%d of %d assets converged for (2,2).\n",
            length(converged), length(eacd22_fits)))


#  EACD(1,2) and EACD(2,1) - the two asymmetric orders

#    (1,2): mu_i = omega + alpha1*x_{i-1} + beta1*mu_{i-1} + beta2*mu_{i-2}
#    (2,1): mu_i = omega + alpha1*x_{i-1} + alpha2*x_{i-2} + beta1*mu_{i-1}

if (!fit_ready("eacd12_fits") || !fit_ready("eacd21_fits")) {
res12 <- fit_eacd_order(c(1, 2)); eacd12_fits <- res12$fits
res21 <- fit_eacd_order(c(2, 1)); eacd21_fits <- res21$fits

cat("=== (1,2) CONVERGENCE STATUS ===\n")
for (nm in names(res12$status)) cat(sprintf("  %-8s: %s\n", nm, res12$status[[nm]]))
cat("\n=== (2,1) CONVERGENCE STATUS ===\n")
for (nm in names(res21$status)) cat(sprintf("  %-8s: %s\n", nm, res21$status[[nm]]))
save_model_progress(eacd12_fits = eacd12_fits, eacd21_fits = eacd21_fits)
}

eacd22_tbl <- rbindlist(lapply(names(eacd22_fits), function(nm) {
  f <- eacd22_fits[[nm]]; p <- f$mPara

  # Parameters table with t-statstics
  
  se <- tryCatch({
    inf <- f$parameterInference
    if (is.matrix(inf) && "SE" %in% colnames(inf)) inf[, "SE"]
    else setNames(rep(NA_real_, length(p)), names(p))
  }, error = function(e) setNames(rep(NA_real_, length(p)), names(p)))

  tv <- function(nm2) if (nm2 %in% names(p) && nm2 %in% names(se) && !is.na(se[nm2]))
                        round(unname(p[nm2]/se[nm2]), 2) else NA

  a1<-unname(p["alpha1"]); a2<-unname(p["alpha2"]); b1<-unname(p["beta1"]); b2<-unname(p["beta2"])
  data.table(asset=nm, omega=round(unname(p["omega"]),5),
    alpha1=round(a1,4), t_a1=tv("alpha1"), alpha2=round(a2,4), t_a2=tv("alpha2"),
    beta1=round(b1,4),  t_b1=tv("beta1"),  beta2=round(b2,4),  t_b2=tv("beta2"),
    persistence=round(a1+a2+b1+b2,4))
}))
cat("=== EACD(2,2) PARAMETERS ===\n")
cat("E&R: a1=0.083 a2=-0.016(t=-2.05) b1=0.799 b2=0.130(t=1.63) sum=0.996\n")
cat("Watch t_a2, t_b2: |t|<2 => second-order terms add little.\n\n")
print(eacd22_tbl)

tbl12 <- rbindlist(lapply(names(eacd12_fits), function(nm) {
  f <- eacd12_fits[[nm]]
  if (is.null(f)) return(data.table(asset=nm, omega=NA_real_, alpha1=NA_real_,
                                     beta1=NA_real_, beta2=NA_real_, persistence=NA_real_))
  p <- f$mPara
  data.table(asset = nm, omega = round(unname(p["omega"]), 5),
             alpha1 = round(unname(p["alpha1"]), 4), beta1 = round(unname(p["beta1"]), 4),
             beta2  = round(unname(p["beta2"]), 4),
             persistence = round(unname(p["alpha1"] + p["beta1"] + p["beta2"]), 4))
}))
cat("=== EACD(1,2) PARAMETERS ===\n\n"); print(tbl12)

tbl21 <- rbindlist(lapply(names(eacd21_fits), function(nm) {
  f <- eacd21_fits[[nm]]
  if (is.null(f)) return(data.table(asset=nm, omega=NA_real_, alpha1=NA_real_,
                                     alpha2=NA_real_, beta1=NA_real_, persistence=NA_real_))
  p <- f$mPara
  data.table(asset = nm, omega = round(unname(p["omega"]), 5),
             alpha1 = round(unname(p["alpha1"]), 4), alpha2 = round(unname(p["alpha2"]), 4),
             beta1  = round(unname(p["beta1"]), 4),
             persistence = round(unname(p["alpha1"] + p["alpha2"] + p["beta1"]), 4))
}))
cat("\n=== EACD(2,1) PARAMETERS ===\n\n"); print(tbl21)

#  FULL ORDER-SELECTION GRID: EACD(1,1) / (1,2) / (2,1) / (2,2).

order_fits <- list("(1,1)" = eacd_fits, "(1,2)" = eacd12_fits,
                    "(2,1)" = eacd21_fits, "(2,2)" = eacd22_fits)
order_k    <- c("(1,1)" = 3, "(1,2)" = 4, "(2,1)" = 4, "(2,2)" = 5)   # omega + alphas + betas
order_crit <- c("(1,2)" = 3.84, "(2,1)" = 3.84, "(2,2)" = 5.99)        # chi-sq crit, df=1,1,2

order_grid <- build_order_grid(order_fits, order_k, order_crit, eacd_fits)

for (nm in names(split_sets)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n=== ORDER SELECTION GRID: %s ===\n\n", nm))
  sub <- order_grid[asset == nm]
  print(sub, row.names = FALSE)
  if (all(is.finite(sub$AIC))) {
    cat(sprintf("  Best by AIC: %s | Best by BIC: %s\n",
                sub$order[which.min(sub$AIC)], sub$order[which.min(sub$BIC)]))
  }
}

#  For the fitted data, the LR test, AIC and BIC all agree that the EACD(2,2) model provides a significantly better fit than the EACD(1,1) model for all three assets. This suggests that using an EACD(1,1) model was too restrictive and could make the BTC and NVDA series appear more persistent than they actually are.

#  After selecting the appropriate order, the near-unit-root behaviour is still present. For GBP/USD, the persistence estimate under EACD(2,2) is almost exactly at the boundary of 1. For BTC and NVDA, however, the persistence estimate is closer to 1 than the EACD(1,1) results suggested. Therefore, the evidence for very high persistence remains, but the EACD(1,1) model overstated how far BTC and NVDA were above 1.

#  The individual alpha and beta coefficients in the EACD(2,2) model should be interpreted with some caution. They are poorly identified, with large coefficients that almost cancel each other out, and reliable standard errors could not be obtained. For this reason, the overall persistence measure is more informative and reliable than interpreting the individual parameter estimates separately.
```


```{r eacd-order-residuals}

#  RESIDUAL DIAGNOSTICS ACROSS ALL FOUR ORDERS 

build_resid_diag_by_order <- function(order_fits, dist_label = "exponential") {
  rbindlist(lapply(names(split_sets), function(nm) {
    rbindlist(lapply(names(order_fits), function(ord) {
      f <- order_fits[[ord]][[nm]]
      if (is.null(f))
        return(data.table(asset = nm, order = ord, n = NA_integer_,
                           LB_resid = NA_real_, LB_resid_p = NA_real_,
                           LB_resid_sq = NA_real_, LB_resid_sq_p = NA_real_,
                           mean_resid = NA_real_, mean_resid_z = NA_real_, sd_resid = NA_real_,
                           disp_stat = NA_real_, verdict = "FAILED to converge"))

      e <- as.numeric(f$residuals); e <- e[is.finite(e) & e > 0]
      n <- length(e)
      if (n <= LB_LAGS)
        return(data.table(asset = nm, order = ord, n = n,
                           LB_resid = NA_real_, LB_resid_p = NA_real_,
                           LB_resid_sq = NA_real_, LB_resid_sq_p = NA_real_,
                           mean_resid = round(mean(e), 4), mean_resid_z = NA_real_, sd_resid = NA_real_,
                           disp_stat = NA_real_, verdict = "degenerate"))

      lb_e_t  <- Box.test(e,   lag = LB_LAGS, type = "Ljung-Box")
      lb_e2_t <- Box.test(e^2, lag = LB_LAGS, type = "Ljung-Box")
      lb_e  <- unname(lb_e_t$statistic)
      lb_e2 <- unname(lb_e2_t$statistic)
      s2 <- var(e); sig_u <- sd((e - 1)^2)
      disp_stat <- sqrt(n) * (s2 - 1) / sig_u

      data.table(asset = nm, order = ord, n = n,
                 LB_resid = round(lb_e, 1), LB_resid_p = signif(lb_e_t$p.value, 3),
                 LB_resid_sq = round(lb_e2, 1), LB_resid_sq_p = signif(lb_e2_t$p.value, 3),
                 mean_resid = round(mean(e), 4), mean_resid_z = round(resid_mean_z(e), 1),
                 sd_resid = round(sd(e), 4),
                 disp_stat = round(disp_stat, 1),
                 verdict = ifelse(abs(disp_stat) > 1.96,
                                   sprintf("Var(eps)!=1 (not %s-consistent)", dist_label),
                                   sprintf("Var(eps)~1 (%s-consistent)", dist_label)))
    }))
  }))
}

resid_diag_by_order <- build_resid_diag_by_order(order_fits, dist_label = "exponential")

for (nm in names(split_sets)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n=== RESIDUAL DIAGNOSTICS BY ORDER: %s ===\n\n", nm))
  print(resid_diag_by_order[asset == nm], row.names = FALSE)
}
```

**Verdict — rung 4.** The EACD(1,1) specification is retained as a description
of the conditional mean and rejected as a complete model. Positivity holds by
construction, the conditional variance is accounted for, and the estimated
persistence is stable across a range of checks. The exponential assumption for
the innovation distribution is not supported: the standardised residuals are
substantially more dispersed than it requires. The direction of the failure
indicates the remedy — dispersion in excess of the exponential arises when short
durations are more common, and long durations more extreme, than a constant
hazard permits. A distribution admitting a decreasing hazard accommodates both.

## QQ plot: EACD residual goodness-of-fit, all orders

```{r qq-helpers}

#  Shared QQ-plot helpers for the goodness-of-fit checks, used once per model
#  family right after that family's own order-selection section -- kept
#  split rather than one combined chunk requiring every family's fits in
#  memory at once. Each family's own order_fits/wacd_order_fits/
#  logacd_order_fits/logacd2_order_fits list only needs to exist while ITS
#  OWN QQ chunk runs, so the fit sections can be run and knitted one at a
#  time instead of all four staying resident together.
#
#  qq_theoretical_q / qq_data_one: eps_hat = x/psi_hat (ACDm's own
#  $residuals), sampled to n_pts=2000 evenly-spaced empirical quantiles --
#  same convention as this document's own survivor-function plots
#  (build_survivor_dt) -- residual vectors run into the millions for
#  BTC/NVDA.
#
#  DISTRIBUTION PER FAMILY (verified against each family's own acdFit()
#  call): EACD/LACD1/LACD2 all use dist="exponential" (eps ~ Exp(1)); WACD
#  uses dist="weibull" with forceErrExpec=TRUE, so eps ~ Weibull(gamma,
#  scale=1/Gamma(1+1/gamma)) with the FITTED gamma read per fit from
#  f$dPara["gamma"].

qq_theoretical_q <- function(probs, dist_type, gamma_hat = NA_real_) {
  if (dist_type == "exponential") qexp(probs, rate = 1)
  else qweibull(probs, shape = gamma_hat, scale = 1 / gamma(1 + 1 / gamma_hat))
}

qq_data_one <- function(f, dist_type, n_pts = 5000) {
  if (is.null(f)) return(NULL)
  e <- sort(as.numeric(f$residuals)); e <- e[is.finite(e) & e > 0]
  n <- length(e)
  if (n < 20) return(NULL)
  idx    <- unique(round(seq(1, n, length.out = min(n_pts, n))))
  probs  <- (idx - 0.5) / n
  gam    <- if (dist_type == "weibull") unname(f$dPara["gamma"]) else NA_real_
  data.table(sample = e[idx], theoretical = qq_theoretical_q(probs, dist_type, gam))
}

qq_fit_quality <- function(d) {
  fit_lm <- lm(sample ~ theoretical, data = d)
  data.table(R2 = round(summary(fit_lm)$r.squared, 4),
             slope = round(unname(coef(fit_lm)[2]), 4),
             intercept = round(unname(coef(fit_lm)[1]), 4),
             max_abs_dev = round(max(abs(d$sample - d$theoretical)), 4))
}

qq_orders <- c("(1,1)", "(1,2)", "(2,1)", "(2,2)")

qq_plot_family <- function(fits, dist, family_name) {
  qq_mf <- rbindlist(lapply(qq_orders, function(ord) {
    fits_ord <- fits[[ord]]
    if (is.null(fits_ord)) return(NULL)
    rbindlist(lapply(names(fits_ord), function(nm) {
      d <- qq_data_one(fits_ord[[nm]], dist)
      if (is.null(d)) return(NULL)
      d[, `:=`(asset = nm, order = ord)]
      d
    }))
  }))

  if (is.null(qq_mf) || nrow(qq_mf) == 0) {
    cat(sprintf("%s: no converged fits at any order -- skipping.\n", family_name))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  print(
    ggplot(qq_mf, aes(x = theoretical, y = sample)) +
      geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.35, colour = "steelblue") +
      geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
      facet_grid(asset ~ order, scales = "free") +
      labs(title    = sprintf("%s -- QQ plot, empirical vs theoretical residual quantiles, all orders", family_name),
           subtitle = if (dist == "weibull")
             "Red dashed line = perfect fit (45 degrees). Theoretical: Weibull(gamma_hat), gamma fitted per asset/order."
           else
             "Red dashed line = perfect fit (45 degrees). Theoretical: Exp(1).",
           x = "Theoretical quantile", y = "Empirical (sample) quantile") +
      theme_minimal() + theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 9))
  )
  invisible(qq_mf)
}

cat("READING IT (applies to every per-model QQ plot in this and later\n")
cat("sections): points hugging the red 45-degree line at both ends = the\n")
cat("assumed distribution is a good fit. Points curving ABOVE the line in\n")
cat("the upper-right (large theoretical quantiles) = observed extreme\n")
cat("durations are heavier-tailed than the model assumes -- the same finding\n")
cat("this document's own survivor-function plots (Section 10.4's\n")
cat("build_survivor_dt) already show, now visible directly rather than via\n")
cat("-log(S(x)). A missing (asset, order) panel means that combination did\n")
cat("not converge -- see that model's own order-selection table for why.\n")
```
