### LACD2 order selection

```{r logacd2-order-selection}

#  LACD2 ORDER SELECTION:
#      log psi_i = omega + sum_j alpha_j*eps_{i-j} + sum_k beta_k*log(psi_{i-k})

make_lacd2_seed_22 <- function(nm) {
  p <- logacd2_fits[[nm]]$mPara
  om <- unname(p["omega"]); a1 <- unname(p["alpha1"]); b1 <- unname(p["beta1"])
  c(om, a1 * 0.95, a1 * 0.05, b1 * 0.85, b1 * 0.15)
}

make_lacd2_seed_asym <- function(nm, order) {
  p <- logacd2_fits[[nm]]$mPara
  om <- unname(p["omega"]); a1 <- unname(p["alpha1"]); b1 <- unname(p["beta1"])
  if (identical(order, c(1, 2))) c(om, a1, b1 * 0.85, b1 * 0.15)   # omega, alpha1, beta1, beta2
  else                            c(om, a1 * 0.95, a1 * 0.05, b1)  # omega, alpha1, alpha2, beta1
}

fit_lacd2_order <- function(order, seed_fn) {
  if (!requireNamespace("callr", quietly = TRUE))
    stop("Package 'callr' is required for crash-isolated LACD2 order fitting -- install.packages(\"callr\")")
  fits <- list(); status <- list()
  for (nm in names(split_sets)) {
    if (is.null(logacd2_fits[[nm]])) {
      fits[nm]     <- list(NULL)
      status[[nm]] <- "SKIPPED (LACD2(1,1) baseline did not converge -- nothing to seed from)"
      next
    }
    x    <- get_fit_series(nm, FIT_N)
    seed <- seed_fn(nm)
    cat(sprintf("\n=== LACD2%s: %s (n = %s) ===\n",
                paste0("(", order[1], ",", order[2], ")"), nm, format(length(x), big.mark = ",")))

    fit <- tryCatch(
      callr::r(function(x, order, seed) {
        library(ACDm)
        tryCatch(
          withCallingHandlers(
            acdFit(durations = x, model = "LACD2", dist = "exponential",
                   order = order, optimFnc = "nlminb", startPara = seed,
                   control = list(eval.max = 1000, iter.max = 800),
                   output = FALSE),
            warning = function(w) {
              if (grepl("NA/NaN function evaluation", conditionMessage(w)))
                invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
            }),
          error = function(e) { cat("  [subprocess] FAILED to converge:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
      }, args = list(x = x, order = order, seed = seed), timeout = 1800),
      error = function(e) {
        cat("  subprocess crashed or timed out -- this session is UNAFFECTED:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })

    fits[nm]     <- list(fit)   # [nm]<-list() not [[nm]]<- : preserves a NULL (failed-fit) entry
    status[[nm]] <- if (is.null(fit)) "FAILED (crash, timeout, or over-parameterisation)" else "converged"
  }
  list(fits = fits, status = status)
}

if (!fit_ready("logacd2_22_fits")) {
res22b <- fit_lacd2_order(c(2, 2), make_lacd2_seed_22)
logacd2_22_fits <- res22b$fits

cat("\n=== LACD2(2,2) CONVERGENCE STATUS ===\n")
for (nm in names(res22b$status)) cat(sprintf("  %-8s: %s\n", nm, res22b$status[[nm]]))
save_model_progress(logacd2_22_fits = logacd2_22_fits)
}

if (!fit_ready("logacd2_12_fits") || !fit_ready("logacd2_21_fits")) {
res12b <- fit_lacd2_order(c(1, 2), function(nm) make_lacd2_seed_asym(nm, c(1, 2)))
logacd2_12_fits <- res12b$fits
res21b <- fit_lacd2_order(c(2, 1), function(nm) make_lacd2_seed_asym(nm, c(2, 1)))
logacd2_21_fits <- res21b$fits

cat("\n=== LACD2(1,2) CONVERGENCE STATUS ===\n")
for (nm in names(res12b$status)) cat(sprintf("  %-8s: %s\n", nm, res12b$status[[nm]]))
cat("\n=== LACD2(2,1) CONVERGENCE STATUS ===\n")
for (nm in names(res21b$status)) cat(sprintf("  %-8s: %s\n", nm, res21b$status[[nm]]))
save_model_progress(logacd2_12_fits = logacd2_12_fits, logacd2_21_fits = logacd2_21_fits)
}


#  ORDER-SELECTION GRID: LACD2, all four orders, exponential.

logacd2_order_fits <- list("(1,1)" = logacd2_fits, "(1,2)" = logacd2_12_fits,
                            "(2,1)" = logacd2_21_fits, "(2,2)" = logacd2_22_fits)
logacd2_order_k    <- c("(1,1)" = 3, "(1,2)" = 4, "(2,1)" = 4, "(2,2)" = 5)
logacd2_order_crit <- c("(1,2)" = 3.84, "(2,1)" = 3.84, "(2,2)" = 5.99)

logacd2_persist_of <- function(f) {
  p <- f$mPara
  unname(sum(p[grepl("^beta", names(p))]))
}

if (!exists("gof", inherits = FALSE))  gof  <- function(f, what) f$goodnessOfFit[what, "value"]
if (!exists("lb15", inherits = FALSE)) lb15 <- function(f, sq = FALSE, p = FALSE) {
  e <- as.numeric(f$residuals); e <- e[is.finite(e) & e > 0]
  if (length(e) <= LB_LAGS) return(NA_real_)
  bt <- Box.test(if (sq) e^2 else e, lag = LB_LAGS, type = "Ljung-Box")
  if (p) return(bt$p.value)
  unname(bt$statistic)
}

logacd2_order_grid <- rbindlist(lapply(names(split_sets), function(nm) {
  rbindlist(lapply(names(logacd2_order_fits), function(ord) {
    f <- logacd2_order_fits[[ord]][[nm]]
    na_row <- function(verdict) data.table(
      asset = nm, order = ord, k = logacd2_order_k[[ord]],
      logLik = NA_real_, AIC = NA_real_, BIC = NA_real_,
      persist_log_scale = NA_real_, LB_resid = NA_real_,
      LR = NA_real_, LR_crit = NA_real_, verdict = verdict)
    if (is.null(f)) return(na_row(if (ord == "(1,1)") "FAILED to converge" else "SKIPPED (no (1,1) baseline to seed from, or failed itself)"))

    row <- tryCatch({
      ll <- gof(f, "LogLikelihood")
      lr <- lr_crit <- NA_real_; verdict <- "-- baseline --"
      if (ord != "(1,1)") {
        base <- logacd2_fits[[nm]]
        if (is.null(base)) {
          verdict <- "no (1,1) baseline -- LR not computable"
        } else {
          lr      <- 2 * (ll - gof(base, "LogLikelihood"))
          lr_crit <- logacd2_order_crit[[ord]]
          verdict <- ifelse(lr > lr_crit, "sig. better than (1,1)", "NOT sig. better than (1,1)")
        }
      }
      data.table(asset = nm, order = ord, k = logacd2_order_k[[ord]],
                 logLik = round(ll, 1), AIC = round(gof(f, "AIC"), 1), BIC = round(gof(f, "BIC"), 1),
                 persist_log_scale = round(logacd2_persist_of(f), 4), LB_resid = round(lb15(f), 1),
                 LR = round(lr, 2), LR_crit = lr_crit, verdict = verdict)
    }, error = function(e) {
      cat(sprintf("  [%s %s] grid-row error: %s\n", nm, ord, conditionMessage(e)))
      NULL
    })

    if (is.null(row) || !is.finite(row$logLik)) return(na_row("converged but degenerate (non-finite fit)"))
    row
  }))
}))

for (nm in names(split_sets)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n=== LACD2 ORDER SELECTION GRID: %s ===\n\n", nm))
  sub <- logacd2_order_grid[asset == nm]
  print(sub, row.names = FALSE)
  if (all(is.finite(sub$AIC))) {
    cat(sprintf("  Best by AIC: %s | Best by BIC: %s\n",
                sub$order[which.min(sub$AIC)], sub$order[which.min(sub$BIC)]))
  }
}

```

```{r logacd2-order-full-table}

logacd2_full_row <- function(nm, ord, f) {
  na_row <- function(verdict, n = NA_integer_)
    data.table(
      asset = nm, order = ord, n = n, omega = NA_real_,
      alpha1 = NA_real_, alpha2 = NA_real_, beta1 = NA_real_, beta2 = NA_real_,
      persist_log_scale = NA_real_, logLik = NA_real_, AIC = NA_real_, BIC = NA_real_,
      mean_resid = NA_real_, mean_resid_z = NA_real_, sd_resid = NA_real_,
      disp_stat = NA_real_, exponential = NA_character_,
      LB_resid = NA_real_, LB_resid_p = NA_real_, LB_resid_sq = NA_real_, LB_resid_sq_p = NA_real_,
      verdict = verdict)

  if (is.null(f)) return(na_row(if (ord == "(1,1)") "FAILED to converge" else "SKIPPED (no (1,1) baseline to seed from, or failed itself)"))
  p <- f$mPara
  e <- as.numeric(f$residuals); e <- e[is.finite(e) & e > 0]; n <- length(e)
  if (n <= LB_LAGS) return(na_row("degenerate (too few finite residuals for LB)", n = n))

  lb1_t <- Box.test(e,   lag = LB_LAGS, type = "Ljung-Box")
  lb2_t <- Box.test(e^2, lag = LB_LAGS, type = "Ljung-Box")
  s2 <- var(e); sig_u <- sd((e - 1)^2); disp <- sqrt(n) * (s2 - 1) / sig_u

  data.table(
    asset = nm, order = ord, n = n,
    omega  = round(unname(p["omega"]), 5),
    alpha1 = round(unname(p["alpha1"]), 4),
    alpha2 = if ("alpha2" %in% names(p)) round(unname(p["alpha2"]), 4) else NA_real_,
    beta1  = round(unname(p["beta1"]), 4),
    beta2  = if ("beta2" %in% names(p)) round(unname(p["beta2"]), 4) else NA_real_,
    persist_log_scale = round(logacd2_persist_of(f), 4),
    logLik = round(gof(f, "LogLikelihood"), 1), AIC = round(gof(f, "AIC"), 1), BIC = round(gof(f, "BIC"), 1),
    mean_resid = round(mean(e), 4), mean_resid_z = round(resid_mean_z(e), 1), sd_resid = round(sd(e), 4),
    disp_stat = round(disp, 1), exponential = ifelse(abs(disp) > 1.96, "REJECTED", "not rejected"),
    LB_resid = round(unname(lb1_t$statistic), 1), LB_resid_p = signif(lb1_t$p.value, 3),
    LB_resid_sq = round(unname(lb2_t$statistic), 1), LB_resid_sq_p = signif(lb2_t$p.value, 3),
    verdict = "ok"
  )
}

logacd2_full_tbl <- rbindlist(lapply(names(logacd2_order_fits), function(ord)
  rbindlist(lapply(names(split_sets), function(nm)
    logacd2_full_row(nm, ord, logacd2_order_fits[[ord]][[nm]])))), fill = TRUE)

cat("=== LACD2, ALL FOUR ORDERS: parameters, AIC/BIC, residual diagnostics ===\n\n")
print(logacd2_full_tbl, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r qq-lacd2-selected-specs}
  print(
    ggplot(qq_winner_data, aes(x = theoretical, y = sample)) +
      geom_point(size = 0.6, alpha = 0.4, colour = "darkgreen") +
      geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
      facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free", ncol = 2) +
      labs(title    = "Selected specifications: LACD2(2,2) for BTCUSDT and NVDA -- does the QQ fit actually support these as the chosen models?",
           subtitle = "This document's own recommendation (sim_winner, Section 11)",
           x = "Theoretical quantile", y = "Empirical (sample) quantile") +
      theme_minimal()
  )

  cat("\n=== Quantitative fit check: LACD2(2,2), BTCUSDT/NVDA ===\n\n")
  print(qq_winner_quality[, .(asset, order, R2, slope, intercept, max_abs_dev)], row.names = FALSE)

  cat("\nREADING IT: slope~1, intercept~0, R2 close to 1 = points sit\n")
  cat("essentially on the 45-degree line = good fit. Compare directly against\n")
  cat("each asset's row in the LACD2 per-model QQ plot above: this panel is\n")
  cat("that exact (asset, order) cell, pulled out and quantified on its own.\n")
} else {
  cat("Neither selected specification had a converged fit to check.\n")
}
```

```{r}
suppressMessages({ library(data.table); library(ggplot2) })

dens_specs <- list(
  list(label = "LACD(2,2) -- GBP/USD", f = logacd2_order_fits[["(2,2)"]][["GBP/USD"]], dist = "exponential"),
  list(label = "LACD(2,2) -- BTCUSDT", f = logacd2_order_fits[["(2,2)"]][["BTCUSDT"]], dist = "exponential"),
  list(label = "LACD(2,2) -- NVDA",    f = logacd2_order_fits[["(2,2)"]][["NVDA"]],    dist = "exponential")
)

# Empirical residuals, trimmed at the 99th percentile per spec (a few
# extreme residuals otherwise squash the histogram's x-axis and hide the
# body of the distribution, which is what this plot is meant to show).
dens_plot_dat <- rbindlist(lapply(dens_specs, function(s) {
  if (is.null(s$f)) { cat(sprintf("%s: NO CONVERGED FIT -- skipped.\n", s$label)); return(NULL) }
  e <- as.numeric(s$f$residuals); e <- e[is.finite(e) & e > 0]
  cap <- quantile(e, 0.99, names = FALSE)
  data.table(panel = s$label, resid = e[e <= cap])
}))

# Theoretical density curve, same distribution/params each fit actually used.
dens_curve_dat <- rbindlist(lapply(dens_specs, function(s) {
  if (is.null(s$f)) return(NULL)
  e <- as.numeric(s$f$residuals); e <- e[is.finite(e) & e > 0]
  cap <- quantile(e, 0.99, names = FALSE)
  xs <- seq(0.001, cap, length.out = 300)
  ys <- if (s$dist == "weibull") {
    gam <- unname(s$f$dPara["gamma"])
    dweibull(xs, shape = gam, scale = 1 / gamma(1 + 1 / gam))   # forceErrExpec: E[eps]=1
  } else {
    dexp(xs, rate = 1)
  }
  data.table(panel = s$label, x = xs, y = ys)
}))

ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(data = dens_plot_dat, aes(x = resid, y = after_stat(density)),
                  bins = 60, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(data = dens_curve_dat, aes(x = x, y = y), colour = "red", linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  labs(title    = "Density overlay: standardised residuals vs theoretical distribution",
       subtitle = "Histogram = empirical eps_hat (trimmed at 99th pct); red = theoretical density (Exp(1) or Weibull(gamma_hat))",
       x = "Standardised residual (eps_hat = x / psi_hat)", y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Simulation: does the winning model reproduce the real process?

Fitting well by AIC/LB15 is a summary statistic, not proof a model can
*generate* data that looks like the real thing -- and for a model whose
persistence is at or above 1, it is not proof it can generate data at all
over a long horizon. An unbroken forward simulation with persistence >= 1
diverges almost surely; this is a property of the fitted process, not an
implementation gap. WACD(2,2)'s AIC-best pick for BTCUSDT (persistence
1.020) and EACD(2,2)'s for NVDA (persistence 1.003) both diverged to `Inf`
within a few hundred steps when stress-tested against the real fitted
parameters, while GBP/USD's WACD(2,2) (persistence 0.999) stayed bounded
indefinitely.

So the per-asset pick used for simulation is **not** always the AIC-best
model on the ladder. GBP/USD keeps WACD(2,2) -- already stable. BTCUSDT and
NVDA switch to **LACD1(1,1)**, the one already-fitted model for each of
them with persistence genuinely below 1 (|beta1|: BTCUSDT 0.802, NVDA
0.858 -- `logacd-table` above). This is a real trade, not a free upgrade:
LACD1(1,1)'s AIC is substantially worse than the (2,2) picks for both
assets (BTCUSDT 5,795,254 vs 1,487,136; NVDA 2,997,735 vs 2,572,748) --
the price of a process that can be run forward at all is accepting a
worse-fitting one. Log-ACD's log-linear recursion has a second convenient
property for this purpose beyond stationarity: `psi = exp(log psi)` is
positive by construction, so unlike the linear (2,2) recursion it needs no
explicit non-negativity guard.

Each winning model's own fitted recursion and innovation distribution
generates a fresh duration path forward from a TRAIN-tail seed, for as
many steps as TRAIN itself had (TEST is TEST_DAYS = 5 days now, comparable
in scale to the 14-day TRAIN window rather than the whole remaining sample
-- ample steps either way for stable quantile/ACF estimates, and
simulation length no longer depends on how TEST_DAYS is set). The
simulated path never sees a single real duration from either TRAIN or
TEST; it is generated purely from the fitted parameters and freshly drawn
innovations. Distance between the simulated and real TEST distributions is
measured two ways -- MAE/RMSE between matched duration quantiles (does the
marginal shape match?) and MAE/RMSE between matched ACF lags (does the
dependence structure match?) -- rather than a one-step-ahead comparison,
since a full stochastic simulation has no real per-observation match to
compare against.

```{r sim-vs-real-setup}
# =============================================================================
#  Four forward-simulation recursions, dispatched by model kind:
#
#  simulate_acd22(): linear order-(2,2) recursion (GBP/USD's WACD(2,2)).
#  x_i AND psi_i are BOTH generated going forward -- unlike the one-step-
#  ahead prediction later in this doc (pred_tbl), which recomputes psi from
#  REAL past x's. alpha2/beta2 are NEGATIVE for the WACD fit, a real risk
#  of driving simulated psi negative that an order-1 recursion never faces,
#  hence the explicit guard inside the loop.
#
#  simulate_lacd2_22(): log-linear order-(2,2) recursion (BTCUSDT/NVDA's
#  actual pick, LACD2(2,2)) -- alpha multiplies RAW eps_i-j (not logged),
#  beta multiplies log(psi_i-j), matching logacd2-order-selection's own
#  model. psi = exp(log psi) is positive by construction, so no negativity
#  guard is needed the way simulate_acd22() needs one -- but unlike
#  order-(1,1) (a simple, always-stable-if-|beta1|<1 AR(1) on log-psi),
#  order-(2,2)'s stability is an AR(2) question: beta1+beta2 < 1 is
#  necessary but NOT sufficient for the characteristic roots of
#  1 - beta1*z - beta2*z^2 to lie outside the unit circle. `cap` and
#  `diverged_at` below are the actual safety net, not the beta1+beta2
#  figure alone -- read a diverged row as informative, not a bug, exactly
#  as simulate_acd22()'s own guard is read for GBP/USD.
#
#  simulate_lacd1_22()/simulate_lacd1(): LACD1's own (2,2)/(1,1) recursions,
#  kept defined and available (not currently the winning pick for any
#  asset via sim_winner, but used directly by lacd1-sim-setup below for the
#  head-to-head LACD1-vs-LACD2 comparison, and a straight swap in
#  sim_winner if LACD2(2,2) turns out unusable for a given asset).
#
#  wacd22_fits/logacd_fits/logacd22_fits/logacd2_22_fits are defined earlier
#  in the doc but, like every other model object here, only live in THIS
#  session if that chunk has already run -- so fall back to the on-disk
#  cache if any is missing, same reasoning as the Log-ACD chunks' own
#  cache-load fix.
#
#  ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  SIMULATION DESIGN -- corrected out-of-sample procedure:
#
#  INITIALISE from the END OF TRAIN, don't hold it FIXED: x_seed is the
#  last (1 or 2, matching recursion order) TRAIN adjDur value(s), and
#  psi_seed is the model's own LAST FITTED TRAIN conditional mean(s)
#  (f$muHats, the same exp-scale psi every ACDm model family exposes --
#  wacd-prediction-accuracy-1day already uses this exact convention for its
#  own one-step-ahead recursion). These are genuinely different numbers from
#  the crude TRAIN mean unless psi has already converged to its
#  unconditional mean by the end of TRAIN. Critically, x_seed/psi_seed are
#  used ONLY to seed step 1 -- from there the recursion is fully
#  self-referential: psi_i depends on the PREVIOUSLY SIMULATED x_{i-1}/
#  psi_{i-1} (simulate_acd22()/simulate_lacd1_22()/simulate_lacd2_22()/
#  simulate_lacd1(), unchanged below), never on a value held fixed across
#  the whole path -- the correction this design implements is precisely
#  "initial condition, not constant conditional mean".
#
#  LENGTH: each path runs for exactly length(TEST) steps (not TRAIN length,
#  as an earlier version of this chunk did) -- a direct counterfactual for
#  the actual TEST period, not just a long free-running draw for stable
#  quantile estimates (eacd-simulate/wacd-simulate already provide that,
#  separately, as an in-sample stationary-distribution check).
#
#  REPLICATIONS: B independent paths, not one -- a single simulated path is
#  one random draw of the innovations; judging an observed TEST statistic
#  against ONE draw conflates genuine model misfit with ordinary sampling
#  variation. The DISTRIBUTION across B paths is the actual comparison
#  target (sim-vs-real-distance below).
#
#  CHOOSING B: bounded above by runtime (B forward passes of length
#  length(TEST) each, O(n) per pass -- cheap) and below by how much Monte
#  Carlo noise is tolerable in the resulting interval. B=200 keeps a 95%
#  simulated interval's own coverage accurate to roughly +-3 percentage
#  points (SE of a proportion ~ sqrt(0.5*0.5/200) ~ 3.5%) -- adequate for a
#  clean "does the observed value sit inside or outside the interval"
#  reading. Raise to 500-1000 for a smoother pooled density plot or a finer
#  Monte Carlo p-value (resolution 1/B); there is no formal minimum, only a
#  precision-vs-runtime trade-off, and this is deliberately far below the
#  SIM_N used for the (unrelated) in-sample stationary check, since each
#  path here is only length(TEST) long, not a full stationary-distribution
#  draw.
#
#  RAW-SCALE COMPARISON: the model is fitted on adjDur, but the comparison
#  target (observed TEST durations) is on the raw scale, so every simulated
#  path is converted back via x_raw_sim(t) = s(t) * x_adj_sim(t), using
#  te_dt$factor -- the EXACT s(t_i) that TEST row's own adjDur was divided
#  by (split-attach-adjdur's merge, applied identically to TRAIN and TEST),
#  not a separately-recomputed approximation.
# =============================================================================
if (!exists("wacd22_fits", inherits = FALSE) && file.exists(MODEL_CACHE_FILE)) {
  wacd22_fits <- readRDS(MODEL_CACHE_FILE)$wacd22_fits
}
if (!exists("logacd_fits", inherits = FALSE) && file.exists(MODEL_CACHE_FILE)) {
  logacd_fits <- readRDS(MODEL_CACHE_FILE)$logacd_fits
}
if (!exists("logacd22_fits", inherits = FALSE) && file.exists(MODEL_CACHE_FILE)) {
  logacd22_fits <- readRDS(MODEL_CACHE_FILE)$logacd22_fits
}
if (!exists("logacd2_22_fits", inherits = FALSE) && file.exists(MODEL_CACHE_FILE)) {
  logacd2_22_fits <- readRDS(MODEL_CACHE_FILE)$logacd2_22_fits
}

simulate_acd22 <- function(eps, w, a1, a2, b1, b2, x_seed, psi_seed, cap) {
  n <- length(eps)
  x <- numeric(n); psi <- numeric(n)
  x[1:2]   <- x_seed
  psi[1:2] <- psi_seed
  diverged_at <- NA_integer_
  for (i in 3:n) {
    psi[i] <- w + a1 * x[i - 1] + a2 * x[i - 2] + b1 * psi[i - 1] + b2 * psi[i - 2]
    if (!is.finite(psi[i]) || psi[i] <= 0) psi[i] <- .Machine$double.eps
    x[i] <- psi[i] * eps[i]
    if (!is.finite(x[i]) || x[i] > cap) { diverged_at <- i; break }
  }
  if (!is.na(diverged_at)) x <- x[1:(diverged_at - 1)]
  list(x = x, diverged_at = diverged_at)
}

simulate_lacd1 <- function(eps, w, a, b, x_seed1, psi_seed1, cap) {
  n <- length(eps)
  x <- numeric(n); lp <- numeric(n)
  x[1]  <- x_seed1
  lp[1] <- log(psi_seed1)
  diverged_at <- NA_integer_
  for (i in 2:n) {
    log_eps_prev <- log(x[i - 1]) - lp[i - 1]           # log(eps_i-1) = log(x_i-1) - log(psi_i-1)
    lp[i]  <- w + a * log_eps_prev + b * lp[i - 1]
    psi_i  <- exp(lp[i])
    x[i]   <- psi_i * eps[i]
    if (!is.finite(x[i]) || x[i] > cap) { diverged_at <- i; break }
  }
  if (!is.na(diverged_at)) x <- x[1:(diverged_at - 1)]
  list(x = x, diverged_at = diverged_at)
}

# Order-(2,2) generalisation of simulate_lacd1() -- same log(eps_i-j) =
# log(x_i-j) - log(psi_i-j) reconstruction, now summed over two lags each
# for alpha and beta. psi_i checked for finiteness BEFORE computing x[i]
# (unlike the (1,1) version, where a stable AR(1) makes that redundant) --
# an unstable AR(2) root can drive lp[i] to +-Inf, and exp(Inf) then
# log(Inf)-Inf on the NEXT step would produce NaN silently rather than
# tripping the cap check the way a merely-large-but-finite value does.
simulate_lacd1_22 <- function(eps, w, a1, a2, b1, b2, x_seed, psi_seed, cap) {
  n <- length(eps)
  x <- numeric(n); lp <- numeric(n)
  x[1:2]  <- x_seed
  lp[1:2] <- log(psi_seed)
  diverged_at <- NA_integer_
  for (i in 3:n) {
    log_eps1 <- log(x[i - 1]) - lp[i - 1]
    log_eps2 <- log(x[i - 2]) - lp[i - 2]
    lp[i]  <- w + a1 * log_eps1 + a2 * log_eps2 + b1 * lp[i - 1] + b2 * lp[i - 2]
    psi_i  <- exp(lp[i])
    if (!is.finite(psi_i)) { diverged_at <- i; break }
    x[i] <- psi_i * eps[i]
    if (!is.finite(x[i]) || x[i] > cap) { diverged_at <- i; break }
  }
  if (!is.na(diverged_at)) x <- x[1:(diverged_at - 1)]
  list(x = x, diverged_at = diverged_at)
}

# LACD2(2,2): same log-psi state and same AR(2)-stability caveat as
# simulate_lacd1_22(), but the shock term is RAW eps_i-j (not logged) --
# eps_i-1 reconstructed as x_i-1/psi_i-1 (the un-logged analogue of
# simulate_lacd1_22's log(x)-log(psi)), matching logacd2-order-selection's
# own model = omega + alpha*eps_i-j + beta*log(psi_i-j).
simulate_lacd2_22 <- function(eps, w, a1, a2, b1, b2, x_seed, psi_seed, cap) {
  n <- length(eps)
  x <- numeric(n); lp <- numeric(n)
  x[1:2]  <- x_seed
  lp[1:2] <- log(psi_seed)
  diverged_at <- NA_integer_
  for (i in 3:n) {
    eps1 <- x[i - 1] / exp(lp[i - 1])
    eps2 <- x[i - 2] / exp(lp[i - 2])
    lp[i]  <- w + a1 * eps1 + a2 * eps2 + b1 * lp[i - 1] + b2 * lp[i - 2]
    psi_i  <- exp(lp[i])
    if (!is.finite(psi_i)) { diverged_at <- i; break }
    x[i] <- psi_i * eps[i]
    if (!is.finite(x[i]) || x[i] > cap) { diverged_at <- i; break }
  }
  if (!is.na(diverged_at)) x <- x[1:(diverged_at - 1)]
  list(x = x, diverged_at = diverged_at)
}

sim_winner <- list(                               # the per-asset picks argued for above
  "GBP/USD" = list(fits = "wacd22_fits",    kind = "linear22", dist = "weibull",     label = "WACD(2,2)"),
  "BTCUSDT" = list(fits = "logacd2_22_fits", kind = "lacd2_22", dist = "exponential", label = "LACD2(2,2)"),
  "NVDA"    = list(fits = "logacd2_22_fits", kind = "lacd2_22", dist = "exponential", label = "LACD2(2,2)")
)

SIM_B <- 100   # replications per asset -- see this chunk's own header note for how this was chosen

# Shared by every simulate-vs-real comparison in this document (sim_winner's
# picks below, AND lacd1-sim-setup's head-to-head LACD1(2,2) comparison) --
# one function, not a near-duplicate copy, so both stay consistent by
# construction. kind in {"linear22","lacd1_22","lacd2_22","lacd1"}.
sim_vs_real_one <- function(nm, f, kind, dist, label, B = SIM_B) {
  if (is.null(f)) { cat(sprintf("%s: %s not fitted -- skipped.\n", nm, label)); return(NULL) }

  ord <- if (kind == "lacd1") 1L else 2L

  tr <- split_sets[[nm]]$train$adjDur; tr <- tr[is.finite(tr) & tr > 0]

  te_dt <- split_sets[[nm]]$test[is.finite(adjDur) & adjDur > 0 & is.finite(duration) & duration > 0]
  setorder(te_dt, time)
  n_sim <- nrow(te_dt)   # TEST length -- each path is a direct counterfactual for the TEST period

  # ---- initial state: LAST TRAIN observation(s) and LAST FITTED TRAIN
  # psi(s) -- see this chunk's own header note for why f$muHats, not
  # mean(tr). tail() on both preserves chronological order (older, newer),
  # matching simulate_*()'s own x[1:2]/psi[1:2] seeding convention.
  have_muhats <- !is.null(f$muHats) && length(f$muHats) >= ord
  psi_seed <- if (have_muhats) tail(as.numeric(f$muHats), ord) else rep(mean(tr), ord)
  x_seed   <- tail(tr, ord)

  p   <- f$mPara
  cap <- 1000 * mean(tr)

  # ---- B independent forward paths, each n_sim steps, EACH started from
  # the SAME last-train state (see header note: distribution across paths,
  # not one draw, is the actual comparison target).
  sim_paths_adj <- vector("list", B)
  n_diverged <- 0L
  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    eps <- if (dist == "weibull") {
      gam <- unname(f$dPara["gamma"])
      rweibull(n_sim, shape = gam, scale = 1 / gamma(1 + 1 / gam))   # forceErrExpec: E[eps]=1
    } else {
      rexp(n_sim)                                                   # Exp(1)
    }

    sim_out <- switch(kind,
      "linear22" = simulate_acd22(eps, unname(p["omega"]), unname(p["alpha1"]), unname(p["alpha2"]),
                                   unname(p["beta1"]), unname(p["beta2"]), x_seed, psi_seed, cap),
      "lacd1_22" = simulate_lacd1_22(eps, unname(p["omega"]), unname(p["alpha1"]), unname(p["alpha2"]),
                                      unname(p["beta1"]), unname(p["beta2"]), x_seed, psi_seed, cap),
      "lacd2_22" = simulate_lacd2_22(eps, unname(p["omega"]), unname(p["alpha1"]), unname(p["alpha2"]),
                                      unname(p["beta1"]), unname(p["beta2"]), x_seed, psi_seed, cap),
      "lacd1"    = simulate_lacd1(eps, unname(p["omega"]), unname(p["alpha1"]), unname(p["beta1"]),
                                   x_seed, psi_seed, cap)
    )
    if (!is.na(sim_out$diverged_at)) n_diverged <- n_diverged + 1L
    x_adj <- sim_out$x
    length(x_adj) <- n_sim   # pad a diverged path with NA so every path aligns 1:1 to the same
                             # TEST timestamps for the raw-scale conversion below
    sim_paths_adj[[b]] <- x_adj
  }

  if (n_diverged > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("%-8s: %d of %d %s paths diverged before reaching TEST length (%s steps).\n",
                nm, n_diverged, B, label, format(n_sim, big.mark = ",")))
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("%-8s: %d paths x %s steps simulated from %s (TEST length matched, seeded from last TRAIN x/psi).\n",
                nm, B, format(n_sim, big.mark = ","), label))
  }

  # ---- undo the diurnal adjustment: x_raw_sim(t) = s(t) * x_adj_sim(t) ----
  sim_paths_raw <- lapply(sim_paths_adj, function(x_adj) x_adj * te_dt$factor)

  list(sim_raw = sim_paths_raw, real_raw = te_dt$duration,
       sim_adj = sim_paths_adj, real_adj = te_dt$adjDur,
       model = label, n_diverged = n_diverged, B = B)
}

set.seed(42)
sim_results <- setNames(lapply(names(split_sets), function(nm) {
  win  <- sim_winner[[nm]]
  fits <- get(win$fits)                           # inherits=TRUE (default): lives in the calling scope,
  f    <- fits[[nm]]
  sim_vs_real_one(nm, f, win$kind, win$dist, win$label)
}), names(split_sets))

# ---- Homogeneous Poisson (rung 1) baseline, same B/length(TEST) design as
# sim_vs_real_one() above, but genuinely different: i.i.d. Exp(lambda_hat)
# draws, NO recursion, NO dependence on x_seed/psi_seed at all -- that is
# the entire point of this baseline. It does NOT go through
# sim_vs_real_one()'s switch(kind, ...) because Poisson has no acdFit()
# object at all (no mPara/dPara/muHats) -- only lambda_hat, calibrated on
# TRAIN adjDur exactly as poisson-calibrate does (1/mean(TRAIN adjDur)).
# Shares SIM_B with sim_results above, so changing SIM_B updates both.
sim_poisson_one <- function(nm, B = SIM_B) {
  tr <- split_sets[[nm]]$train$adjDur; tr <- tr[is.finite(tr) & tr > 0]
  lambda_hat <- 1 / mean(tr)

  te_dt <- split_sets[[nm]]$test[is.finite(adjDur) & adjDur > 0 & is.finite(duration) & duration > 0]
  setorder(te_dt, time)
  n_sim <- nrow(te_dt)

  sim_paths_adj <- lapply(seq_len(B), function(b) rexp(n_sim, rate = lambda_hat))
  sim_paths_raw <- lapply(sim_paths_adj, function(x_adj) x_adj * te_dt$factor)

  cat(sprintf("%-8s: %d paths x %s steps simulated from Homogeneous Poisson (lambda_hat=%.4f).\n",
              nm, B, format(n_sim, big.mark = ","), lambda_hat))

  list(sim_raw = sim_paths_raw, real_raw = te_dt$duration,
       sim_adj = sim_paths_adj, real_adj = te_dt$adjDur,
       model = "Homogeneous Poisson", n_diverged = 0L, B = B)
}

set.seed(5872)   # poisson-calibrate's own seed, kept separate from sim_results' set.seed(42)
sim_results_poisson <- setNames(lapply(names(split_sets), sim_poisson_one), names(split_sets))
```
```{r}
sim_dist_tbl_poisson  <- rbindlist(lapply(names(sim_results_poisson), function(nm) {
  r <- sim_results_poisson[[nm]]
  path_stats <- rbindlist(lapply(r$sim_raw, function(x) as.list(path_stats_one(x))), fill = TRUE)
  obs <- path_stats_one(r$real_raw)
  rbindlist(lapply(names(obs), function(s) {
    v <- path_stats[[s]]; v <- v[is.finite(v)]
    lo <- quantile(v, 0.025, names = FALSE); hi <- quantile(v, 0.975, names = FALSE)
    data.table(asset = nm, model = r$model, stat = s, observed = round(unname(obs[s]), 4),
               sim_mean = round(mean(v), 4), sim_p2.5 = round(lo, 4), sim_p97.5 = round(hi, 4),
               in_95pct_interval = unname(obs[s]) >= lo & unname(obs[s]) <= hi)
  }))
}))
print(sim_dist_tbl_poisson)
print(plot_sim_density(sim_results_poisson, " -- Homogeneous Poisson"))
print(plot_sim_acf(sim_results_poisson,     " -- Homogeneous Poisson"))

```
```{r}

# ---- Shape/dependence distance for Poisson, mean-of-B-paths vs observed ----
# Same construction as sim-vs-real-distance's own sim_shape_tbl (mean
# quantile curve and mean per-path-then-averaged ACF across the B paths,
# compared against observed TEST) -- just applied to sim_results_poisson
# instead of sim_results. Needs sim_mae()/sim_rmse()/sim_q_probs already
# defined in sim-vs-real-distance.

sim_shape_tbl_poisson <- rbindlist(lapply(names(sim_results_poisson), function(nm) {
  r <- sim_results_poisson[[nm]]
  if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
  valid_paths <- Filter(function(x) sum(is.finite(x) & x > 0) >= LB_LAGS * 4, r$sim_raw)
  if (length(valid_paths) == 0) {
    return(data.table(asset = nm, model = r$model, quantile_MAE = NA_real_, quantile_RMSE = NA_real_,
                       acf_MAE = NA_real_, acf_RMSE = NA_real_))
  }
  q_sim_mat <- sapply(valid_paths, function(x) quantile(x[is.finite(x) & x > 0], sim_q_probs, names = FALSE))
  a_sim_mat <- sapply(valid_paths, function(x)
    as.numeric(acf(x[is.finite(x) & x > 0], lag.max = LB_LAGS, plot = FALSE)$acf)[-1])
  q_sim <- rowMeans(q_sim_mat)   # mean quantile curve across B paths
  a_sim <- rowMeans(a_sim_mat)   # per-path ACF, THEN averaged across paths
  q_re  <- quantile(r$real_raw, sim_q_probs, names = FALSE)
  a_re  <- as.numeric(acf(r$real_raw, lag.max = LB_LAGS, plot = FALSE)$acf)[-1]
  data.table(asset = nm, model = r$model,
             quantile_MAE  = round(sim_mae(q_sim, q_re), 4), quantile_RMSE = round(sim_rmse(q_sim, q_re), 4),
             acf_MAE       = round(sim_mae(a_sim, a_re), 4), acf_RMSE      = round(sim_rmse(a_sim, a_re), 4))
}))
```

```{r sim-vs-real-distance}
# =============================================================================
#  Two comparisons, both now built on B independent TEST-length paths (see
#  sim-vs-real-setup's own header note) and on the RAW duration scale:
#
#    1. SUMMARY-STATISTIC DISTRIBUTION: mean/sd/CV/ACF(1,5,10) computed
#       INDEPENDENTLY on each of the B simulated paths, giving a simulated
#       DISTRIBUTION for each statistic (sim_mean, and a 95% interval
#       [sim_p2.5, sim_p97.5]) to compare the SINGLE observed TEST value
#       against -- in_95pct_interval flags whether the model's own simulated
#       TEST-period behaviour is consistent with what was actually observed.
#       This is the direct implementation of "compare against the
#       distribution of simulated outcomes", not a single point estimate.
#
#    2. SHAPE/DEPENDENCE DISTANCE: quantile_MAE/RMSE (99 percentiles, mean
#       curve across the B paths, vs the observed TEST quantile curve -- does
#       the simulated MARGINAL distribution have the right shape?) and
#       acf_MAE/RMSE (lags 1-LB_LAGS, same lag convention as every
#       Ljung-Box test elsewhere in this document -- does the simulated
#       DEPENDENCE structure match?). The mean ACF is computed PER PATH,
#       THEN averaged across paths -- never on the B paths concatenated into
#       one long series, which would introduce spurious breaks at every
#       path boundary and distort the estimate.
#
#  The earlier plain (position-by-position) MAE/RMSE is dropped: with B
#  independent TEST-length paths there is even less of a genuine per-event
#  pairing to exploit than the single-path version had, and the two
#  comparisons above already isolate shape and dependence distance without
#  that noise.
# =============================================================================
if (!exists("sim_mae", inherits = FALSE)) {
  sim_mae  <- function(a, b) mean(abs(a - b))
  sim_rmse <- function(a, b) sqrt(mean((a - b) ^ 2))
}
sim_q_probs <- seq(0.01, 0.99, by = 0.01)
sim_acf_lags_report <- c(1, 5, 10)

# One path's worth of summary statistics -- reused for every simulated path
# AND for the single observed TEST series below.
path_stats_one <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x) & x > 0]
  if (length(x) < LB_LAGS * 4) return(NULL)
  ac <- acf(x, lag.max = max(sim_acf_lags_report), plot = FALSE)$acf
  c(mean = mean(x), sd = sd(x), cv = sd(x) / mean(x),
    setNames(ac[sim_acf_lags_report + 1], paste0("acf", sim_acf_lags_report)))
}

# ---- 1. Summary-statistic distribution: observed vs simulated interval ----
sim_dist_tbl <- rbindlist(lapply(names(sim_results), function(nm) {
  r <- sim_results[[nm]]
  if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)

  path_stats <- rbindlist(lapply(r$sim_raw, function(x) as.list(path_stats_one(x))), fill = TRUE)
  obs <- path_stats_one(r$real_raw)
  if (is.null(obs) || nrow(path_stats) == 0) return(NULL)

  rbindlist(lapply(names(obs), function(s) {
    v <- path_stats[[s]]; v <- v[is.finite(v)]
    lo <- quantile(v, 0.025, names = FALSE); hi <- quantile(v, 0.975, names = FALSE)
    data.table(asset = nm, model = r$model, B = r$B, n_diverged = r$n_diverged, stat = s,
               observed = round(unname(obs[s]), 4),
               sim_mean = round(mean(v), 4), sim_p2.5 = round(lo, 4), sim_p97.5 = round(hi, 4),
               in_95pct_interval = unname(obs[s]) >= lo & unname(obs[s]) <= hi)
  }))
}))

cat("=== SIMULATED (B paths, TEST length, seeded from last TRAIN x/psi) vs OBSERVED TEST: SUMMARY STATISTICS ===\n\n")
print(sim_dist_tbl)
cat("\nREADING IT: sim_mean/sim_p2.5/sim_p97.5 summarise the SAME statistic\n")
cat("computed independently on each of B simulated paths (each exactly\n")
cat("length(TEST) steps, raw scale, all seeded from the same last-TRAIN\n")
cat("state). observed inside [sim_p2.5, sim_p97.5] (in_95pct_interval = TRUE)\n")
cat("means the fitted model's own simulated TEST-period behaviour is\n")
cat("consistent with what actually happened, at the 95% level; FALSE flags a\n")
cat("statistic the model systematically misses.\n")

# ---- 2. Shape/dependence distance: mean-of-B-paths vs observed -----------
sim_shape_tbl <- rbindlist(lapply(names(sim_results), function(nm) {
  r <- sim_results[[nm]]
  if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
  valid_paths <- Filter(function(x) sum(is.finite(x) & x > 0) >= LB_LAGS * 4, r$sim_raw)
  if (length(valid_paths) == 0) {
    return(data.table(asset = nm, model = r$model, quantile_MAE = NA_real_, quantile_RMSE = NA_real_,
                       acf_MAE = NA_real_, acf_RMSE = NA_real_))
  }
  q_sim_mat <- sapply(valid_paths, function(x) quantile(x[is.finite(x) & x > 0], sim_q_probs, names = FALSE))
  a_sim_mat <- sapply(valid_paths, function(x)
    as.numeric(acf(x[is.finite(x) & x > 0], lag.max = LB_LAGS, plot = FALSE)$acf)[-1])
  q_sim <- rowMeans(q_sim_mat)   # mean quantile curve across B paths
  a_sim <- rowMeans(a_sim_mat)   # per-path ACF, THEN averaged across paths -- see header note
  q_re  <- quantile(r$real_raw, sim_q_probs, names = FALSE)
  a_re  <- as.numeric(acf(r$real_raw, lag.max = LB_LAGS, plot = FALSE)$acf)[-1]
  data.table(asset = nm, model = r$model,
             quantile_MAE  = round(sim_mae(q_sim, q_re), 4), quantile_RMSE = round(sim_rmse(q_sim, q_re), 4),
             acf_MAE       = round(sim_mae(a_sim, a_re), 4), acf_RMSE      = round(sim_rmse(a_sim, a_re), 4))
} ))

cat("\n=== SHAPE/DEPENDENCE DISTANCE: mean-of-B-paths vs observed TEST ===\n\n")
print(sim_shape_tbl)
cat("\nREADING IT: quantile_MAE/RMSE compares the mean simulated quantile\n")
cat("curve (99 percentiles, averaged across B paths) against the observed\n")
cat("TEST quantile curve -- marginal SHAPE distance, in seconds, same units\n")
cat("as duration. acf_MAE/RMSE compares mean simulated ACF (unitless, in\n")
cat(sprintf("[-1,1], lags 1-%d, averaged PER-PATH then across paths) against\n", LB_LAGS))
cat("observed ACF -- dependence-structure distance. Small quantile distance\n")
cat("with large ACF distance means the model gets the marginal duration\n")
cat("distribution right but misstates real duration clustering, or vice\n")
cat("versa -- kept as separate columns rather than one combined score.\n")

if (any(sapply(sim_results, function(r) !is.null(r) && r$n_diverged > 0))) {
  cat("\nSome paths diverged before reaching TEST length -- n_diverged above\n")
  cat("counts how many of the B; see sim-vs-real-setup's own per-asset\n")
  cat("message. For a WACD(2,2) or order-1 pick this is unexpected (chosen\n")
  cat("for persistence < 1 and, for order-1, guaranteed AR(1) stability) and\n")
  cat("worth investigating. For a LACD1(2,2)/LACD2(2,2) pick it is NOT\n")
  cat("automatically a bug -- beta1+beta2 < 1 is necessary but not sufficient\n")
  cat("for AR(2) stability on the log-psi recursion, so some divergence is\n")
  cat("informative about that asset's own richer-order dynamics.\n")
}
```

```{r sim-vs-real-plot}
# =============================================================================
#  Visual companion to sim-vs-real-distance's own quantile_MAE/RMSE and
#  acf_MAE/RMSE numbers -- same "observed vs simulated" comparison
#  poisson-plot-dist already uses for rung 1 (log x-axis, density-scale
#  histogram overlay), reused here as a shared function so the LACD1(2,2)
#  simulation section below can call the identical plot without duplicating
#  it.
#
#  DENSITY plot addresses the quantile_MAE/RMSE question (right shape?);
#  ACF plot addresses the acf_MAE/RMSE question (right dependence
#  structure?) -- kept as two separate plots for the same reason the two
#  distance metrics are kept as separate columns rather than combined into
#  one score.
#
#  BTC/NVDA-scale caps (2e6 points) match poisson-plot-dist's own reasoning:
#  a plot with tens of millions of points renders nothing useful; the
#  numeric distance metrics already computed always use the full series.
# =============================================================================
plot_sim_density <- function(sim_results, title_suffix = "") {
  plot_dat <- rbindlist(lapply(names(sim_results), function(nm) {
    r <- sim_results[[nm]]
    if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
    d_sim <- unlist(r$sim_raw); d_sim <- d_sim[is.finite(d_sim) & d_sim > 0]   # pooled across all
                                                # B paths -- fine for a density/histogram (order
                                                # doesn't matter), unlike the ACF plot below
    d_re  <- r$real_raw[is.finite(r$real_raw) & r$real_raw > 0]
    if (length(d_sim) > 2e6) d_sim <- d_sim[sample.int(length(d_sim), 2e6)]
    if (length(d_re)  > 2e6) d_re  <- d_re[1:2e6]
    facet_lbl <- sprintf("%s -- %s", nm, r$model)
    rbindlist(list(
      data.table(asset = facet_lbl, source = "Observed (TEST)", duration = d_re),
      data.table(asset = facet_lbl, source = sprintf("Simulated (%d paths, pooled)", r$B), duration = d_sim)
    ))
  }))
  if (nrow(plot_dat) == 0) { cat("No simulated results to plot.\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }

  ggplot(plot_dat, aes(x = duration, fill = source)) +
    geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 60, position = "identity", alpha = 0.5) +
    scale_x_log10() +
    facet_wrap(~ asset, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
    labs(title    = paste0("Simulated vs real TEST durations", title_suffix),
         subtitle = "Log x-axis, density scale, RAW duration scale -- shape mismatch here is what quantile_MAE/RMSE quantify",
         x = "Duration, seconds (log scale)", y = "Density", fill = NULL) +
    theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")
}

plot_sim_acf <- function(sim_results, title_suffix = "") {
  acf_dat <- rbindlist(lapply(names(sim_results), function(nm) {
    r <- sim_results[[nm]]
    if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
    valid_paths <- Filter(function(x) sum(is.finite(x) & x > 0) >= LB_LAGS * 4, r$sim_raw)
    if (length(valid_paths) == 0) return(NULL)
    a_sim_mat <- sapply(valid_paths, function(x)
      as.numeric(acf(x[is.finite(x) & x > 0], lag.max = LB_LAGS, plot = FALSE)$acf)[-1])
    a_sim <- rowMeans(a_sim_mat)   # per-path ACF, THEN averaged -- see sim-vs-real-distance's own note
    a_re  <- as.numeric(acf(r$real_raw, lag.max = LB_LAGS, plot = FALSE)$acf)[-1]
    facet_lbl <- sprintf("%s -- %s", nm, r$model)
    rbindlist(list(
      data.table(asset = facet_lbl, source = "Observed (TEST)", lag = seq_along(a_re),  acf = a_re),
      data.table(asset = facet_lbl, source = sprintf("Simulated (mean of %d paths)", length(valid_paths)),
                 lag = seq_along(a_sim), acf = a_sim)
    ))
  }))
  if (nrow(acf_dat) == 0) { cat("No simulated results (with enough length) to plot ACF for.\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }

  ggplot(acf_dat, aes(x = lag, y = acf, colour = source)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(size = 1.2) +
    facet_wrap(~ asset, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
    labs(title    = paste0("ACF, simulated vs real TEST durations", title_suffix),
         subtitle = sprintf("Lags 1-%d, RAW duration scale -- dependence-structure mismatch here is what acf_MAE/RMSE quantify", LB_LAGS),
         x = "Lag", y = "ACF", colour = NULL) +
    theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")
}

print(plot_sim_density(sim_results, " -- sim_winner picks"))
print(plot_sim_acf(sim_results,     " -- sim_winner picks"))
```

### Simulation: LACD1(2,2) for BTCUSDT/NVDA

`sim-vs-real-setup`/`sim-vs-real-distance` above simulate `sim_winner`'s own
picks -- LACD2(2,2) for BTCUSDT/NVDA. This runs the identical forward
simulation and distributional-distance check for LACD1(2,2)
(`logacd22_fits`) on those same two assets instead, using
`simulate_lacd1_22()` already defined in `sim-vs-real-setup` above (built
there, unused by `sim_winner` since LACD2(2,2) was the pick that section
argues for) -- not a new recursion. GBP/USD is excluded: its own pick is
WACD(2,2), not a Log-ACD variant, so it has no LACD1-vs-LACD2 comparison to
make.

```{r lacd1-sim-setup}
# =============================================================================
#  Same simulation design as sim-vs-real-setup -- calls the identical
#  sim_vs_real_one() (B paths, TEST length, seeded from last TRAIN x and
#  last FITTED TRAIN psi, raw-scale conversion; see that chunk's own header
#  note) -- LACD1(2,2) in place of LACD2(2,2), same two assets. One shared
#  function, not a near-duplicate copy, so the two stay consistent by
#  construction.
# =============================================================================
lacd1_sim_assets <- intersect(c("BTCUSDT", "NVDA"), names(logacd22_fits))

set.seed(42)
sim_results_lacd1 <- setNames(lapply(lacd1_sim_assets, function(nm) {
  sim_vs_real_one(nm, logacd22_fits[[nm]], kind = "lacd1_22", dist = "exponential", label = "LACD1(2,2)")
}), lacd1_sim_assets)
```

```{r lacd1-sim-distance}
# =============================================================================

  sim_mae  <- function(a, b) mean(abs(a - b))

}
if (!exists("sim_q_probs", inherits = FALSE)) sim_q_probs <- seq(0.01, 0.99, by = 0.01)
if (!exists("sim_acf_lags_report", inherits = FALSE)) sim_acf_lags_report <- c(1, 5, 10)
if (!exists("path_stats_one", inherits = FALSE)) {
  path_stats_one <- function(x) {
    x <- x[is.finite(x) & x > 0]
    if (length(x) < LB_LAGS * 4) return(NULL)
    ac <- acf(x, lag.max = max(sim_acf_lags_report), plot = FALSE)$acf
    c(mean = mean(x), sd = sd(x), cv = sd(x) / mean(x),
      setNames(ac[sim_acf_lags_report + 1], paste0("acf", sim_acf_lags_report)))
  }
}

sim_dist_tbl_lacd1 <- rbindlist(lapply(names(sim_results_lacd1), function(nm) {
  r <- sim_results_lacd1[[nm]]
  if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
  path_stats <- rbindlist(lapply(r$sim_raw, function(x) as.list(path_stats_one(x))), fill = TRUE)
  obs <- path_stats_one(r$real_raw)
  if (is.null(obs) || nrow(path_stats) == 0) return(NULL)
  rbindlist(lapply(names(obs), function(s) {
    v <- path_stats[[s]]; v <- v[is.finite(v)]
    lo <- quantile(v, 0.025, names = FALSE); hi <- quantile(v, 0.975, names = FALSE)
    data.table(asset = nm, model = r$model, B = r$B, n_diverged = r$n_diverged, stat = s,
               observed = round(unname(obs[s]), 4),
               sim_mean = round(mean(v), 4), sim_p2.5 = round(lo, 4), sim_p97.5 = round(hi, 4),
               in_95pct_interval = unname(obs[s]) >= lo & unname(obs[s]) <= hi)
  }))
}))

sim_shape_tbl_lacd1 <- rbindlist(lapply(names(sim_results_lacd1), function(nm) {
  r <- sim_results_lacd1[[nm]]
  if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
  valid_paths <- Filter(function(x) sum(is.finite(x) & x > 0) >= LB_LAGS * 4, r$sim_raw)
  if (length(valid_paths) == 0) return(NULL)
  q_sim_mat <- sapply(valid_paths, function(x) quantile(x[is.finite(x) & x > 0], sim_q_probs, names = FALSE))
  a_sim_mat <- sapply(valid_paths, function(x)

  q_sim <- rowMeans(q_sim_mat); a_sim <- rowMeans(a_sim_mat)
  q_re <- quantile(r$real_raw, sim_q_probs, names = FALSE)
  a_re <- as.numeric(acf(r$real_raw, lag.max = LB_LAGS, plot = FALSE)$acf)[-1]

             acf_MAE       = round(sim_mae(a_sim, a_re), 4), acf_RMSE      = round(sim_rmse(a_sim, a_re), 4))
```

### One-step-ahead forecast for the simulated models

The simulation above asks "does the fitted model reproduce the real
process." This asks the separate, standard OOS question this document runs
for every other model on the ladder (`eacd-prediction-accuracy-1day`,
`wacd-prediction-accuracy-1day`) -- for the SAME `sim_winner` picks (WACD(2,2)
for GBP/USD, LACD2(2,2) for BTCUSDT/NVDA), evaluated the same way: parameters
frozen at their TRAIN-fitted values, psi/log-psi rolled forward one step at a
time using the ACTUAL observed previous durations (never a previously
predicted value), on the first calendar day of TEST
(`FORECAST_DAY_START`/`FORECAST_DAY_END`, same window `ipp-forecast` and
every other single-day accuracy chunk use).

```{r sim-pred-accuracy-1day}
# =============================================================================
#  ONE-STEP-AHEAD, order-(2,2), for whichever model sim_winner actually
#  simulated per asset -- generalises eacd-prediction-accuracy-1day/
#  wacd-prediction-accuracy-1day (both order-(1,1)) to the two order-(2,2)
#  recursions this document now has: WACD's linear one and LACD2's
#  log-linear one (raw-eps shock, matching simulate_lacd2_22's own model).
#
#  psi_i computed from REAL x_{i-1}/x_{i-2} (adjDur) at every step, never
#  from this function's own prior prediction -- the "one-step-ahead" in the
#  name means exactly that: the model is asked to predict ONE step past
#  whatever actually happened, repeatedly, not to roll its own forecasts
#  forward the way sim-vs-real-setup's simulation deliberately does.
#
#  SEEDING: 2 pre-sample psi values (order-(2,2) needs two, not one) --
#  the model's own last 2 fitted TRAIN psi (f$muHats tail) if available,
#  else the TRAIN adjDur mean repeated twice. Which one was actually used
#  is printed per asset, not just described here (same transparency
#  wacd-prediction-accuracy-1day already provides for its own order-(1,1)
#  seed).
#
#  test_day too short for order-(2,2) (n<3, no room for even one recursion
#  step past the two seeds) is reported and skipped, not forced.
#
#  SELF-CONTAINED: FORECAST_DAY_START/FORECAST_DAY_END are normally defined
#  by ipp-forecast (Section 10.2.1), but this chunk shouldn't error out just
#  because that chunk wasn't run first this session -- same reasoning as
#  logacd-order-selection's own gof()/lb15() guard. Definition matches
#  ipp-forecast's own exactly (first calendar day of TEST).
# =============================================================================
if (!exists("FORECAST_DAY_START", inherits = FALSE)) {
  FORECAST_DAY_START <- SPLIT_TIME
  FORECAST_DAY_END   <- SPLIT_TIME + 86400
}

psi_seed_general <- function(f, q, train_mean) {
  have_muhats <- !is.null(f$muHats) && length(f$muHats) >= q
  if (have_muhats) tail(as.numeric(f$muHats), q) else rep(train_mean, q)
}

# DIVERGENCE GUARD, both recursions: unlike EACD/WACD's own alpha*x term
# (bounded in the sense that x's own scale is what psi predicts), LACD2's
# alpha multiplies RAW eps = x/psi directly, uncompressed -- unlike LACD1,
# where the SAME kind of extreme ratio is first passed through log(), which
# compresses a large eps down to a modest additive shock. One genuinely
# extreme test-day observation (a real duration far above what psi predicted
# for it) can therefore inject a large RAW value straight into log(psi) here,
# and because this is a (2,2) recursion, that shock re-enters the recursion
# for TWO more steps via beta1*lp[i-1]/beta2*lp[i-2] before it can decay --
# confirmed directly: a single ~500x-typical observation mid-day, fed through
# this exact function with real fitted-scale coefficients, sends psi to
# 1e34 within 3 steps and Inf/NaN shortly after. simulate_lacd2_22() (the
# SIMULATION function) already guards against exactly this; this ONE-STEP
# prediction function originally did not -- fixed here to match.
one_step_wacd22 <- function(x, w, a1, a2, b1, b2, psi_seed, cap) {
  n <- length(x); psi <- numeric(n); psi[1:2] <- psi_seed
  diverged_at <- NA_integer_
  if (n > 2) for (i in 3:n) {
    psi[i] <- w + a1 * x[i - 1] + a2 * x[i - 2] + b1 * psi[i - 1] + b2 * psi[i - 2]
    if (!is.finite(psi[i]) || psi[i] <= 0 || psi[i] > cap) { diverged_at <- i; break }
  }
  list(psi = psi, diverged_at = diverged_at)
}

one_step_lacd2_22 <- function(x, w, a1, a2, b1, b2, psi_seed, cap) {
  n <- length(x); lp <- numeric(n); lp[1:2] <- log(psi_seed)
  diverged_at <- NA_integer_
  if (n > 2) for (i in 3:n) {
    e1 <- x[i - 1] / exp(lp[i - 1])
    e2 <- x[i - 2] / exp(lp[i - 2])
    lp[i] <- w + a1 * e1 + a2 * e2 + b1 * lp[i - 1] + b2 * lp[i - 2]
    psi_i <- exp(lp[i])
    if (!is.finite(psi_i) || psi_i <= 0 || psi_i > cap) { diverged_at <- i; break }
  }
  list(psi = exp(lp), diverged_at = diverged_at)
}

# LACD1(2,2): alpha multiplies log(eps_i-j), not raw eps -- log() compresses
# a large x/psi ratio into a modest additive shock (verified this session:
# LACD1's own log-psi ACF decays cleanly at beta^k with no comparable
# blow-up risk), so this is structurally much less divergence-prone than
# one_step_lacd2_22 above. cap/diverged_at kept anyway, defensively, for the
# same reporting-not-hiding reason every other recursion in this document
# carries one -- not because a blow-up is expected here.
one_step_lacd1_22 <- function(x, w, a1, a2, b1, b2, psi_seed, cap) {
  n <- length(x); lp <- numeric(n); lp[1:2] <- log(psi_seed)
  diverged_at <- NA_integer_
  if (n > 2) for (i in 3:n) {
    log_eps1 <- log(x[i - 1]) - lp[i - 1]
    log_eps2 <- log(x[i - 2]) - lp[i - 2]
    lp[i] <- w + a1 * log_eps1 + a2 * log_eps2 + b1 * lp[i - 1] + b2 * lp[i - 2]
    psi_i <- exp(lp[i])
    if (!is.finite(psi_i) || psi_i <= 0 || psi_i > cap) { diverged_at <- i; break }
  }
  list(psi = exp(lp), diverged_at = diverged_at)
}

# STALE-CACHE SELF-HEAL: sim_pred_acc_1day's own schema changed when the
# divergence guard was added (n_used/diverged columns, truncated MAE/RMSE) --
# an object left over in this session (or loaded via save_model_progress) from
# BEFORE that fix has neither column and still carries the exploded, unguarded
# numbers. Trusting exists() alone here would silently reprint those stale
# values forever, exactly the failure class logacd-lognormal-fit's own
# stale-cache fix already exists to prevent -- so require the new columns to
# be present before treating a cached object as valid.
if (exists("sim_pred_acc_1day", inherits = FALSE) &&
    !all(c("n_used", "diverged") %in% names(sim_pred_acc_1day))) {
  cat("sim_pred_acc_1day: cached object predates the divergence guard (missing\n")
  cat("n_used/diverged columns) -- discarding and recomputing rather than\n")
  cat("reprinting stale, unguarded numbers.\n")
  rm(sim_pred_acc_1day)
}

if (!exists("sim_pred_acc_1day", inherits = FALSE)) {

sim_pred_acc_1day <- rbindlist(lapply(names(split_sets), function(nm) {
  win  <- sim_winner[[nm]]
  fits <- get(win$fits)
  f    <- fits[[nm]]
  if (is.null(f)) { cat(sprintf("%s: winning model not fitted -- skipped.\n", nm)); return(NULL) }

  p  <- f$mPara
  om <- unname(p["omega"]); a1 <- unname(p["alpha1"]); a2 <- unname(p["alpha2"])
  b1 <- unname(p["beta1"]); b2 <- unname(p["beta2"])

  adj_all <- diurnal_fits[[nm]]$adj   # time/duration(raw)/factor/adjDur, WHOLE sample

  train_adj <- adj_all[time < SPLIT_TIME]
  train_adj <- train_adj[is.finite(adjDur) & adjDur > 0]
  train_mean_adj <- mean(train_adj$adjDur)

  train_dur_raw  <- train_adj$duration[is.finite(train_adj$duration) & train_adj$duration > 0]
  train_mean_raw <- mean(train_dur_raw)
  train_last_raw <- tail(train_dur_raw, 1)

  test_day <- adj_all[time >= FORECAST_DAY_START & time < FORECAST_DAY_END]
  test_day <- test_day[is.finite(adjDur) & adjDur > 0 & is.finite(duration) & duration > 0]
  setorder(test_day, time)

  x_adj <- test_day$adjDur
  n <- length(x_adj)
  if (n < 3) {
    cat(sprintf("%-8s: test day too short (n=%d) for an order-(2,2) one-step forecast -- skipped.\n", nm, n))
    return(NULL)
  }

  psi_seed <- psi_seed_general(f, 2, train_mean_adj)
  cat(sprintf("%-8s: %s, psi seeded from %s (test day n = %d)\n", nm, win$label,
              if (!is.null(f$muHats) && length(f$muHats) >= 2) "last 2 fitted TRAIN psi (muHats)"
              else "TRAIN adjDur mean (x2)", n))

  cap <- 1000 * train_mean_adj   # same cap convention as sim-vs-real-setup's own simulate_*() functions
  step_out <- if (win$kind == "linear22") {
    one_step_wacd22(x_adj, om, a1, a2, b1, b2, psi_seed, cap = cap)
  } else if (win$kind == "lacd1_22") {
    one_step_lacd1_22(x_adj, om, a1, a2, b1, b2, psi_seed, cap = cap)
  } else {
    one_step_lacd2_22(x_adj, om, a1, a2, b1, b2, psi_seed, cap = cap)
  }
  psi_adj  <- step_out$psi
  diverged <- !is.na(step_out$diverged_at)
  n_used   <- if (diverged) step_out$diverged_at - 1L else n

  if (diverged) {
    cat(sprintf(
      "%-8s: %s ONE-STEP-AHEAD DIVERGED after %d of %d test-day steps -- a single\n           extreme x/psi ratio injected a large additive shock into log(psi) (LACD2's\n           raw-eps alpha term doesn't compress it the way LACD1's log-eps does); MAE/RMSE\n           below computed over the pre-divergence prefix only (n_used), not the full day.\n",
      nm, win$label, n_used, n))
  }

  # ALL THREE methods evaluated over the SAME pre-divergence prefix (n_used),
  # even though only the model recursion itself can diverge -- an apples-to-
  # apples comparison requires identical evaluation windows.
  idx <- seq_len(n_used)
  x_raw <- test_day$duration[idx]

  # naive-last, RAW scale directly; row 1 uses TRAIN's own last observed RAW duration.
  x_raw_ext <- c(train_last_raw, test_day$duration)
  pred_naive_last_raw <- x_raw_ext[seq_len(n)][idx]

  pred_raw <- (psi_adj * test_day$factor)[idx]   # back-transformed to raw seconds

  data.table(
    asset = nm, n = n, n_used = n_used, diverged = diverged,
    model = c(sprintf("%s: one-step-ahead", win$label), "Naive: mean", "Naive: last value"),
    MAE  = round(c(mean(abs(x_raw - pred_raw)), mean(abs(x_raw - train_mean_raw)),
                   mean(abs(x_raw - pred_naive_last_raw))), 4),
    RMSE = round(c(sqrt(mean((x_raw - pred_raw)^2)), sqrt(mean((x_raw - train_mean_raw)^2)),
                   sqrt(mean((x_raw - pred_naive_last_raw)^2))), 4)
  )
}))

save_model_progress(sim_pred_acc_1day = sim_pred_acc_1day)
}

cat("\n=== One-step-ahead prediction accuracy, sim_winner models, SINGLE test day ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Target day: %s to %s\n\n", format(FORECAST_DAY_START), format(FORECAST_DAY_END)))
for (nm in names(split_sets)) {
  sub <- sim_pred_acc_1day[asset == nm]
  if (nrow(sub) == 0) next
  cat(sprintf("--- %s: n = %d%s ---\n", nm, sub$n[1],
              if (isTRUE(sub$diverged[1])) sprintf(" (DIVERGED -- n_used = %d)", sub$n_used[1]) else ""))
  print(sub[, .(model, MAE, RMSE)])
  cat("\n")
}

cat("\nREADING IT: same evaluation as eacd-prediction-accuracy-1day/wacd-\n")
cat("prediction-accuracy-1day's own (1,1) versions -- same day, same naive\n")
cat("benchmarks, errors in RAW seconds. The model row differs per asset\n")
cat("(WACD(2,2) for GBP/USD, LACD2(2,2) for BTCUSDT/NVDA) because that is\n")
cat("what sim_winner actually simulated for each -- this is the point-forecast\n")
cat("counterpart to that simulation's own distributional check, not a\n")
cat("re-run of the (1,1) baseline already reported elsewhere. A richer order\n")
cat("beating its own naive benchmarks by a similar or larger margin than the\n")
cat("(1,1) versions do is evidence the extra lag pulls its weight on point\n")
cat("forecasts, not just on the in-sample likelihood the order-selection\n")
cat("grids compared earlier.\n")
cat("\nDIVERGED rows: LACD2(2,2)'s alpha multiplies RAW eps=x/psi, uncompressed\n")
cat("(unlike LACD1's log(eps)) -- one genuinely extreme test-day duration can\n")
cat("inject a large shock into log(psi) that then re-enters the recursion for\n")
cat("two more steps via beta1/beta2 before decaying, overflowing exp(). n_used\n")
cat("(< n) marks how many of the day's steps were evaluated before that\n")
cat("happened; all three rows (model, Naive: mean, Naive: last) are scored on\n")
cat("that same shortened window for a fair comparison. This is informative\n")
cat("about that day's data, not evidence of a coding error -- the same\n")
cat("AR(2)-instability caveat sim-vs-real-distance's own DIVERGED handling\n")
cat("already gives for the simulation.\n")
```

### One-step-ahead forecast: LACD1(2,2) for BTCUSDT/NVDA

`sim-pred-accuracy-1day` above evaluates `sim_winner`'s own picks -- LACD2(2,2)
for BTCUSDT/NVDA specifically. This runs the identical evaluation (same
target day, same naive benchmarks, same divergence handling) for LACD1(2,2)
(`logacd22_fits`) on those same two assets instead, as a direct head-to-head:
same order, same two assets, same day, only the innovation term differs
(log(eps) vs raw eps). Reuses `psi_seed_general()`/`one_step_lacd1_22()`
already defined in `sim-pred-accuracy-1day` above -- not redefined here.

```{r lacd1-pred-accuracy-1day}
# =============================================================================
#  LACD1(2,2) one-step-ahead, BTCUSDT/NVDA only -- GBP/USD is excluded here
#  since its sim_winner/ladder pick is WACD(2,2), not a Log-ACD variant, and
#  logacd22_fits was fit for all three assets but this comparison is only
#  meaningful for the two sim_winner evaluated under LACD2(2,2) above.
# =============================================================================
lacd1_pred_assets <- intersect(c("BTCUSDT", "NVDA"), names(logacd22_fits))

if (exists("lacd1_pred_acc_1day", inherits = FALSE) &&
    !all(c("n_used", "diverged") %in% names(lacd1_pred_acc_1day))) {
  cat("lacd1_pred_acc_1day: cached object predates the divergence guard --\n")
  cat("discarding and recomputing rather than reprinting stale numbers.\n")
  rm(lacd1_pred_acc_1day)
}

if (!exists("lacd1_pred_acc_1day", inherits = FALSE)) {

lacd1_pred_acc_1day <- rbindlist(lapply(lacd1_pred_assets, function(nm) {
  f <- logacd22_fits[[nm]]
  if (is.null(f)) { cat(sprintf("%s: LACD1(2,2) not fitted -- skipped.\n", nm)); return(NULL) }

  p  <- f$mPara
  om <- unname(p["omega"]); a1 <- unname(p["alpha1"]); a2 <- unname(p["alpha2"])
  b1 <- unname(p["beta1"]); b2 <- unname(p["beta2"])

  adj_all <- diurnal_fits[[nm]]$adj

  train_adj <- adj_all[time < SPLIT_TIME]
  train_adj <- train_adj[is.finite(adjDur) & adjDur > 0]
  train_mean_adj <- mean(train_adj$adjDur)

  train_dur_raw  <- train_adj$duration[is.finite(train_adj$duration) & train_adj$duration > 0]
  train_mean_raw <- mean(train_dur_raw)
  train_last_raw <- tail(train_dur_raw, 1)

  test_day <- adj_all[time >= FORECAST_DAY_START & time < FORECAST_DAY_END]
  test_day <- test_day[is.finite(adjDur) & adjDur > 0 & is.finite(duration) & duration > 0]
  setorder(test_day, time)

  x_adj <- test_day$adjDur
  n <- length(x_adj)
  if (n < 3) {
    cat(sprintf("%-8s: test day too short (n=%d) for an order-(2,2) one-step forecast -- skipped.\n", nm, n))
    return(NULL)
  }

  psi_seed <- psi_seed_general(f, 2, train_mean_adj)
  cat(sprintf("%-8s: LACD1(2,2), psi seeded from %s (test day n = %d)\n", nm,
              if (!is.null(f$muHats) && length(f$muHats) >= 2) "last 2 fitted TRAIN psi (muHats)"
              else "TRAIN adjDur mean (x2)", n))

  cap <- 1000 * train_mean_adj
  step_out <- one_step_lacd1_22(x_adj, om, a1, a2, b1, b2, psi_seed, cap = cap)
  psi_adj  <- step_out$psi
  diverged <- !is.na(step_out$diverged_at)
  n_used   <- if (diverged) step_out$diverged_at - 1L else n

  if (diverged) {
    cat(sprintf(
      "%-8s: LACD1(2,2) ONE-STEP-AHEAD DIVERGED after %d of %d test-day steps --\n           MAE/RMSE below computed over the pre-divergence prefix only (n_used).\n",
      nm, n_used, n))
  }

  idx <- seq_len(n_used)
  x_raw <- test_day$duration[idx]

  x_raw_ext <- c(train_last_raw, test_day$duration)
  pred_naive_last_raw <- x_raw_ext[seq_len(n)][idx]

  pred_raw <- (psi_adj * test_day$factor)[idx]

  data.table(
    asset = nm, n = n, n_used = n_used, diverged = diverged,
    model = c("LACD1(2,2): one-step-ahead", "Naive: mean", "Naive: last value"),
    MAE  = round(c(mean(abs(x_raw - pred_raw)), mean(abs(x_raw - train_mean_raw)),
                   mean(abs(x_raw - pred_naive_last_raw))), 4),
    RMSE = round(c(sqrt(mean((x_raw - pred_raw)^2)), sqrt(mean((x_raw - train_mean_raw)^2)),
                   sqrt(mean((x_raw - pred_naive_last_raw)^2))), 4)
  )
}))

save_model_progress(lacd1_pred_acc_1day = lacd1_pred_acc_1day)
}

cat("\n=== One-step-ahead prediction accuracy, LACD1(2,2), SINGLE test day (BTCUSDT/NVDA) ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Target day: %s to %s\n\n", format(FORECAST_DAY_START), format(FORECAST_DAY_END)))
for (nm in lacd1_pred_assets) {
  sub <- lacd1_pred_acc_1day[asset == nm]
  if (nrow(sub) == 0) next
  cat(sprintf("--- %s: n = %d%s ---\n", nm, sub$n[1],
              if (isTRUE(sub$diverged[1])) sprintf(" (DIVERGED -- n_used = %d)", sub$n_used[1]) else ""))
  print(sub[, .(model, MAE, RMSE)])
  cat("\n")
}

cat("\n=== LACD1(2,2) vs LACD2(2,2), same assets, same day (head-to-head) ===\n\n")
if (exists("sim_pred_acc_1day", inherits = FALSE)) {
  cmp <- rbindlist(list(
    lacd1_pred_acc_1day[grepl("one-step-ahead", model), .(asset, model, MAE, RMSE)],
    sim_pred_acc_1day[asset %in% lacd1_pred_assets & grepl("one-step-ahead", model), .(asset, model, MAE, RMSE)]
  ))
  print(dcast(cmp, asset ~ model, value.var = c("MAE", "RMSE")))
} else {
  cat("sim_pred_acc_1day not yet in scope -- run sim-pred-accuracy-1day first for the head-to-head comparison.\n")
}

cat("\nREADING IT: same day, same two assets, same naive benchmarks as sim-pred-\n")
cat("accuracy-1day's own LACD2(2,2) rows -- the only thing that differs is the\n")
cat("innovation term (log(eps) here vs raw eps there). A lower MAE/RMSE for\n")
cat("LACD1(2,2) here is evidence the compression log() gives the innovation\n")
cat("term matters for POINT-forecast accuracy too, not just for the divergence\n")
cat("robustness sim-vs-real-distance's own DIVERGED handling already showed for\n")
cat("the simulation. If n_used differs between the two models' rows for the\n")
cat("same asset, that itself is direct evidence of which specification is more\n")
cat("fragile on this particular test day.\n")
```






```{r logacd-compare}
# =============================================================================
#  Does Log-ACD resolve the near-zero-duration corruption that broke WACD?
#
#  THE TEST (two signals, from the WACD diagnostic):
#    residual mean ~ 1  AND  log-likelihood < 0  =  clean fit.
#  WACD gave residual mean 1.15 / 0.85 and POSITIVE log-likelihood on BTC/NVDA;
#  the corruption scaled with the sub-millisecond mass (0% / 11% / 31%).
#
#  NOTE ON PARAMETERS: log-ACD's alpha multiplies log(eps) and beta multiplies
#  log(psi); neither is on the linear-ACD scale, and beta is NOT the linear
#  alpha+beta. We therefore do NOT read persistence from the log-ACD fit -- the
#  persistence result stays with EACD. Log-ACD's claim is a CLEAN FIT where the
#  Weibull failed, not a competing persistence estimate.
#  NOTE ON AIC: log-likelihoods/AIC are not cleanly comparable across the three
#  models (different densities/parameterisations), so we compare the FIT-HEALTH
#  signals (residual mean, sign of logLik), not raw AIC.
# =============================================================================
gof <- function(f, w) f$goodnessOfFit[w, "value"]

# fit-health across all three models, ordered by sub-ms mass to show the gradient
fit_health <- rbindlist(lapply(names(logacd_fits), function(nm) {
  d  <- get_fit_series(nm, FIT_N)
  re <- as.numeric(eacd_fits[[nm]]$residuals);   re <- re[is.finite(re)]
  rw <- as.numeric(wacd_fits[[nm]]$residuals);   rw <- rw[is.finite(rw)]
  rl <- as.numeric(logacd_fits[[nm]]$residuals); rl <- rl[is.finite(rl)]
  data.table(
    asset       = nm,
    sub_ms_pct  = round(100*mean(d < 0.001), 1),
    EACD_mean   = round(mean(re), 3),  EACD_z   = round(resid_mean_z(re), 1),
    EACD_logL   = round(gof(eacd_fits[[nm]],  "LogLikelihood"), 0),
    WACD_mean   = round(mean(rw), 3),  WACD_z   = round(resid_mean_z(rw), 1),
    WACD_logL   = round(gof(wacd_fits[[nm]],  "LogLikelihood"), 0),
    LogACD_mean = round(mean(rl), 3),  LogACD_z = round(resid_mean_z(rl), 1),
    LogACD_logL = round(gof(logacd_fits[[nm]],"LogLikelihood"), 0)
  )
}))
setorder(fit_health, sub_ms_pct)

cat("=== CONDITIONAL-MEAN FIT HEALTH ACROSS MODELS (ordered by sub-ms mass) ===\n")
cat("Clean fit = residual mean ~ 1 AND log-likelihood < 0. The _z columns are\n")
cat("formal Z-stats for E[eps]=1, reported for rigor -- NOT a 1.96 pass/fail\n")
cat("(at this n, |z|>1.96 fires on almost any nonzero deviation); read their\n")
cat("MAGNITUDE, and use it to see the SAME sub-ms-driven gradient the _mean\n")
cat("columns already show, stated in standard-error units instead of raw units.\n\n")
print(fit_health)

cat("\nREADING IT:\n")
cat("  EACD  : residual mean ~1 and logL<0 on ALL assets (exponential density\n")
cat("          is finite at 0, so it never corrupts) -- the QMLE baseline.\n")
cat("  WACD  : clean for FX (0% sub-ms) but corrupts as sub-ms mass grows --\n")
cat("          residual mean departs from 1, logL turns POSITIVE (11%->+10k,\n")
cat("          31%->+247k). The Weibull density diverges near zero at low gamma.\n")
cat("  LogACD: residual mean back to ~1 and logL<0 on ALL THREE. Modelling\n")
cat("          log(psi) removes the near-zero sensitivity -- the corruption is\n")
cat("          resolved on exactly the assets where the Weibull failed.\n")

# ---- self-check: confirm the log-ACD recursion matches ACDm's muHats ----------
cat("\n=== Recursion check (LACD1 hand-recursion vs ACDm muHats) ===\n")
psi_logacd <- function(x, w, a, b, psi1) {
  n <- length(x); lp <- numeric(n); lp[1] <- log(psi1)
  for (i in 2:n) lp[i] <- w + a*(log(x[i-1]) - lp[i-1]) + b*lp[i-1]
  exp(lp)
}
for (nm in names(logacd_fits)) {
  f <- logacd_fits[[nm]]; x <- get_fit_series(nm, FIT_N); p <- f$mPara
  psi <- psi_logacd(x, unname(p["omega"]), unname(p["alpha1"]), unname(p["beta1"]), f$muHats[1])
  k <- 100:length(x)
  cat(sprintf("  %-8s: max rel err vs muHats = %.1e\n", nm,
              max(abs(psi[k]-f$muHats[k])/f$muHats[k])))
}
cat("(near machine precision => the recursion used for forecasting is exact)\n")
```



```{r residual-mean-verification}
# =============================================================================
#  INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION of the residual mean.
#
#  The residual mean is computed identically for WACD and log-ACD: mean of the
#  package's $residuals. To confirm the log-ACD 1.000 is not a package artefact,
#  we recompute the standardised residual FROM SCRATCH as eps = x / psi, using
#  the package's fitted conditional mean (muHats), and check it matches
#  $residuals. If hand-computed and package residuals agree, the 1.000 is real.
#
#  This treats all three models identically -- no model is given special
#  handling. The residual mean is a COMPUTED outcome in every case; the
#  exponential-innovation models (EACD, log-ACD) land at 1 because the
#  exponential MLE imposes mean(x/psi)=1 at a clean optimum, while the Weibull
#  (WACD) can deviate -- and does, where the near-zero mass corrupts the fit.
# =============================================================================
verify_resid <- rbindlist(lapply(names(logacd_fits), function(nm) {
  x <- get_fit_series(nm, FIT_N)                    # the durations fitted on

  rbindlist(lapply(c("EACD","WACD","LogACD"), function(mod) {
    f <- switch(mod,
                EACD   = eacd_fits[[nm]],
                WACD   = wacd_fits[[nm]],
                LogACD = logacd_fits[[nm]])

    psi <- as.numeric(f$muHats)                     # package's conditional mean
    pkg_resid <- as.numeric(f$residuals)            # package's residuals

    # hand-computed standardised residual, from scratch
    hand_resid <- x / psi

    # align lengths (both should be FIT_N; guard just in case)
    n <- min(length(hand_resid), length(pkg_resid))
    hand <- hand_resid[seq_len(n)]; hand <- hand[is.finite(hand)]
    pkg  <- pkg_resid[seq_len(n)];  pkg  <- pkg[is.finite(pkg)]

    data.table(
      asset          = nm,
      model          = mod,
      pkg_resid_mean = round(mean(pkg), 4),         # what the tables report
      hand_resid_mean= round(mean(hand), 4),        # recomputed x/psi
      max_abs_diff   = signif(max(abs(hand_resid[seq_len(n)] - pkg_resid[seq_len(n)]),
                                  na.rm = TRUE), 3)  # do they match?
    )
  }))
}))

cat("=== Residual mean: package vs hand-computed (x / muHats) ===\n")
cat("If pkg_resid_mean == hand_resid_mean and max_abs_diff ~ 0, the residual\n")
cat("mean is a genuine computed outcome, identical method across all models.\n\n")
print(verify_resid)

cat("\nREADING IT:\n")
cat("  - EACD & LogACD hand_resid_mean ~ 1.000: confirmed real, not a package\n")
cat("    artefact -- the exponential MLE lands mean(x/psi)=1 at a clean optimum.\n")
cat("  - WACD hand_resid_mean deviates for BTC/NVDA (matching pkg): the Weibull\n")
cat("    does NOT impose mean=1, and the near-zero corruption pulls it off 1.\n")
cat("  - max_abs_diff ~ 0 everywhere: package $residuals == x/muHats, so the\n")
cat("    same computation is applied to every model. No special handling.\n")
```


```{r prediction-mae-rmse}
# =============================================================================
#  OUT-OF-SAMPLE PREDICTION -- MAE / RMSE, test set, one-step-ahead.
#
#  Parameters FROZEN at TRAIN-only estimates. Conditional mean rolled forward
#  one step at a time using the ACTUAL observed previous duration. One-step is
#  the only viable scheme (two assets integrated -> multi-step diverges).
#
#  MODELS & DISTRIBUTION:
#    EACD(1,1) -- exponential innovation, LINEAR mean:
#                 psi_i = w + a*x_{i-1} + b*psi_{i-1}
#    Log-ACD   -- exponential innovation, LOG-LINEAR mean (LACD1, verified
#                 against ACDm source): log psi_i = w + a*log(eps_{i-1}) + b*log psi_{i-1}
#    Naive:mean -- train mean always (= homogeneous-Poisson prediction)
#    Naive:last -- previous actual (random walk)
#  Both ACD models use the EXPONENTIAL innovation, isolating the effect of the
#  mean specification (linear vs log) on point forecasts.
#
#  Errors in SECONDS, NOT comparable across assets; compare WITHIN asset and
#  % improvement over naive across.
# =============================================================================

psi_lin <- function(x, w, a, b, psi1) {          # EACD
  n <- length(x); p <- numeric(n); p[1] <- psi1
  for (i in 2:n) p[i] <- w + a*x[i-1] + b*p[i-1]
  p
}
psi_logacd <- function(x, w, a, b, psi1) {       # LACD1, verified vs ACDm source
  n <- length(x); lp <- numeric(n); lp[1] <- log(psi1)
  for (i in 2:n) {
    log_eps <- log(x[i-1]) - lp[i-1]
    lp[i]   <- w + a*log_eps + b*lp[i-1]
  }
  exp(lp)
}
mae  <- function(x,f) mean(abs(x-f))
rmse <- function(x,f) sqrt(mean((x-f)^2))

pred_tbl <- rbindlist(lapply(names(split_sets), function(nm) {
  tr <- split_sets[[nm]]$train$adjDur; tr <- tr[is.finite(tr) & tr>0]
  te <- split_sets[[nm]]$test$adjDur;  te <- te[is.finite(te) & te>0]
  # FULL test set, no cap -- same reasoning as FIT_N -> Inf for training: a
  # fixed row-count cap is a different amount of calendar time per asset, and
  # the OOS evaluation should cover each asset's whole test period, not a
  # sub-day slice of it for BTC. The psi recursion below is O(n) vector
  # arithmetic, not an MLE fit, so this costs nothing to uncap.
  mean_tr <- mean(tr)

  pe <- eacd_fits[[nm]]$mPara
  psi_e <- psi_lin(te, unname(pe["omega"]), unname(pe["alpha1"]), unname(pe["beta1"]), mean_tr)

  pl <- logacd_fits[[nm]]$mPara
  psi_l <- psi_logacd(te, unname(pl["omega"]), unname(pl["alpha1"]), unname(pl["beta1"]), mean_tr)

  pred_uncond <- rep(mean_tr, length(te))
  pred_last   <- c(mean_tr, te[-length(te)])

  data.table(
    asset = nm, n_test = length(te),
    model = c("EACD(1,1)","Log-ACD","Naive: mean","Naive: last"),
    MAE   = round(c(mae(te,psi_e),  mae(te,psi_l),  mae(te,pred_uncond),  mae(te,pred_last)), 4),
    RMSE  = round(c(rmse(te,psi_e), rmse(te,psi_l), rmse(te,pred_uncond), rmse(te,pred_last)), 4)
  )
}))

cat("=== OUT-OF-SAMPLE PREDICTION (test set, one-step-ahead, train-frozen) ===\n")
cat("Both ACD models use the EXPONENTIAL innovation; they differ only in the\n")
cat("mean recursion (linear vs log-linear). Errors in seconds; compare WITHIN asset.\n\n")
for (nm in names(split_sets)) {
  cat(sprintf("--- %s (n_test=%s) ---\n", nm, format(pred_tbl[asset==nm]$n_test[1], big.mark=",")))
  print(pred_tbl[asset==nm, .(model, MAE, RMSE)])
  cat("\n")
}

cat("=== % IMPROVEMENT OVER NAIVE-MEAN (the constant-rate Poisson benchmark) ===\n\n")
imp <- pred_tbl[, {bm<-MAE[model=="Naive: mean"]; br<-RMSE[model=="Naive: mean"]
  .(model=model, MAE_impr=round(100*(bm-MAE)/bm,1), RMSE_impr=round(100*(br-RMSE)/br,1))},
  by=asset][model %in% c("EACD(1,1)","Log-ACD")]
print(dcast(imp, asset ~ model, value.var=c("MAE_impr","RMSE_impr")))
```

```{r}

#  1) **Seed**: 

#  Starting point for a search - optimiser can move up/down, negative/past one - no floor
#  "startPara" is an initial value for the optimiser, not a constraint. The parameters move freely from it.
#  Seeds can't be a cause of persistence > 1

#  2) **Optimiser**:  Ref-https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ACDm/ACDm.pdf
#                     https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/ACDm/html/acdFit.html

#  A search procedure for finding the maximum of log-liklihood.
#  Four available: "optim", "nlimb", "solnp", "optimx"
#  Used: "optim" - with method = "Nelder-Mead" - package default
#        "nlimb" - Why? - duration magnitudes in microseconds and nanoseconds makes the likelihood numerically stiff. 
#        "solnp" - constrained solver - imposes "alpha+beta < 1" during estimation.

#  3) **Maximum Liklihood Estimation**: 

#  picks the parameters that make the observed sample most probable under the model.
#  Durations are dependent - Can't write joint density as a product of marginals - Use prediction-error decomposition - factor the joint density into a chain of one-step ahead conditional densities - Ecch factor is the density of the next duration given everything before it. 

#  trial param values -> recursion, find psi_i -> form standardised residuals epsilon_i -> sum log-density for N -> handover to optimiser, which picks new param values and repeats.

#  No-closed form -> Numerical Optimisation
#  For Poisson, closed form is present, lambda = 1/x , direct.
#  For ACD, psi_i depends on psi_{i-1} and inturn depends on psi_{i-2}....entire history.
#  No algebraic solution exists.

#  4) Stationarity, Persistence, Explosive

```
